question: Among schools with a school-level SAT excellence rate above 0.3, what is the highest ages-5-17 free-meal eligibility rate?
evidence: SAT excellence rate is the share of test takers scoring at least 1500.
SQL: SELECT MAX(1.0 * f."Free Meal Count (Ages 5-17)" / NULLIF(f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)", 0)) FROM frpm AS f JOIN satscores AS s ON s.cds = f.cdscode WHERE s.rtype = 'S' AND s.numtsttakr > 0 AND f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)" > 0 AND 1.0 * s.numge1500 / NULLIF(s.numtsttakr, 0) > 0.3

question: For locally funded schools whose K-12 minus ages-5-17 enrollment difference exceeds the average such difference among locally funded schools, list each school's directory-listed name and DOC type.
SQL: SELECT s.school, s.doctype FROM frpm AS f JOIN schools AS s ON f.cdscode = s.cdscode WHERE s.fundingtype = 'Locally funded' AND (f."Enrollment (K-12)" - f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)") > (SELECT AVG(f2."Enrollment (K-12)" - f2."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)") FROM frpm AS f2 JOIN schools AS s2 ON f2.cdscode = s2.cdscode WHERE s2.fundingtype = 'Locally funded') ORDER BY s.cdscode NULLS FIRST

question: For the five schools with ownership code 66 and the largest K-12 free-or-reduced-price meal counts, give each school's K-12 eligible meal rate rounded to six decimal places.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(1.0 * f."FRPM Count (K-12)" / NULLIF(NULLIF(f."Enrollment (K-12)", 0), 0) AS DECIMAL), 6) FROM frpm AS f JOIN schools AS s ON s.cdscode = f.cdscode WHERE s.soc = '66' AND NOT f."FRPM Count (K-12)" IS NULL AND f."Enrollment (K-12)" > 0 ORDER BY f."FRPM Count (K-12)" DESC NULLS LAST, s.cdscode NULLS FIRST LIMIT 5

question: What is the ratio of merged Unified School District schools in Orange County to merged Elementary School District schools?
SQL: SELECT CASE WHEN (SUM(CASE WHEN doc = '54' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(CASE WHEN doc = '54' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN doc = '52' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) FROM schools WHERE statustype = 'Merged' AND county = 'Orange'

question: What are the mailing street address and name of the school with the seventh-highest recorded average mathematics score?
SQL: SELECT sc.mailstreet, sc.school FROM satscores AS sat JOIN schools AS sc ON sc.cdscode = sat.cds WHERE sat.rtype = 'S' AND NOT sat.avgscrmath IS NULL ORDER BY sat.avgscrmath DESC NULLS LAST, sat.cds NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1 OFFSET 6

question: How many non-charter schools in Los Angeles County have a K-12 free-meal percentage below 0.18%?
SQL: SELECT COUNT(t2.school) FROM frpm AS t1 INNER JOIN schools AS t2 ON t1.cdscode = t2.cdscode WHERE t2.county = 'Los Angeles' AND t2.charter = 0 AND CASE WHEN (t1."Free Meal Count (K-12)") IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((t1."Free Meal Count (K-12)") AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END * 100 / NULLIF(t1."Enrollment (K-12)", 0) < 0.18

question: Which schools served a grade span of Kindergarten to 9th grade in the county of Los Angeles and what is its Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (Ages 5-17)?
evidence: FRPM eligibility percentage is free-or-reduced-price meal recipients divided by same-age-band enrollment, times 100.
SQL: SELECT t2.school, t1."FRPM Count (Ages 5-17)" * 100 / NULLIF(t1."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)", 0) FROM frpm AS t1 INNER JOIN schools AS t2 ON t1.cdscode = t2.cdscode WHERE t2.county = 'Los Angeles' AND t2.gsserved = 'K-9'

question: What is the Percent (%) Eligible Free (K-12) in the school administered by an administrator whose first name is Alusine. List the district code of the school.
evidence: K-12 free-meal eligibility percentage is K-12 free-meal recipients divided by K-12 enrollment, times 100.
SQL: SELECT t1."Free Meal Count (K-12)" * 100 / NULLIF(t1."Enrollment (K-12)", 0), t1."District Code" FROM frpm AS t1 INNER JOIN schools AS t2 ON t1.cdscode = t2.cdscode WHERE t2.admfname1 = 'Alusine'

question: List the distinct available administrator email addresses for public intermediate/middle schools in San Bernardino city and county, in a unified school district, opened during 2009 or 2010.
SQL: WITH matched AS (SELECT admemail1, admemail2, admemail3 FROM schools WHERE county = 'San Bernardino' AND city = 'San Bernardino' AND doctype = 'Unified School District' AND soctype = 'Intermediate/Middle Schools (Public)' AND opendate >= '2009-01-01' AND opendate < '2011-01-01') SELECT admemail1 AS email FROM matched WHERE NOT admemail1 IS NULL AND TRIM(CAST(admemail1 AS TEXT)) <> '' UNION SELECT admemail2 AS email FROM matched WHERE NOT admemail2 IS NULL AND TRIM(CAST(admemail2 AS TEXT)) <> '' UNION SELECT admemail3 AS email FROM matched WHERE NOT admemail3 IS NULL AND TRIM(CAST(admemail3 AS TEXT)) <> '' ORDER BY email NULLS FIRST

question: I'm comparing three high schools in Alameda County and want to focus on the one with the biggest student body. The schools have these CDS codes: 1751010130583, 1612910137588, and 1611760134270. Which of these three schools has the highest enrollment of students aged 5-17? Please give me the 5-digit NCES school identification number for that school. If two or more of them tie for the highest enrollment, give me the NCES identification number of each tied school.
evidence: NCES school identification number: the 5-digit school-level NCES identifier. Enrollment (Ages 5-17): the number of students aged 5 through 17 enrolled at the school.
SQL: SELECT t1.ncesschool FROM schools AS t1 INNER JOIN frpm AS t2 ON t1.cdscode = t2.cdscode WHERE CASE WHEN (t2.cdscode) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((t2.cdscode) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END IN (1751010130583, 1612910137588, 1611760134270) AND t2."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)" = (SELECT MAX(f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)") FROM frpm AS f WHERE CASE WHEN (f.cdscode) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((f.cdscode) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END IN (1751010130583, 1612910137588, 1611760134270))

question: I'm profiling the High Tech High charter network in San Diego. For charter number 756, what is the average number of SAT test takers per school across all of its schools with a San Diego mailing city? Count every school regardless of operational status, and treat a school with no SAT record as having zero test takers. Round the average to two decimals.
evidence: Charter number 756 is the state-issued charter number.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(SUM(COALESCE(sc.numtsttakr, 0)) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_sat_test_takers_per_school FROM schools AS s LEFT JOIN satscores AS sc ON sc.cds = s.cdscode WHERE CASE WHEN (s.charternum) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((s.charternum) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END = 756 AND s.mailcity = 'San Diego'

question: Following up on the SAT participation review: among the currently operating high schools in the district with NCES identification number 0613360 that had no SAT test takers, which one begins serving students at the earliest grade? Please give me each such school's name and grade span served. Note that a high school must actually enroll students through grade 12-offering grade 12 without enrollment doesn't count. A school with no SAT record counts as having zero SAT test takers and should be included; only exclude schools with a positive number of SAT test takers. Compare starting grades as school grades-preschool comes before kindergarten, which comes before grade 1-and use the lowest grade the school actually serves, not just what it offers. If several schools tie at the earliest grade, list them all alphabetically by school name.
evidence: NCES identification number 0613360 is the school district identification number assigned by the National Center for Education Statistics.
SQL: WITH cohort AS (SELECT s.school AS school_name, s.gsserved AS grade_span_served, CASE WHEN SUBSTRING(CAST(s.gsserved AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION('-' IN s.gsserved || '-') - 1) = 'P' THEN -1 WHEN SUBSTRING(CAST(s.gsserved AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION('-' IN s.gsserved || '-') - 1) = 'K' THEN 0 ELSE CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST(s.gsserved AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION('-' IN s.gsserved || '-') - 1)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST(s.gsserved AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION('-' IN s.gsserved || '-') - 1)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END END AS start_rank FROM schools AS s LEFT JOIN satscores AS t ON s.cdscode = t.cds WHERE s.ncesdist = '0613360' AND s.statustype = 'Active' AND CAST(s.gsserved AS TEXT) LIKE '%12' AND COALESCE(t.numtsttakr, 0) = 0) SELECT school_name, grade_span_served FROM cohort WHERE start_rank = (SELECT MIN(start_rank) FROM cohort) ORDER BY school_name NULLS FIRST

question: I'm profiling schools run directly by the California State Board of Education. Which of those schools has the highest average SAT reading score? If several tie for the highest, give me all of them. For each school, I need its name and its full mailing street address - the complete address, not an abbreviated one. Only include schools the State Board runs directly, and the score must be the school's own result, not a district-wide figure.
evidence: State Board of Education: the state authority that directly runs and oversees certain California schools.
SQL: SELECT s.school, s.mailstreet FROM satscores AS t JOIN schools AS s ON t.cds = s.cdscode WHERE s.doctype = 'State Board of Education' AND NOT t.sname IS NULL AND NOT t.avgscrread IS NULL AND t.avgscrread = (SELECT MAX(t2.avgscrread) FROM satscores AS t2 JOIN schools AS s2 ON t2.cds = s2.cdscode WHERE s2.doctype = 'State Board of Education' AND NOT t2.sname IS NULL AND NOT t2.avgscrread IS NULL)

question: I'm trying to verify where a school I was told about is located. It's a high school in Alameda County with Breakfast Provision 2 status, serving grades 9 through 12, and its identification number is 1611920113902. What city is this school in?
evidence: The identification number is the school's CDS code; Educational Instruction Level Code 'HS' identifies a high school; grades 9 through 12 means lowest grade 9 and highest grade 12; Breakfast Provision 2 is a National School Lunch Program provision status.
SQL: SELECT s.city FROM schools AS s INNER JOIN frpm AS f ON s.cdscode = f.cdscode WHERE CASE WHEN (s.cdscode) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((s.cdscode) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END = 1611920113902 AND f."NSLP Provision Status" = 'Breakfast Provision 2' AND s.county = 'Alameda' AND f."Low Grade" = '9' AND f."High Grade" = '12' AND s.eilcode = 'HS'

question: I'm reviewing NSLP Provision 2 schools. Can you give me the name and city of every high school (educational instruction level code HS) whose meal-program status is exactly Provision 2 and whose lowest grade served is above ninth grade? One row per school, ordered by school name. Note: only the status named Provision 2 counts-the breakfast and lunch variants are separate statuses and shouldn't be included.
SQL: SELECT t2.school AS school, t2.city AS city FROM frpm AS t1 INNER JOIN schools AS t2 ON t1.cdscode = t2.cdscode WHERE t1."NSLP Provision Status" = 'Provision 2' AND t2.eilcode = 'HS' AND CASE WHEN (t1."Low Grade") IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((t1."Low Grade") AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END > 9 ORDER BY t2.school NULLS FIRST

question: I'm profiling California's statewide benefit charter networks. Among the schools run by a statewide benefit charter network, which single school had the highest number of SAT test takers who scored 1500 or above? Please give me that school's name and its phone number. If several schools tie for the highest count, list every tied school with its phone number.
evidence: Statewide benefit charter: a charter school network authorized directly by the California State Board of Education to operate schools throughout the state; charter schools authorized by a school district or county office of education are not statewide benefit charters.
SQL: SELECT s.school AS school_name, s.phone AS phone FROM satscores AS t INNER JOIN schools AS s ON t.cds = s.cdscode WHERE s.doctype = 'Statewide Benefit Charter' AND t.rtype = 'S' AND t.numge1500 = (SELECT MAX(t2.numge1500) FROM satscores AS t2 INNER JOIN schools AS s2 ON t2.cds = s2.cdscode WHERE s2.doctype = 'Statewide Benefit Charter' AND t2.rtype = 'S')

question: I'm looking at a directly-funded charter high school in California with CDS code 1611190130609. Could you tell me its average SAT math score and how many students took the SAT there? Just that one school's figures. If the school with that CDS code turns out not to be directly funded, then there's no answer.
evidence: CDS code: the identification number the California Department of Education assigns to a county, district, or school. Directly-funded charter school: a charter school that receives its funding directly from the state rather than through its district.
SQL: SELECT t1.avgscrmath AS average_math_score, t1.numtsttakr AS number_of_test_takers FROM satscores AS t1 INNER JOIN frpm AS t2 ON t1.cds = t2.cdscode WHERE CASE WHEN (t1.cds) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((t1.cds) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END = 1611190130609 AND t2."Charter Funding Type" = 'Directly funded'

question: I'm looking at SAT participation in Contra Costa County. How many schools in the county had more SAT test takers than the school with CDS code 7618040730051? That school is itself a Contra Costa County school, so I just want the count of schools strictly ahead of it by number of SAT test takers, based on the SAT results snapshot in the data. A single number is all I need.
evidence: CDS code: the County-District-School identifier that the California Department of Education assigns to each school and district in the state.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS school_count FROM satscores WHERE cname = 'Contra Costa' AND NOT sname IS NULL AND numtsttakr > (SELECT numtsttakr FROM satscores WHERE CASE WHEN (cds) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((cds) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END = 7618040730051)

question: I'm comparing schools in San Francisco. How many public schools with a San Francisco mailing city had an average total SAT score of at least 1500? Please count only schools whose district type is 'Unified School District', 'High School District', 'Elementary School District', or 'County Office of Education (COE)' - exclude any other district type. I just need the single count of qualifying schools.
evidence: A school's total SAT score is the sum of its average reading, average math, and average writing scores; a school's mailing city is the city in its mailing address.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM satscores AS t1 INNER JOIN schools AS t2 ON t1.cds = t2.cdscode WHERE t2.mailcity = 'San Francisco' AND t2.doctype IN ('Unified School District', 'High School District', 'Elementary School District', 'County Office of Education (COE)') AND (t1.avgscrread + t1.avgscrmath + t1.avgscrwrite) >= 1500

question: What is the lowest grade level at which any school in our district begins serving students? If several schools tie at the lowest grade, just report that single grade level for the whole district. Our district is NCES district ID 0632640.
evidence: 'P' stands for preschool.
SQL: SELECT t1."Low Grade" AS lowest_grade FROM frpm AS t1 INNER JOIN schools AS t2 ON t1.cdscode = t2.cdscode WHERE t2.ncesdist = '0632640' ORDER BY (t1."Low Grade" = 'P') DESC NULLS LAST, (t1."Low Grade" = 'K') DESC NULLS LAST, CASE WHEN (t1."Low Grade") IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((t1."Low Grade") AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END NULLS FIRST, t1."Low Grade" NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1

question: I'm reviewing administrator coverage across Amador and Madera counties, and I want to see which administrator first names actually cover the most schools. For the two administrator first names whose holders run the most schools across the two counties (ranking names by the number of schools their holders run, with the alphabetically earlier name ranking higher if two names run equally many schools), please give me one row per public school district in those two counties and per those two first names, showing the district name, the first name, and the number of schools in that district run by an administrator with that first name - including every public school district, even ones where that's zero. Every administrator listed for a school counts, not just the first-listed one. A public school district means a unified school district, an elementary school district, a high school district, or a county office of education, and only Amador and Madera counties are in scope.
SQL: WITH scope AS (SELECT cdscode, district, admfname1 AS fn FROM schools WHERE county IN ('Amador', 'Madera') AND doctype IN ('Unified School District', 'Elementary School District', 'High School District', 'County Office of Education (COE)') AND NOT admfname1 IS NULL UNION SELECT cdscode, district, admfname2 FROM schools WHERE county IN ('Amador', 'Madera') AND doctype IN ('Unified School District', 'Elementary School District', 'High School District', 'County Office of Education (COE)') AND NOT admfname2 IS NULL UNION SELECT cdscode, district, admfname3 FROM schools WHERE county IN ('Amador', 'Madera') AND doctype IN ('Unified School District', 'Elementary School District', 'High School District', 'County Office of Education (COE)') AND NOT admfname3 IS NULL), ranked AS (SELECT fn, COUNT(DISTINCT cdscode) AS schools_run FROM scope GROUP BY fn ORDER BY schools_run DESC NULLS LAST, fn ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 2), districts AS (SELECT DISTINCT district FROM schools WHERE county IN ('Amador', 'Madera') AND doctype IN ('Unified School District', 'Elementary School District', 'High School District', 'County Office of Education (COE)')) SELECT d.district AS district_name, r.fn AS first_name, (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT s.cdscode) FROM scope AS s WHERE s.district = d.district AND s.fn = r.fn) AS school_count FROM districts AS d CROSS JOIN ranked AS r ORDER BY d.district NULLS FIRST, r.fn NULLS FIRST

question: For the 2014-2015 academic year, what was the average number of enrolled students aged 5 to 17 eligible for free or reduced price meals per Youth Authority school? Count every Youth Authority school regardless of its status (active, closed, or merged), and treat a Youth Authority school with no meal-program record as zero. Please give me just that one number, rounded to two decimal places.
evidence: A Youth Authority school is a school the state directory classifies as a Youth Authority Facility.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(SUM(COALESCE(t1."FRPM Count (Ages 5-17)", 0.0)) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(t2.cdscode), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_frpm_ages_5_17 FROM schools AS t2 LEFT JOIN frpm AS t1 ON t1.cdscode = t2.cdscode WHERE CAST(t2.soctype AS TEXT) LIKE '%Youth Authority%'

question: I have a school's CDS code from a separate list of Alameda County schools on Breakfast Provision 2, and I need to confirm which school it is. For the school with CDS code 1612590136051, please give me the school name and the educational instruction level name. This CDS code identifies exactly one school, so return only that school.
evidence: Breakfast Provision 2: the NSLP provision status category the school participates in. CDS code 1612590136051: the school identifier being asked about.
SQL: SELECT s.school, s.eilname FROM schools AS s INNER JOIN frpm AS f ON s.cdscode = f.cdscode WHERE f."NSLP Provision Status" = 'Breakfast Provision 2' AND f."County Name" = 'Alameda' AND CASE WHEN (s.cdscode) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((s.cdscode) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END = 1612590136051

question: I'm looking at the schools that the State Board of Education directly runs or charters. Which individual school among them had the most students score at least 1500 on the SAT? Please give me that school's name and its administrator's email address. If two schools tie on that count, list both.
evidence: Schools run or chartered by the State Board of Education are identified by their district ownership type.
SQL: SELECT t2.school, t2.admemail1 FROM satscores AS t1 INNER JOIN schools AS t2 ON t1.cds = t2.cdscode WHERE t2.doctype = 'State Board of Education' AND t1.rtype = 'S' AND t1.numge1500 = (SELECT MAX(t3.numge1500) FROM satscores AS t3 INNER JOIN schools AS t4 ON t3.cds = t4.cdscode WHERE t4.doctype = 'State Board of Education' AND t3.rtype = 'S')

question: We're relocating to far Northern California and want to know how far north California's middle schools reach. A middle school means a school serving the middle grades, the level between elementary school and high school — count it as a middle school if either its school type or its school name marks it as serving the middle grades, so a junior high school whose name says 'Middle' counts. Include both open and closed schools. Please tell me which middle school is located furthest north in California, along with its school type (the value of the field named 'School Type'), its school name, and its latitude in degrees. If several middle schools tie for the highest latitude, list all of them.
evidence: middle school: a school serving the middle grades, the level between elementary school and high school
SQL: SELECT t1."School Type", t1."School Name", t2.latitude FROM frpm AS t1 INNER JOIN schools AS t2 ON t1.cdscode = t2.cdscode WHERE (CAST(t1."School Type" AS TEXT) LIKE '%Middle%' OR CAST(t1."School Name" AS TEXT) LIKE '%Middle%') AND t2.latitude = (SELECT MAX(t2b.latitude) FROM frpm AS t1b INNER JOIN schools AS t2b ON t1b.cdscode = t2b.cdscode WHERE CAST(t1b."School Type" AS TEXT) LIKE '%Middle%' OR CAST(t1b."School Name" AS TEXT) LIKE '%Middle%')

question: I'm working on a story about campuses Los Angeles County opened during 2007 and the SAT participation they drew. What was the average number of SAT test takers per school across Los Angeles County schools that opened during 2007 and are run by a school district? Please give me that single number, rounded to two decimals. A few things to keep in mind: a county office of education counts as the school district for the schools it runs; "opened during 2007" means the opening date falls in calendar year 2007; and a school with no SAT record counts as zero test takers.
evidence: SAT test takers: the number of test takers recorded for the school.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(SUM(COALESCE(sat.numtsttakr, 0)) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_sat_test_takers FROM schools AS s LEFT JOIN satscores AS sat ON sat.cds = s.cdscode WHERE s.county = 'Los Angeles' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(s.opendate AS TIMESTAMP)) = '2007' AND (CAST(s.doctype AS TEXT) ILIKE '%school district%' OR CAST(s.doctype AS TEXT) ILIKE '%county office of education%')

question: I'm reviewing charter school funding models and want to compare the directly funded and locally funded charters that are currently in operation. For each of the two funding categories, please give me: (1) the number of charter schools currently in operation, counting only schools the directory lists as active (open), not closed or merged; (2) total 2014-2015 K-12 enrollment; (3) the average percentage of students eligible for free or reduced-price meals, on a 0-100 scale, rounded to two decimals; and (4) the average combined SAT score (reading + math + writing) across schools that have reported scores, rounded to two decimals. Note that schools without SAT results should still count in the school count, enrollment total, and meal-eligibility average. Please give me these figures grouped by funding category.
evidence: Directly funded and locally funded are the two charter funding categories. Free or reduced-price meal eligibility is measured by the K-12 eligible percentage. Combined SAT score is the sum of the average reading, math and writing scores.
SQL: SELECT s.fundingtype AS funding_category, COUNT(*) AS operating_charter_schools, SUM(f."Enrollment (K-12)") AS total_k12_enrollment, ROUND(CAST(AVG(f."Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (K-12)") * 100 AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_frpm_percentage, ROUND(CAST(AVG(sat.avgscrread + sat.avgscrmath + sat.avgscrwrite) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_combined_sat FROM schools AS s LEFT JOIN frpm AS f ON f.cdscode = s.cdscode LEFT JOIN satscores AS sat ON sat.cds = s.cdscode WHERE s.charter = 1 AND s.statustype = 'Active' AND s.fundingtype IN ('Directly funded', 'Locally funded') GROUP BY s.fundingtype ORDER BY funding_category NULLS FIRST

question: Among California's state special schools, which one begins enrolling students at the latest grade level? Please give me: the school's name, the earliest grade level covered by its K-12 enrollment, its K-12 enrollment, and how many SAT test takers it had. In the grade-level codes, P means pre-kindergarten and K means kindergarten, and grades progress from pre-kindergarten to kindergarten to grades 1 through 12 — so a school starting at grade 1 starts later than one starting at kindergarten. If a state special school has no SAT record, still consider it a candidate and report it as having 0 SAT test takers. If two schools start at the same grade level, prefer the one with the larger K-12 enrollment; if still tied, the one whose name comes first alphabetically. The data is for the 2014-2015 school year.
evidence: A state special school is a school operated by the state of California that serves students with special needs, such as the schools for the deaf or the blind.
SQL: SELECT s.school AS school_name, f."Low Grade" AS starting_grade, f."Enrollment (K-12)" AS k12_enrollment, COALESCE(t.numtsttakr, 0) AS sat_test_takers FROM schools AS s JOIN frpm AS f ON f.cdscode = s.cdscode LEFT JOIN satscores AS t ON t.cds = s.cdscode WHERE s.doctype = 'State Special Schools' ORDER BY CASE f."Low Grade" WHEN 'P' THEN 0 WHEN 'K' THEN 1 ELSE CASE WHEN (f."Low Grade") IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((f."Low Grade") AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END + 1 END DESC NULLS LAST, f."Enrollment (K-12)" DESC NULLS LAST, s.school ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1

question: I'm putting together a brief on SAT participation among California's larger public schools. How many individual named school sites in the state with a K-12 enrollment over 500 and a highest grade served of 8 or below had no SAT test takers? I just need the school_count, a single whole number. Please count a school as an individual school site with a name - district and county offices of education are not schools. Include every qualifying school site statewide even if it shows no SAT results at all; such a site simply had no test takers. By highest grade served I mean the top grade level the school serves, as a grade number from 1 through 12.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS school_count FROM schools AS s JOIN frpm AS f ON f.cdscode = s.cdscode LEFT JOIN satscores AS t ON t.cds = s.cdscode WHERE NOT s.school IS NULL AND f."Enrollment (K-12)" > 500 AND CASE WHEN (f."High Grade") IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((f."High Grade") AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END BETWEEN 1 AND 8 AND COALESCE(t.numtsttakr, 0) = 0

question: I'm studying charter schools run by county offices of education. Using the K-12 school meal program records, for the charter schools these county offices operate, broken down by charter funding type (directly funded and locally funded only), I'd like to know: how many are currently operating, their total K-12 enrollment, and their total number of FRPM-eligible K-12 students. A school counts as currently operating only if its status is Active. Please give me one row per funding type, with directly funded first.
evidence: FRPM means free or reduced price meal eligibility.
SQL: SELECT f."Charter Funding Type" AS funding_type, COUNT(*) AS active_charter_schools, SUM(f."Enrollment (K-12)") AS total_k12_enrollment, SUM(f."FRPM Count (K-12)") AS total_frpm_students FROM frpm AS f INNER JOIN schools AS s ON f.cdscode = s.cdscode WHERE f."Charter School (Y/N)" = 1 AND f."District Type" = 'County Office of Education (COE)' AND f."Charter Funding Type" IN ('Directly funded', 'Locally funded') AND s.statustype = 'Active' GROUP BY f."Charter Funding Type" ORDER BY CASE f."Charter Funding Type" WHEN 'Directly funded' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END NULLS FIRST

question: I'm documenting now-closed California schools whose students performed best on the SAT writing section, and I need the runner-up. Among schools whose status is Closed (not Active, Merged or Pending), and which have an average SAT writing score, can you tell me which school had the second-highest average SAT writing score? By second-highest I mean the best score strictly below the highest – if several schools share that score, please list them all. For each school, give me its name, its own district and county, and its average SAT writing score.
evidence: SAT writing score: the average writing score of the school's SAT test takers.
SQL: WITH j AS (SELECT t2.school AS school, t2.district AS district, t2.county AS county, t1.avgscrwrite AS avgscrwrite FROM satscores AS t1 INNER JOIN schools AS t2 ON t1.cds = t2.cdscode WHERE t2.statustype = 'Closed' AND NOT t1.avgscrwrite IS NULL AND NOT t1.sname IS NULL) SELECT school, district, county, avgscrwrite FROM j WHERE avgscrwrite = (SELECT MAX(avgscrwrite) FROM j WHERE avgscrwrite < (SELECT MAX(avgscrwrite) FROM j))

question: I'm a parent looking at high schools in California, and I want to know how often a school that's still open has no seniors taking the SAT at all. How many currently open public high schools in California had zero students take the SAT? By 'currently open' I mean the school's status is Active, not closed or merged. By 'high school' I mean a school whose educational instruction level is High School. Please count a school that has no SAT record at all as having zero test takers. I just want that one number.
evidence: SAT test takers: the number of test takers recorded for the school in the SAT scores data.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS zero_taker_open_high_schools FROM schools AS sc LEFT JOIN satscores AS s ON sc.cdscode = s.cds WHERE sc.statustype = 'Active' AND sc.eilname = 'High School' AND COALESCE(s.numtsttakr, 0) = 0

question: I'm planning a targeted meal-support pilot and want to compare one school against similar schools in our county. The county I mean is the one where Fremont High (CDS code 1612590125716) is located - please identify the county by that CDS code, not by the school name. For that county, please look at all K-12 schools with more than 500 free meals and fewer than 700 FRPM meals, and give me back: the county name; the number of schools; the average free-meal percentage and the average FRPM percentage, both on a 0-100 scale with each school's own percentage rounded to 2 decimals before averaging; the number of charter schools and the number of non-charter schools (charter vs. non-charter per the charter indicator in the frpm data); and the average SAT score, where a school's SAT score is the sum of its three SAT section averages, counted only for schools that actually have SAT records, with no SAT record meaning the school is simply excluded from that average. Please round the reported averages to 2 decimals.
evidence: Free meal percentage = free meal count (K-12) / enrollment (K-12) * 100; FRPM percentage = FRPM count (K-12) / enrollment (K-12) * 100; charter school = charter indicator 1, non-charter = charter indicator 0.
SQL: WITH targetcounty AS (SELECT "County Name" AS countyname FROM frpm WHERE CASE WHEN (cdscode) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((cdscode) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END = 1612590125716), cohort AS (SELECT f.cdscode, ROUND(CAST(f."Free Meal Count (K-12)" / NULLIF(f."Enrollment (K-12)", 0) * 100 AS DECIMAL), 2) AS freepct, ROUND(CAST(f."FRPM Count (K-12)" / NULLIF(f."Enrollment (K-12)", 0) * 100 AS DECIMAL), 2) AS frpmpct, f."Charter School (Y/N)" AS charterflag, sd.avgscrread + sd.avgscrmath + sd.avgscrwrite AS satscore FROM frpm AS f JOIN targetcounty AS t ON f."County Name" = t.countyname LEFT JOIN satscores AS sd ON f.cdscode = sd.cds WHERE f."Free Meal Count (K-12)" > 500 AND f."FRPM Count (K-12)" < 700) SELECT (SELECT countyname FROM targetcounty) AS county_name, COUNT(*) AS school_count, ROUND(CAST(AVG(freepct) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_free_meal_pct, ROUND(CAST(AVG(frpmpct) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_frpm_pct, SUM(CASE WHEN charterflag = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS charter_count, SUM(CASE WHEN charterflag = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS non_charter_count, ROUND(CAST(AVG(satscore) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_sat_score FROM cohort

question: I'm studying the 1980 growth of public schooling in San Diego County. What was the average number of schools per month that opened in San Diego County in 1980 under a school district's jurisdiction? I need just that single number. Please average over all 12 months of 1980 (months with no openings count as zero), and give me the exact average without rounding.
evidence: A school district is a local education agency that runs K-12 public schools; it is an elementary school district, a high school district, or a unified school district.
SQL: SELECT CASE WHEN (COUNT(*)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((COUNT(*)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END / NULLIF(12, 0) AS monthly_average FROM schools WHERE county = 'San Diego' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(opendate AS TIMESTAMP)) = '1980' AND doctype IN ('Elementary School District', 'High School District', 'Unified School District')

question: Among California schools whose students have an average SAT Math score above 400, what percentage offer virtual instruction, either exclusively or in part? Please give me a single percentage value rounded to one decimal place.
evidence: In the school directory, the exclusive-virtual category is coded 'F' and the partial-virtual category is coded 'P'.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN s.virtual IN ('F', 'P') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS pct FROM satscores AS sat JOIN schools AS s ON sat.cds = s.cdscode WHERE sat.rtype = 'S' AND sat.avgscrmath > 400

question: A parent is asking about a school and could only give me the CDS code 1612590137943. Can you look up that school and give me its name, county, district, and city; its K-12 enrollment; the number of K-12 students eligible for free or reduced price meals and the percentage eligible (report the percentage exactly as it appears, without rounding); and the SAT results - number of test takers, average reading score, average math score, average writing score, and the number of test takers whose total score is at least 1500?
evidence: CDS code: the state's County-District-School identification code assigned to each school; FRPM: the Free or Reduced Price Meal program, where the FRPM count is the number of students eligible.
SQL: SELECT s.school AS school_name, s.county AS county, s.district AS district, s.city AS city, f."Enrollment (K-12)" AS enrollment_k12, f."FRPM Count (K-12)" AS frpm_count, f."Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (K-12)" AS pct_eligible_frpm, sat.numtsttakr AS num_sat_takers, sat.avgscrread AS avg_reading, sat.avgscrmath AS avg_math, sat.avgscrwrite AS avg_writing, sat.numge1500 AS num_ge_1500 FROM schools AS s JOIN frpm AS f ON f.cdscode = s.cdscode LEFT JOIN satscores AS sat ON sat.cds = s.cdscode WHERE CASE WHEN (s.cdscode) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((s.cdscode) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END = 1612590137943

question: I'm putting together a profile of Alameda County high schools, focusing on economic disadvantage among schools that serve up through 12th grade. Among those schools, can you tell me which one has the highest free meal rate? For each school you identify, give me one line with: the school name, its free meal rate to 4 decimal places, whether it is a charter school (Yes/No/Unknown), the grades it serves, and its SAT performance level (Below Average, Average, Above Average, or No SAT Data). Please use the school's grade span of enrollment from the school directory (the GSserved field of the schools table) both to decide whether it serves up through 12th grade and for the grades-it-serves column-do not use the free-meal program record's Low Grade/High Grade for either. If several schools tie for the highest free meal rate, list every one of them.
evidence: Free meal rate = Free Meal Count (K-12) / Enrollment (K-12). SAT performance level is based on the SAT total (Reading + Math + Writing): Below Average if below 1200, Average if 1200 to 1500, Above Average if above 1500, and 'No SAT Data' if no SAT scores are available.
SQL: WITH cohort AS (SELECT f."School Name" AS school_name, f."Free Meal Count (K-12)" * 1.0 / NULLIF(f."Enrollment (K-12)", 0) AS free_rate, sc.charter, sc.gsserved, s.avgscrread, s.avgscrmath, s.avgscrwrite FROM frpm AS f LEFT JOIN schools AS sc ON sc.cdscode = f.cdscode LEFT JOIN satscores AS s ON s.cds = f.cdscode WHERE f."County Name" = 'Alameda' AND RIGHT(CAST(sc.gsserved AS TEXT), 2) = '12') SELECT school_name, ROUND(CAST(free_rate AS DECIMAL), 4) AS highest_free_meal_rate, CASE WHEN charter = 1 THEN 'Yes' WHEN charter = 0 THEN 'No' ELSE 'Unknown' END AS is_charter, gsserved AS grades_served, CASE WHEN avgscrread IS NULL THEN 'No SAT Data' WHEN avgscrread + avgscrmath + avgscrwrite < 1200 THEN 'Below Average' WHEN avgscrread + avgscrmath + avgscrwrite <= 1500 THEN 'Average' ELSE 'Above Average' END AS sat_performance FROM cohort WHERE free_rate = (SELECT MAX(f2."Free Meal Count (K-12)" * 1.0 / NULLIF(f2."Enrollment (K-12)", 0)) FROM frpm AS f2 JOIN schools AS s2 ON s2.cdscode = f2.cdscode WHERE f2."County Name" = 'Alameda' AND RIGHT(CAST(s2.gsserved AS TEXT), 2) = '12')

question: Could you pull a full profile for the school with CDS code 7618040113118? I need its name, phone number, website, average SAT reading, math and writing scores, whether it is a charter school, its K-12 enrollment for the 2014-2015 academic year, and the percentage of its students eligible for free or reduced price meals on a 0-100 scale rounded to two decimal places. Alongside that, please find the highest average SAT math score achieved by any active school with at least 10 SAT test takers – if several schools tie for the highest, just give me that single score – and how far below that highest score this school's math score falls.
evidence: CDS code is the California Department of Education's school identifier; a charter school is one with charter status recorded as 1.
SQL: WITH benchmark AS (SELECT MAX(t.avgscrmath) AS topmath FROM satscores AS t INNER JOIN schools AS s ON s.cdscode = t.cds WHERE s.statustype = 'Active' AND t.numtsttakr >= 10) SELECT s.school AS "School Name", s.phone AS "Phone Number", s.website AS website, t.avgscrread AS "Average SAT Reading Score", t.avgscrmath AS "Average SAT Math Score", t.avgscrwrite AS "Average SAT Writing Score", f."Charter School (Y/N)" AS "Charter School Status", f."Enrollment (K-12)" AS "K-12 Enrollment (2014-2015)", ROUND(CAST(f."Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (K-12)" * 100 AS DECIMAL), 2) AS "Percent Eligible Free/Reduced Price Meals", b.topmath AS "Highest Average Math Score", b.topmath - t.avgscrmath AS "Gap Below Highest Math Score" FROM schools AS s INNER JOIN satscores AS t ON t.cds = s.cdscode LEFT JOIN frpm AS f ON f.cdscode = s.cdscode AND f."Academic Year" = '2014-2015' CROSS JOIN benchmark AS b WHERE CASE WHEN (s.cdscode) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((s.cdscode) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END = 7618040113118

question: I'm mapping where exclusively virtual schools are concentrated. For the five counties with the most exclusively virtual schools - if several counties tie with the fifth-highest count, include all of them - please give me for each county: the county name, how many exclusively virtual schools it has, and the name of the exclusively virtual school in that county with the highest average SAT reading score. If several schools tie for the highest average reading score in a county, list each of them. If none of the county's exclusively virtual schools has a reported reading average, show 'None' as the school name.
evidence: An exclusively virtual school is one whose Virtual field holds the code 'F'.
SQL: WITH virtual_counts AS (SELECT county, COUNT(*) AS virtual_schools FROM schools WHERE virtual = 'F' GROUP BY county), top_counties AS (SELECT county, virtual_schools FROM virtual_counts WHERE virtual_schools >= (SELECT MIN(virtual_schools) FROM (SELECT virtual_schools FROM virtual_counts ORDER BY virtual_schools DESC NULLS LAST, county NULLS FIRST LIMIT 5) AS __photo_derived_1)), best AS (SELECT s.county, s.school, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY s.county ORDER BY sat.avgscrread DESC NULLS LAST) AS r FROM schools AS s JOIN satscores AS sat ON s.cdscode = sat.cds WHERE s.virtual = 'F' AND NOT sat.avgscrread IS NULL) SELECT t.county, t.virtual_schools, COALESCE(b.school, 'None') AS school FROM top_counties AS t LEFT JOIN best AS b ON b.county = t.county AND b.r = 1 ORDER BY t.virtual_schools DESC NULLS LAST, t.county NULLS FIRST

question: I'm comparing online-only schooling options. I'd like to know, for Santa Barbara County and for the county that contains the school with CDS code 1100170109835 (which identifies one school), how many exclusive-virtual schools are in each county. Please give me each county's name with its number of exclusive-virtual schools, listing the county with the larger number first, or alphabetically by county name if they tie.
evidence: A school counts as exclusive-virtual only if its virtual-instruction category is coded 'F'.
SQL: WITH target AS (SELECT county FROM schools WHERE CASE WHEN (cdscode) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((cdscode) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END = 1100170109835), cands AS (SELECT county FROM target UNION SELECT 'Santa Barbara') SELECT c.county AS county, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM schools AS s WHERE s.county = c.county AND s.virtual = 'F') AS num FROM cands AS c ORDER BY num DESC NULLS LAST, c.county NULLS FIRST

question: I'm studying how concentrated economic need relates to SAT outcomes in California public schools. Among regular, non-charter schools with more than 100 K-12 students, I'd like two extremes plus one benchmark school: the school with the largest count of FRPM-eligible students, the school with the smallest FRPM share (the proportion of its K-12 enrollment that is FRPM-eligible – smallest by that share, not the raw count), and the school with CDS code 4615150435602 from my notes. If a school answers more than one part, report it once per part, and label each row with which part it answers ('largest FRPM-eligible count', 'smallest FRPM share', or 'the CDS code from my notes', in that order). Include ties. For each school, please give: school name, county, city, full mailing address as four columns (mailing street, mailing city, mailing state, mailing ZIP), website, K-12 enrollment, FRPM-eligible student count, FRPM share, average total SAT score (reading + math + writing) among its SAT takers, percentage of its SAT takers scoring 1500 or more, opening date, and status ('closed' if a closing date is recorded, otherwise 'open'). Nothing else, please.
evidence: CDS code: the California Department of Education's identification code for a school; the benchmark school in my notes is identified by CDS code 4615150435602.
SQL: WITH cohort AS (SELECT f.cdscode, f."School Name" AS schoolname, f."FRPM Count (K-12)" AS frpmcount, f."Enrollment (K-12)" AS enrollment, f."FRPM Count (K-12)" * 1.0 / NULLIF(f."Enrollment (K-12)", 0) AS frpmshare, CASE WHEN (f.cdscode) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((f.cdscode) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END AS code_num FROM frpm AS f WHERE f."Charter School (Y/N)" = 0 AND f."Enrollment (K-12)" > 100) SELECT 'largest FRPM-eligible count' AS requestpart, c.schoolname AS schoolname, s.county AS county, s.city AS city, s.mailstreet AS mailingstreet, s.mailcity AS mailingcity, s.mailstate AS mailingstate, s.mailzip AS mailingzip, s.website AS website, c.enrollment AS enrollment, c.frpmcount AS frpmcount, c.frpmshare AS frpmshare, t.avgscrread + t.avgscrmath + t.avgscrwrite AS avgtotalsat, CAST(t.numge1500 * 100.0 AS DOUBLE PRECISION) / NULLIF(NULLIF(t.numtsttakr, 0), 0) AS pct1500plus, s.opendate AS opendate, CASE WHEN NOT s.closeddate IS NULL THEN 'closed' ELSE 'open' END AS schoolstatus FROM cohort AS c JOIN schools AS s ON c.code_num = CASE WHEN (s.cdscode) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((s.cdscode) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END LEFT JOIN satscores AS t ON c.code_num = CASE WHEN (t.cds) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((t.cds) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END WHERE c.frpmcount = (SELECT MAX(x.frpmcount) FROM cohort AS x) UNION ALL SELECT 'smallest FRPM share', c.schoolname, s.county, s.city, s.mailstreet, s.mailcity, s.mailstate, s.mailzip, s.website, c.enrollment, c.frpmcount, c.frpmshare, t.avgscrread + t.avgscrmath + t.avgscrwrite, CAST(t.numge1500 * 100.0 AS DOUBLE PRECISION) / NULLIF(NULLIF(t.numtsttakr, 0), 0), s.opendate, CASE WHEN NOT s.closeddate IS NULL THEN 'closed' ELSE 'open' END FROM cohort AS c JOIN schools AS s ON c.code_num = CASE WHEN (s.cdscode) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((s.cdscode) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END LEFT JOIN satscores AS t ON c.code_num = CASE WHEN (t.cds) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((t.cds) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END WHERE c.frpmshare = (SELECT MIN(x.frpmshare) FROM cohort AS x) UNION ALL SELECT 'the CDS code from my notes', c.schoolname, s.county, s.city, s.mailstreet, s.mailcity, s.mailstate, s.mailzip, s.website, c.enrollment, c.frpmcount, c.frpmshare, t.avgscrread + t.avgscrmath + t.avgscrwrite, CAST(t.numge1500 * 100.0 AS DOUBLE PRECISION) / NULLIF(NULLIF(t.numtsttakr, 0), 0), s.opendate, CASE WHEN NOT s.closeddate IS NULL THEN 'closed' ELSE 'open' END FROM cohort AS c JOIN schools AS s ON c.code_num = CASE WHEN (s.cdscode) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((s.cdscode) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END LEFT JOIN satscores AS t ON c.code_num = CASE WHEN (t.cds) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((t.cds) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END WHERE c.code_num = 4615150435602

question: I'm auditing FRPM enrollment reporting and need to contact some elementary and middle schools. Please list the name and street address of every named school whose K-12 enrollment exceeds its enrollment of students aged 5-17 by more than 30 students, and whose highest grade of enrollment is grade 8 or below. Kindergarten counts as grade 8 or below. Give me one row per school; any order is fine.
evidence: K-12 enrollment is enrollment counted for kindergarten through grade 12. Enrollment of ages 5-17 is enrollment counted for students aged 5 through 17. Highest grade of enrollment is the highest grade level the school enrolls students in (e.g., grade 8 for a school serving kindergarten through grade 8).
SQL: SELECT s.school, s.street FROM schools AS s JOIN frpm AS f ON f.cdscode = s.cdscode WHERE NOT s.school IS NULL AND f."Enrollment (K-12)" - f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)" > 30 AND (f."High Grade" = 'K' OR (f."High Grade" = CAST(CASE WHEN (f."High Grade") IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((f."High Grade") AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END AS TEXT) AND CASE WHEN (f."High Grade") IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((f."High Grade") AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END <= 8)) ORDER BY s.cdscode NULLS FIRST

question: I'm auditing high-school-level campuses that draw enrollments beyond their surrounding school-age population. Can you give me a list of schools where the K-12 enrollment exceeds the ages-5-17 enrollment by more than 30, limited to schools whose lowest served grade is grade 9 or a later grade (a school's lowest served grade being the low end of the grade range reported in the same enrollment record as its K-12 and ages-5-17 counts)? For each school, I just need the school name and street address. Please order the results by the school's CDS code, smallest first.
evidence: CDS code: a school's identifier in the California schools data.
SQL: SELECT s.school, s.street FROM schools AS s JOIN frpm AS f ON f.cdscode = s.cdscode WHERE NOT s.school IS NULL AND f."Enrollment (K-12)" - f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)" > 30 AND CASE WHEN (f."Low Grade") IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((f."Low Grade") AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END BETWEEN 9 AND 12 ORDER BY s.cdscode NULLS FIRST

question: I'm researching where high SAT performance coexists with concentrated poverty, to help target college-access support by county. For the 2014-15 academic year, for each county, how many schools had both a K-12 free-meal eligibility rate above 0.1 and at least one SAT taker scoring 1500 or higher on the school's own SAT record? Please list only counties that have at least one such school, with the county name and the number of its qualifying schools, sorted from most such schools to fewest, and alphabetically by county name when counties tie.
evidence: K-12 free-meal eligibility rate: the share of a school's K-12 enrollment that is eligible for free meals (free meal count divided by K-12 enrollment).
SQL: SELECT s.cname AS county, COUNT(*) AS qualifying_schools FROM satscores AS s JOIN frpm AS f ON f.cdscode = s.cds WHERE s.rtype = 'S' AND s.numge1500 > 0 AND f."Enrollment (K-12)" > 0 AND 1.0 * f."Free Meal Count (K-12)" / NULLIF(f."Enrollment (K-12)", 0) > 0.1 GROUP BY s.cname ORDER BY qualifying_schools DESC NULLS LAST, county ASC NULLS FIRST

question: I have a school on file with CDS code 1611430131177. Find the school in the same county as that school whose own SAT record shows the most students scoring at least 1500 (not a district-wide roll-up). If two schools tie on that count, use the one with the smaller CDS code. Send me that school's administrator's first and last name.
evidence: CDS code: the County-District-School identifier assigned to each school; scoring at least 1500: a test taker whose combined SAT score is 1500 or higher.
SQL: SELECT s.admfname1, s.admlname1 FROM satscores AS x JOIN schools AS s ON s.cdscode = x.cds JOIN frpm AS f ON f.cdscode = x.cds WHERE x.rtype = 'S' AND s.county = (SELECT county FROM schools WHERE CASE WHEN (cdscode) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((cdscode) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END = 1611430131177) ORDER BY x.numge1500 DESC NULLS LAST, CASE WHEN (f."School Code") IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((f."School Code") AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1

question: I'm working on a story about the largest schools in the state with the worst SAT excellence rates. Among schools where at least 700 students took the SAT, can you find the school with the lowest SAT excellence rate? If several schools tie for the lowest rate, go with the one with the smallest school code. I just need that school's street, city, ZIP code and state so I can visit and request an interview.
evidence: The SAT excellence rate is the share of SAT test takers scoring at least 1500. A school code is a number.
SQL: SELECT s.street, s.city, s.zip, s.state FROM satscores AS sat JOIN schools AS s ON s.cdscode = sat.cds LEFT JOIN frpm AS f ON f.cdscode = sat.cds WHERE sat.rtype = 'S' AND NOT sat.numge1500 IS NULL AND sat.numtsttakr >= 700 ORDER BY 1.0 * sat.numge1500 / NULLIF(sat.numtsttakr, 0) ASC NULLS FIRST, CASE WHEN (f."School Code") IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((f."School Code") AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1

question: I'm planning reviews of Provision 2 meal programs under the NSLP and want to see which cities concentrate magnet schools under that provision. For each city that has at least one, can you give me the number of the city's magnet schools that run a Provision 2 meal program? Use the city where the school is located, not its mailing city. Also, if a school's NSLP entry lists multiple provision types, don't count it as running Provision 2.
evidence: NSLP is the National School Lunch Program. Provision 2 is a federal provision under the NSLP that lets a school serve meals at no charge to all students regardless of family income.
SQL: SELECT s.city AS city, COUNT(*) AS magnet_schools FROM frpm AS f JOIN schools AS s ON f.cdscode = s.cdscode WHERE s.magnet = 1 AND CAST(f."NSLP Provision Status" AS TEXT) LIKE '%Provision 2%' GROUP BY s.city ORDER BY magnet_schools DESC NULLS LAST, city NULLS FIRST

question: I'm preparing a mailing campaign and need a list of public high schools in Los Angeles County that have more than 500 free or reduced-price meal recipients ages 5-17. By public high schools I mean every public high-school category in the meal program report - regular high schools, continuation high schools, and high schools in single-school districts - not just regular ones; middle and junior high schools don't count. For each school, please give me the school name exactly as listed in the school directory, plus the campus (physical) street address - not a mailing or post-office address - along with the city, state and ZIP code, each as a separate field. Schools sharing a name are separate schools, so one row per school. Please sort the list by school name.
evidence: 'Free or reduced-price meal recipients ages 5-17' refers to the count reported in the meal program report for students ages 5-17 receiving free or reduced-price meals.
SQL: SELECT s.school AS school_name, s.street, s.city, s.state, s.zip FROM frpm AS f JOIN schools AS s ON f.cdscode = s.cdscode WHERE f."County Name" = 'Los Angeles' AND CAST(f."School Type" AS TEXT) LIKE '%High School%' AND CAST(f."School Type" AS TEXT) NOT LIKE '%Junior%' AND f."FRPM Count (Ages 5-17)" > 500 ORDER BY s.school COLLATE "C" NULLS FIRST, s.cdscode NULLS FIRST

question: I'd like to compare SAT participation across counties in California that run magnet schools under Provision 2 of the National School Lunch Program. For every county with at least one Provision 2 magnet school, can you give me the county name and the total number of SAT test takers from those schools? Please include every such county even if the total is 0, and list them in any order.
evidence: Provision 2 school: a school whose NSLP Provision Status is Provision 2. Magnet school: a school identified as a magnet school or providing a magnet program.
SQL: SELECT s.county AS county, SUM(COALESCE(sc.numtsttakr, 0)) AS total_sat_test_takers FROM schools AS s INNER JOIN frpm AS f ON s.cdscode = f.cdscode LEFT JOIN satscores AS sc ON sc.cds = s.cdscode WHERE s.magnet = 1 AND f."NSLP Provision Status" = 'Provision 2' GROUP BY s.county ORDER BY total_sat_test_takers DESC NULLS LAST, s.county NULLS FIRST

question: List the IDs of borderless card printings for which Card Kingdom lacks a regular-version listing or a foil-version listing.
SQL: SELECT id FROM cards WHERE bordercolor = 'borderless' AND (cardkingdomid IS NULL OR cardkingdomfoilid IS NULL) ORDER BY id NULLS FIRST

question: Which distinct combinations of card name, artist, and promotional-printing flag occur among the printings tied for the most rulings?
SQL: WITH ruling_counts AS (SELECT uuid, COUNT(*) AS n FROM rulings GROUP BY uuid), max_count AS (SELECT MAX(n) AS n FROM ruling_counts) SELECT DISTINCT c.name, c.artist, c.ispromo FROM cards AS c JOIN ruling_counts AS rc ON c.uuid = rc.uuid JOIN max_count AS mx ON rc.n = mx.n ORDER BY c.name NULLS FIRST, c.artist NULLS FIRST, c.ispromo NULLS FIRST

question: What percentage of all card printings have a Simplified Chinese translation? Round to two decimals.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(100.0 * (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.uuid) FROM cards AS c JOIN foreign_data AS f ON f.uuid = c.uuid WHERE f.language = 'Chinese Simplified') / NULLIF(NULLIF((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards), 0), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2)

question: What rules text is printed on Benalish Knight? Return the distinct text as one line.
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT REPLACE(text, CHR(10), ' ') FROM cards WHERE name = 'Benalish Knight' AND NOT text IS NULL

question: Among all Story Spotlight card printings, what percentage have a French translation? Round to two decimals.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(100.0 * (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.uuid) FROM cards AS c JOIN foreign_data AS f ON f.uuid = c.uuid WHERE c.isstoryspotlight = 1 AND f.language = 'French') / NULLIF(NULLIF((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards WHERE isstoryspotlight = 1), 0), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2)

question: What are the cards belong to duel deck a? List the ID.
SQL: SELECT id FROM cards WHERE dueldeck = 'a'

question: How many distinct white-bordered card printings are banned in at least one play format?
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.id) FROM cards AS c JOIN legalities AS l ON l.uuid = c.uuid WHERE l.status = 'Banned' AND c.bordercolor = 'white'

question: How many distinct card printings with no recorded power value or a variable power expression have at least one ruling mentioning 'triggered ability'?
evidence: An asterisk anywhere in a power expression denotes variable power.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t1.id) FROM cards AS t1 INNER JOIN rulings AS t2 ON t1.uuid = t2.uuid WHERE (t1.power IS NULL OR CAST(t1.power AS TEXT) LIKE '%*%') AND CAST(t2.text AS TEXT) LIKE '%triggered ability%'

question: What percentage of cards with format commander and legal status do not have a content warning?
SQL: SELECT CASE WHEN (SUM(CASE WHEN t1.hascontentwarning = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(CASE WHEN t1.hascontentwarning = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(t1.id), 0) FROM cards AS t1 INNER JOIN legalities AS t2 ON t1.uuid = t2.uuid WHERE t2.format = 'commander' AND t2.status = 'Legal'

question: Among card printings with no recorded power value or a variable power expression, what percentage have a French translation? Round to two decimals.
evidence: An asterisk anywhere in a power expression denotes variable power.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(100.0 * (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.uuid) FROM cards AS c JOIN foreign_data AS f ON f.uuid = c.uuid WHERE (c.power IS NULL OR CAST(c.power AS TEXT) LIKE '%*%') AND f.language = 'French') / NULLIF(NULLIF((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards WHERE power IS NULL OR CAST(power AS TEXT) LIKE '%*%'), 0), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2)

question: Among the sets in the block "Ice Age", how many of them have an Italian translation?
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t1.id) FROM sets AS t1 INNER JOIN set_translations AS t2 ON t2.setcode = t1.code WHERE t1.block = 'Ice Age' AND t2.language = 'Italian' AND NOT t2.translation IS NULL

question: What percentage of Coldsnap card printings have both a Card Kingdom regular-product ID and foil-product ID recorded?
SQL: SELECT CASE WHEN (SUM(CASE WHEN NOT t1.cardkingdomfoilid IS NULL AND NOT t1.cardkingdomid IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(CASE WHEN NOT t1.cardkingdomfoilid IS NULL AND NOT t1.cardkingdomid IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(t1.id), 0) FROM cards AS t1 INNER JOIN sets AS t2 ON t2.code = t1.setcode WHERE t2.name = 'Coldsnap'

question: Which play format has the most banned card-printing records? Give that format and the distinct names of its banned cards.
SQL: SELECT format, name FROM (SELECT l.format, c.name, MIN(c.uuid) AS sort_uuid FROM legalities AS l JOIN cards AS c ON c.uuid = l.uuid WHERE l.status = 'Banned' AND l.format = (SELECT format FROM legalities WHERE status = 'Banned' GROUP BY format ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC NULLS LAST, format NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1) GROUP BY l.format, c.name) AS banned_names ORDER BY sort_uuid NULLS FIRST

question: I collect promotional printings and play Brawl. How many different creature cards that have a promotional printing can serve as a Brawl commander? I just want a single number back.
evidence: A promotional printing is a printing of a card made as a promotion, as opposed to a regular set printing. Brawl is a Magic: The Gathering format; the deck's commander is the card that leads it, and only certain cards are legal as a Brawl commander.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT name) AS creature_cards_legal_brawl_commanders FROM cards WHERE ispromo = 1 AND POSITION('Creature' IN types) > 0 AND POSITION('''brawl'': True' IN leadershipskills) > 0

question: I'm cataloguing how the frame styles on Tarmogoyf's printings evolved over time. What is the number of years between the oldest and the newest frame style used on the printings of Tarmogoyf? The span in years is the newer year minus the older year.
evidence: Frame style version means the year a card's frame style dates from.
SQL: SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN (frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END) - MIN(CASE WHEN (frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END) AS years_between FROM cards WHERE name = 'Tarmogoyf' AND frameversion = CAST(CASE WHEN (frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END AS TEXT)

question: How many black-border cards with power 10 or greater are available on Magic: The Gathering Online? I just want a single number.
evidence: Black-border cards are the tournament-legal Magic cards, excluding the joke silver-bordered sets. Power is the first number in the lower-right corner of a creature card.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(id) FROM cards WHERE bordercolor = 'black' AND CAST(availability AS TEXT) LIKE '%mtgo%' AND CASE WHEN (power) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((power) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END >= 10

question: I have the count of sets with fewer than five translations of their name — now I need the gap in cards to size the translation budget. Can you give me the total number of cards contained in those sets? A few things to keep in mind: 'fewer than five' is strict, so a set with exactly five translations doesn't count. All sets count regardless of type or release (core set, expansion, promotional, online-only, etc.). If two languages have the identical translated name string for a set, that's one translation, not two. And a set's card count should be its full size, including promotional and related supplemental printings.
evidence: A 'translation of a set's name' means the localized name of the set in another language, e.g. its French or Simplified Chinese name.
SQL: SELECT SUM(totalsetsize) AS total_cards FROM sets WHERE (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT translation) FROM set_translations WHERE setcode = sets.code) < 5

question: I'm preparing a multilingual catalog and want to gauge how much localizable content exists per kind of set. For every set type, I need the number of sets of that type that have an officially translated name, and the total number of cards in those sets. Please include every set type in the results, even ones where no set has an officially translated name (show zero for both values in that case), and sort the results alphabetically by set type.
evidence: Set type: the expansion type of a set, such as core, expansion or promo. Officially translated name: the set's name rendered in another language, such as Italian or Chinese Traditional.
SQL: SELECT s.type, SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM set_translations AS t WHERE t.setcode = s.code) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS sets_with_translation, SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM set_translations AS t WHERE t.setcode = s.code) THEN s.totalsetsize ELSE 0 END) AS total_cards FROM sets AS s GROUP BY s.type ORDER BY s.type NULLS FIRST

question: How many rulings were issued for Mishra's Factory on the latest date any ruling for it exists? By "latest date" I mean the most recent calendar date on which any ruling for the card exists, and by Mishra's Factory I mean the card by that name across all of its printings. I only want that count.
evidence: ruling: an official rules statement issued for a card on a given date
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t2.text) AS ruling_count FROM cards AS t1 INNER JOIN rulings AS t2 ON t1.uuid = t2.uuid WHERE t1.name = 'Mishra''s Factory' AND t2.date = (SELECT MAX(t4.date) FROM cards AS t3 INNER JOIN rulings AS t4 ON t3.uuid = t4.uuid WHERE t3.name = 'Mishra''s Factory')

question: Which artist has illustrated the most different creature cards, and how many different creature cards is that? I'd like each artist's name along with their count of different creature cards. If two artists are tied for the most, list both.
evidence: A creature card is a card whose card types include Creature.
SQL: SELECT artist, COUNT(DISTINCT name) AS distinct_creatures FROM cards WHERE CAST(types AS TEXT) LIKE '%Creature%' GROUP BY artist HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT name) = (SELECT MAX(cnt) FROM (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT name) AS cnt FROM cards WHERE CAST(types AS TEXT) LIKE '%Creature%' GROUP BY artist) AS __photo_derived_1) ORDER BY artist NULLS FIRST

question: I'm putting together a showcase of zero-mana-cost cards. What is the newest frame version used by any card with a converted mana cost of 0? Please give me that frame version value, and the number of cards in the database that use that frame version. The count should cover all cards in the database, not just the zero-cost ones. If several frame versions tie as the newest, give me each of them with its own count.
evidence: Frame version: the edition of the card frame style a printing uses.
SQL: SELECT frameversion, COUNT(*) AS card_count FROM cards WHERE CASE WHEN (frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END = (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN (frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END) FROM cards WHERE convertedmanacost = 0) GROUP BY frameversion

question: I'm tracking printings of Tarmogoyf. Of all its printings, which frame version is the newest? Please give me the year that identifies that latest frame version, and the percentage of the card's printings that use it, rounded to two decimal places. The percentage should be over all printings of the card.
evidence: A printing is an occurrence of the card in a set; a frame version is the version of the card frame style of a printing.
SQL: WITH target AS (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN (frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END) AS yr FROM cards WHERE name = 'Tarmogoyf') SELECT t.yr AS frame_version_year, ROUND(CAST(CASE WHEN (SUM(CASE WHEN CASE WHEN (c.frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((c.frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END = t.yr THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(CASE WHEN CASE WHEN (c.frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((c.frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END = t.yr THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(c.id), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS percentage FROM cards AS c CROSS JOIN target AS t WHERE c.name = 'Tarmogoyf' GROUP BY t.yr

question: I'm building an artifact-heavy Commander deck and want to know the size of the pool of zero-cost cards available to me. How many different cards have a printed mana cost of {0} and are legal in Commander? A card is legal in Commander if its Commander legality entry is marked Legal.
evidence: Printed mana cost of 0 means the cost shown on the card is {0}. Commander is a format of play in which any card marked Legal for that format is playable.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.name) AS different_cards FROM cards AS c JOIN legalities AS l ON c.uuid = l.uuid WHERE c.manacost = '{0}' AND l.format = 'commander' AND l.status = 'Legal'

question: I'm brewing and looking for cards that combine two keyword abilities. How many cards in the collection have both Flying and Cycling? Note that each printing counts as its own card, and a card only counts if it has both keywords.
evidence: Flying and Cycling are keyword abilities in Magic: The Gathering.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS card_count FROM cards WHERE POSITION(',' || 'Flying' || ',' IN ',' || keywords || ',') > 0 AND POSITION(',' || 'Cycling' || ',' IN ',' || keywords || ',') > 0

question: I'm comparing how mana-cheap Magic: The Gathering sets have become over time. For two sets — the set where Abyssal Horror was first printed, and the most recently released set in the database — I want one row per set with the set name and the percentage of that set's cards that have a mana cost whose converted mana cost is 3 or less, rounded to two decimal places. By "first printed", I mean the set with the earliest release date among the sets Abyssal Horror appears in; if several share that earliest date, use the one whose set code comes first alphabetically. For the most recent set, use the latest release date among all sets; if several share that date, again take the one whose set code comes first alphabetically. By "converted mana cost" I mean the card's mana value, and a card counts as having a mana cost only if a mana cost is printed on it.
evidence: Converted mana cost means the card's mana value; a card has a mana cost when a mana cost is printed on the card.
SQL: WITH first_set AS (SELECT s.code, s.name, s.releasedate FROM sets AS s WHERE s.code IN (SELECT c.setcode FROM cards AS c WHERE c.name = 'Abyssal Horror') ORDER BY s.releasedate ASC NULLS FIRST, s.code ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1), latest_set AS (SELECT s.code, s.name, s.releasedate FROM sets AS s ORDER BY s.releasedate DESC NULLS LAST, s.code ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1), chosen AS (SELECT code, name, releasedate FROM first_set UNION ALL SELECT code, name, releasedate FROM latest_set) SELECT ch.name AS set_name, ROUND(CAST(CASE WHEN (SUM(CASE WHEN NOT c.manacost IS NULL AND c.manacost <> '' AND c.convertedmanacost <= 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(CASE WHEN NOT c.manacost IS NULL AND c.manacost <> '' AND c.convertedmanacost <= 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END * 100.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(c.id), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS pct FROM chosen AS ch JOIN cards AS c ON c.setcode = ch.code GROUP BY ch.code, ch.name, ch.releasedate ORDER BY ch.releasedate ASC NULLS FIRST

question: How many different cards have ever been printed as a release promotion? I just need a single number, covering all printings across the game's entire history with no time restriction. Note that a prerelease printing is a different promotion type and shouldn't be counted as a release promotion.
evidence: A release promotion is a promotional printing whose promotion type is 'release'.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT name) AS release_promo_cards FROM cards WHERE CAST(REPLACE(promotypes, 'prerelease', '') AS TEXT) LIKE '%release%'

question: I'm cataloguing the Abzan clan's cards and need this: among the cards with the Abzan watermark, which one comes last in its set's numbering - i.e. has the highest collector number? Please give me the card's name, its collector number, and how many foreign-language printings exist for that card. If several Abzan-watermarked cards tie for the highest collector number, list every one of them, each with its own count of foreign-language printings. Count each foreign-language edition record of the card as one printing.
evidence: Abzan watermark: the clan mark printed on the card. Collector number: the number of the card within the set it was printed in. Foreign-language printing: the foreign-language edition record of a card.
SQL: SELECT c.name AS card_name, c.number AS collector_number, COUNT(f.id) AS foreign_printings FROM cards AS c LEFT JOIN foreign_data AS f ON f.uuid = c.uuid WHERE c.watermark = 'abzan' AND CASE WHEN (c.number) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((c.number) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END = (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN (number) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((number) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END) FROM cards WHERE watermark = 'abzan') GROUP BY c.uuid, c.name, c.number ORDER BY c.name NULLS FIRST

question: I'm profiling the weak end of the white-bordered printings. How many white-bordered cards have a power less than 3? I just need that single count - only white-bordered cards are in scope, and please don't include anything else in the answer.
evidence: Power is a card's combat strength. A card whose power is shown as * has no known power.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS weak_attackers FROM cards WHERE bordercolor = 'white' AND NOT power IS NULL AND power <> '*' AND power = CAST(CASE WHEN (power) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((power) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END AS TEXT) AND CASE WHEN (power) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((power) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END < 3

question: I'm putting together a showcase of instant-speed cards from Magic: The Gathering. Which cards in the Dark Ascension set have the Flash keyword and, among those, the highest converted mana cost? Please list just the card names, one row per card, alphabetically by name, and include every card that ties on that highest cost.
evidence: Dark Ascension is the Magic: The Gathering set named 'Dark Ascension'. Flash is the keyword that lets a card be cast any time you could cast an instant. Converted mana cost is the total amount of mana a card costs to cast.
SQL: SELECT t1.name FROM cards AS t1 INNER JOIN sets AS t2 ON t2.code = t1.setcode WHERE t2.name = 'Dark Ascension' AND POSITION(',' || 'Flash' || ',' IN ',' || t1.keywords || ',') > 0 AND t1.convertedmanacost = (SELECT MAX(t3.convertedmanacost) FROM cards AS t3 INNER JOIN sets AS t4 ON t4.code = t3.setcode WHERE t4.name = 'Dark Ascension' AND POSITION(',' || 'Flash' || ',' IN ',' || t3.keywords || ',') > 0) ORDER BY t1.name ASC NULLS FIRST

question: I'm preparing localized set icon assets and need to know the foreign-language name coverage of every Magic: The Gathering set released in 2020. For each set released in 2020 (meaning its release date falls within the calendar year 2020), please give me the set's name, its keyrune code, and the number of languages in which the set has an official translated name. Nothing else.
evidence: keyrune code: the code for the set's image icon; official translated name: the set's name rendered in a foreign language by the game's publisher.
SQL: SELECT s.name, s.keyrunecode, COUNT(DISTINCT st.language) AS translated_languages FROM sets AS s LEFT JOIN set_translations AS st ON st.setcode = s.code AND NOT st.translation IS NULL WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(s.releasedate AS TIMESTAMP)) = '2020' GROUP BY s.id, s.name, s.keyrunecode ORDER BY s.name NULLS FIRST

question: I'm sizing a catalogue page of 2017 sets that were localized for international markets. How many cards were there in total across the Magic: The Gathering sets released in 2017 (between January 1 and December 31, 2017) that have a name in a language other than English? A set counts as localized if its name has a foreign-language translation. Include every card in each qualifying set, counting promotional and related supplemental printings as part of the set. I just need the single total across all qualifying sets, not per-set numbers.
evidence: A foreign-language translation is a set's name rendered in a language other than English (e.g. Chinese Simplified, German, Spanish).
SQL: SELECT SUM(s.totalsetsize) AS total_cards FROM sets AS s WHERE s.releasedate BETWEEN '2017-01-01' AND '2017-12-31' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM set_translations AS t WHERE t.setcode = s.code)

question: I've already looked at the heavy hitters in duel deck B (the 'b' deck). Now I want to check the light end: how many cards in duel deck B are not available in foil and have attack power below 3? Note that 'below 3' means strictly below 3 — a power of exactly 3 doesn't count.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS card_count FROM cards WHERE dueldeck = 'b' AND hasfoil = 0 AND NOT power IS NULL AND power = TRIM(CAST(CASE WHEN (power) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((power) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END AS TEXT)) AND CASE WHEN (power) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((power) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END < 3

question: I'm writing a spotlight piece on card artists, and I need to know: among black-bordered cards that are obtainable on Magic Arena and have a printed power of 10 or greater, which artist illustrated the most of them? Please give me the artist's name and the number of those cards they illustrated. A card counts even if it's also available outside Arena, as long as it can be obtained on Arena. If several artists tie for the most, list every one of them along with that count.
evidence: Black border means the card's border color is black; power is the combat strength printed on a creature card, and '10 or greater' means the printed power reads as a number that is at least 10 (10, 11, 12, and so on).
SQL: WITH counts AS (SELECT artist, COUNT(*) AS card_count FROM cards WHERE bordercolor = 'black' AND CAST(LOWER(availability) AS TEXT) LIKE '%arena%' AND CASE WHEN (power) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((power) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END >= 10 GROUP BY artist) SELECT artist, card_count FROM counts WHERE card_count = (SELECT MAX(card_count) FROM counts)

question: I'm going through my paper collection before sharing it publicly, and I want to check something about the cards Wizards of the Coast has flagged. How many different cards are there that carry a sensitive content warning, are available in paper form, and have never been available on Magic Online (MTGO)? I just need that one count.
