evidence: MTGO means Magic: The Gathering Online, the official online version of the game. A sensitive content warning means Wizards of the Coast has marked the card for having sensitive content.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS card_count FROM (SELECT name FROM cards WHERE hascontentwarning = 1 GROUP BY name HAVING MAX(CASE WHEN CAST(availability AS TEXT) LIKE '%paper%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1 AND MAX(CASE WHEN CAST(availability AS TEXT) LIKE '%mtgo%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0) AS __photo_derived_1

question: Hi! I'm preparing a licensing brief for our Japanese partner about Magic: The Gathering localization coverage. Could you pull a report of every expansion type (core, expansion, promo, etc.), showing for each one how many sets of that type carry a Japanese name entry? A Japanese name entry means the set's name-translations include a Japanese-language entry giving the set's name in Japanese. Please include every expansion type in the report even if none of its sets have such an entry (show 0 for those), and sort the results alphabetically by expansion type. Nothing else needed - just the expansion type and the count.
evidence: Japanese name entry: an entry in the set's name-translations whose language is Japanese and which gives the set's name in Japanese.
SQL: SELECT s.type AS expansion_type, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN st.language = 'Japanese' AND NOT st.translation IS NULL AND TRIM(CAST(st.translation AS TEXT)) <> '' THEN s.code END) AS japanese_named_sets FROM sets AS s LEFT JOIN set_translations AS st ON st.setcode = s.code GROUP BY s.type ORDER BY s.type NULLS FIRST

question: I'm cataloguing Arena-exclusive illustrated art of big creatures. How many artists have illustrated at least one black-bordered card that is available on Arena but never on Magic Online and has a fixed printed power of at least 5? I want just the number of artists, nothing else. Count across all printings in the collection with no time restriction. Note that a card whose power varies is not a fixed number, so it shouldn't count as power 5 or more.
evidence: Arena and Magic Online are online platforms; a card's availability lists every platform it can be played on: 'arena' is Arena and 'mtgo' is Magic Online. Power is the attack strength printed on a creature card. Black-bordered refers to the standard card border color black.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT artist) AS artists FROM cards WHERE bordercolor = 'black' AND CAST(availability AS TEXT) LIKE '%arena%' AND CAST(availability AS TEXT) NOT LIKE '%mtgo%' AND CASE WHEN (power) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((power) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END >= 5

question: I collect trading cards, and one of my favorites is Ancestor's Chosen. Of all the sets that include this card, look at the one released most recently - if several sets share that latest release date, consider them together. How many creature cards in that set (or sets) have power greater than toughness? I just want that single count, nothing else.
evidence: Power is the attack strength printed on a creature card; toughness is the defense strength printed on a creature card.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS power_over_toughness FROM cards WHERE CAST(types AS TEXT) LIKE '%Creature%' AND CASE WHEN (power) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((power) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END > CASE WHEN (toughness) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((toughness) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END AND setcode IN (SELECT c2.setcode FROM cards AS c2 JOIN sets AS s2 ON s2.code = c2.setcode WHERE c2.name = 'Ancestor''s Chosen' AND s2.releasedate = (SELECT MAX(s3.releasedate) FROM sets AS s3 JOIN cards AS c3 ON c3.setcode = s3.code WHERE c3.name = 'Ancestor''s Chosen'))

question: Among the Commander-leadable cards that the Card Kingdom catalog lists for both a foil printing and a regular non-foil printing – cards listed for only one of the two printings don't count – I want the single most recent card frame year (the latest calendar year among the frame versions), and the count of cards in that group whose frame version is that year. Please return just that one row: the frame year and its card count.
evidence: A card 'may lead a Commander deck' if it can be the deck's commander – the one card that leads the deck and sets its color identity – not merely be included among the deck's other cards.
SQL: WITH cmd AS (SELECT frameversion, SUBSTRING(CAST(leadershipskills AS TEXT) FROM POSITION('commander' IN leadershipskills)) AS tail FROM cards WHERE NOT cardkingdomid IS NULL AND NOT cardkingdomfoilid IS NULL) SELECT frameversion AS frame_year, COUNT(*) AS card_count FROM cmd WHERE CASE WHEN (LENGTH(CAST('True' AS TEXT))) >= 0 THEN SUBSTRING(CAST(tail AS TEXT) FROM LENGTH(CAST('commander' AS TEXT)) + LENGTH(CAST('True' AS TEXT)) FOR LENGTH(CAST('True' AS TEXT))) ELSE SUBSTRING(CAST(tail AS TEXT) FROM GREATEST(1, (LENGTH(CAST('commander' AS TEXT)) + LENGTH(CAST('True' AS TEXT))) + (LENGTH(CAST('True' AS TEXT)))) FOR LEAST(-(LENGTH(CAST('True' AS TEXT))), (LENGTH(CAST('commander' AS TEXT)) + LENGTH(CAST('True' AS TEXT))) - 1)) END = 'True' GROUP BY frameversion ORDER BY CASE WHEN (frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1

question: I'm compiling the official rulings archive for the Magic: The Gathering card Fireball. How many official rulings have ever been issued for Fireball? I need the total across all time, with no date restriction.
evidence: A ruling is an official clarification issued by Wizards of the Coast about how a card works.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS ruling_count FROM (SELECT DISTINCT r.date, r.text FROM rulings AS r INNER JOIN cards AS c ON r.uuid = c.uuid WHERE c.name = 'Fireball') AS __photo_derived_1

question: Which card whose original type is 'Creature - Elf' has received the most rulings, and how many rulings has it received? I want the card name and the number of rulings. A card and all of its printings/reprints count as one and the same card. If several cards tie for the most rulings, list every one of them.
evidence: A ruling is an official rules clarification issued for a card, on the date it was issued.
SQL: WITH elf_cards AS (SELECT DISTINCT name FROM cards WHERE originaltype = 'Creature - Elf'), elf_rulings AS (SELECT c.name, r.date, r.text FROM cards AS c JOIN rulings AS r ON c.uuid = r.uuid WHERE c.name IN (SELECT name FROM elf_cards) GROUP BY c.name, r.date, r.text), counts AS (SELECT name, COUNT(*) AS ruling_count FROM elf_rulings GROUP BY name) SELECT name, ruling_count FROM counts WHERE ruling_count = (SELECT MAX(ruling_count) FROM counts) ORDER BY name NULLS FIRST

question: I'm reviewing the very first cards in the database and want to compare how widely accepted white cards are versus black cards across play formats. For each card color that appears among the cards with ID 1 through 20, please tell me the card color and the number of play formats in which cards of that color are legal. A card only counts as legal in a format if its legality status for that format is 'Legal' - banned or restricted doesn't count.
evidence: Formats of play: the game formats a card is permitted in, such as commander or vintage.
SQL: SELECT t1.colors AS color, COUNT(DISTINCT t2.format) AS format_count FROM cards AS t1 INNER JOIN legalities AS t2 ON t1.uuid = t2.uuid WHERE t1.id BETWEEN 1 AND 20 AND t2.status = 'Legal' GROUP BY t1.colors ORDER BY t1.colors NULLS FIRST

question: I'm tracking John Avon's artwork. Among his cards that exist as powerful foils, what is the most recent frame year, and how many of those cards carry it? If several years are tied for most recent, give each year with its own count. Match John Avon on the illustrator's name.
evidence: powerful foil: a card whose Card Kingdom identifiers are both present – the regular identifier and the foil identifier.
SQL: SELECT frameversion AS frame_year, COUNT(id) AS card_count FROM cards WHERE artist = 'John Avon' AND NOT cardkingdomid IS NULL AND NOT cardkingdomfoilid IS NULL GROUP BY frameversion HAVING CASE WHEN (frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END = (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN (frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END) FROM cards WHERE artist = 'John Avon' AND NOT cardkingdomid IS NULL AND NOT cardkingdomfoilid IS NULL)

question: I play paper Magic and I'm building a pauper deck. How many printings of cards illustrated by Erica Yang are legal in the pauper format and exist as paper (physically printed) cards? I want just a single count of printings, with each printing counted separately.
evidence: Pauper is a Magic: The Gathering format where only common-rarity cards are legal; a printing is a specific physical or digital release of a card in a set; 'legal in pauper' means the card's pauper legality status is Legal; 'paper' means a physical printed card.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS paper_pauper_printings FROM cards AS c INNER JOIN legalities AS l ON c.uuid = l.uuid WHERE c.artist = 'Erica Yang' AND l.format = 'pauper' AND l.status = 'Legal' AND CAST(c.availability AS TEXT) LIKE '%paper%'

question: I keep a Card Kingdom catalogue and want to list the creature cards that Card Kingdom stocks in both foil and non-foil printings. A card counts as stocked in both printings when both its Card Kingdom Foil id and its Card Kingdom id are present. Please give me one row per card, with each card's Card Kingdom Foil id and Card Kingdom id, and nothing else. I only need the three cards with the lowest Card Kingdom Foil ids in alphabetical order, with ties broken by the Card Kingdom id.
evidence: Card Kingdom Foil id: the retailer's identifier for the foil printing; Card Kingdom id: the retailer's identifier for the non-foil printing.
SQL: SELECT cardkingdomfoilid, cardkingdomid FROM cards WHERE NOT cardkingdomfoilid IS NULL AND NOT cardkingdomid IS NULL AND CAST(types AS TEXT) LIKE '%Creature%' ORDER BY cardkingdomfoilid NULLS FIRST, cardkingdomid NULLS FIRST LIMIT 3

question: Among the cards carrying the boros watermark that were printed in a foreign language, which card type is the most common, and how many of those cards have that type? If several types tie for the most, list all of them with their counts.
evidence: "Boros watermark" refers to the guild watermark appearing on cards of the Boros guild; "printed in a foreign language" means the card was printed in any language other than English.
SQL: WITH counted AS (SELECT t1.type AS card_type, COUNT(DISTINCT t1.uuid) AS card_count FROM cards AS t1 INNER JOIN foreign_data AS t2 ON t1.uuid = t2.uuid WHERE t1.watermark = 'boros' GROUP BY t1.type) SELECT card_type, card_count FROM counted WHERE card_count = (SELECT MAX(card_count) FROM counted) ORDER BY card_type NULLS FIRST

question: Among the Magic: The Gathering cards whose watermark is one of the ten Ravnica guild symbols (Azorius, Boros, Dimir, Golgari, Gruul, Izzet, Orzhov, Rakdos, Selesnya, Simic), which guild has the most cards that were printed in another language, and how many of that guild's cards is that? If several guilds tie for the most, give me each tied guild along with the number.
evidence: A Ravnica guild is the guild a card's watermark belongs to; a card 'printed in another language' is a card that exists in a language edition other than English.
SQL: WITH counted AS (SELECT c.watermark AS guild, COUNT(DISTINCT c.uuid) AS number_of_cards FROM cards AS c INNER JOIN foreign_data AS f ON f.uuid = c.uuid WHERE c.watermark IN ('azorius', 'boros', 'dimir', 'golgari', 'gruul', 'izzet', 'orzhov', 'rakdos', 'selesnya', 'simic') GROUP BY c.watermark) SELECT guild, number_of_cards FROM counted WHERE number_of_cards = (SELECT MAX(number_of_cards) FROM counted) ORDER BY guild NULLS FIRST

question: I'm cataloguing the guild cards. Among the cards that carry the Azorius watermark and were printed in at least one foreign language, how many cards are there of each card type? For each card type, please give me the card type exactly as printed, including any supertypes and subtypes, along with the number of cards of that type. List every card type that qualifies, sorted from the largest count to the smallest, and alphabetically by card type when counts are equal.
SQL: SELECT c.type, COUNT(DISTINCT c.uuid) AS number_of_cards FROM cards AS c INNER JOIN foreign_data AS f ON f.uuid = c.uuid WHERE c.watermark = 'azorius' GROUP BY c.type ORDER BY number_of_cards DESC NULLS LAST, c.type ASC NULLS FIRST

question: I'm cataloguing modern-frame printings. How many different cards that have a text box were printed with a frame version of 2015 or a later year? I just need that single count.
evidence: Frame version: the version of the card frame style, given as the year the frame style was introduced.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT name) AS number_of_cards FROM cards WHERE istextless = 0 AND CASE WHEN (frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END >= 2015

question: I'm putting together a showcase of promotional cards and need a list of card names. I want the names of the cards that have a promotional printing and have multiple faces on the same card, but only those printed in the most recent card frame version. A card's frame version is the year its frame style was introduced, so the most recent frame version is the one with the latest year - and it should be the newest frame style overall, not just among promotional multi-faced cards. Please list each card's name once.
evidence: A promotional printing is a printing of a card that was given out for promotional purposes. A card with multiple faces has multiple faces printed on the same card.
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT name FROM cards WHERE ispromo = 1 AND NOT side IS NULL AND CASE WHEN (frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END = (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN (frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END) FROM cards)

question: I'm putting together a retrospective of promotional cards. Can you get me the card name of every promotional card that has multiple faces printed on it (like split, transform, or adventure cards) and was originally released in 2019? By "originally released" I mean the card's own first-release date, not the release date of the set its promotional printing belongs to, and "in 2019" means January 1 through December 31, 2019. If a card has more than one promotional printing from that year, list it just once. I only want the card names, nothing else.
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT name FROM cards WHERE ispromo = 1 AND NOT side IS NULL AND SUBSTRING(CAST(originalreleasedate AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) = '2019'

question: I'm researching printings of the Magic: The Gathering card Tarmogoyf. I want to identify every reprint of Tarmogoyf that was published in a card frame style that was already at least 10 full years old when the set came out. Please give me the set name and release date of every set that qualifies, not just one. Two rules: the frame version is the year that frame style dates from (the frame style itself, not any frame artwork effects), and 'at least 10 full years' is inclusive, measured between the frame version's year and the set's release year.
evidence: Frame version: the year the card frame style of a printing dates from.
SQL: SELECT s.name AS set_name, s.releasedate AS release_date FROM cards AS c INNER JOIN sets AS s ON s.code = c.setcode WHERE c.name = 'Tarmogoyf' AND c.frameversion ~ '^[0-9]+$' AND CASE WHEN (c.frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((c.frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END = CASE WHEN (c.frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((c.frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END AND CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(s.releasedate AS TIMESTAMP))) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(s.releasedate AS TIMESTAMP))) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END - CASE WHEN (c.frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((c.frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END >= 10

question: I'm cataloguing European releases of Counterspell. How many of its printings were released with both a French and an Italian localization? I just need the count as a single number.
evidence: A printing is one release of the card identified by its set and its card number in that set; 'Counterspell' is the English card name as catalogued.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.id) FROM cards AS c JOIN foreign_data AS f ON c.uuid = f.uuid WHERE c.name = 'Counterspell' AND f.language IN ('French', 'Italian') AND c.id IN (SELECT c2.id FROM cards AS c2 JOIN foreign_data AS f2 ON c2.uuid = f2.uuid WHERE c2.name = 'Counterspell' AND f2.language = 'French' INTERSECT SELECT c3.id FROM cards AS c3 JOIN foreign_data AS f3 ON c3.uuid = f3.uuid WHERE c3.name = 'Counterspell' AND f3.language = 'Italian')

question: I'm putting together a localization report. Find the sets that belong to the same expansion type as "From the Vault: Lore" – include that set itself if it qualifies. Among those, which sets never received a name in any foreign language? For each one, give me the set's name and its release date. List each qualifying set once, from the earliest release date to the latest. Don't include anything else.
evidence: Expansion type means the category a set belongs to, such as core, expansion or masters.
SQL: SELECT s.name, s.releasedate FROM sets AS s WHERE s.type = (SELECT type FROM sets WHERE name = 'From the Vault: Lore') AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM set_translations AS t WHERE t.setcode = s.code AND NOT t.translation IS NULL) ORDER BY s.releasedate NULLS FIRST

question: Which set contains the Aven Mindcensor printing that uses the newest card frame? I want the set's name and its release date. Count every printing, including promotional and online-only ones. If several printings share the newest frame, use the most recently released one; if the release dates tie too, list each such set once. Please give me the set name, not its code.
evidence: Frame version: the frame style used for a printing; frame styles are identified by the year that style was introduced.
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT s.name AS setname, s.releasedate FROM cards AS c JOIN sets AS s ON s.code = c.setcode WHERE c.name = 'Aven Mindcensor' AND CASE WHEN (c.frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((c.frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END = (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN (frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END) FROM cards WHERE name = 'Aven Mindcensor') AND s.releasedate = (SELECT MAX(s2.releasedate) FROM cards AS c2 JOIN sets AS s2 ON s2.code = c2.setcode WHERE c2.name = 'Aven Mindcensor' AND CASE WHEN (c2.frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((c2.frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END = (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN (frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END) FROM cards WHERE name = 'Aven Mindcensor'))

question: I'm auditing which recent products were never localized for Spanish-speaking markets. Can you find every set released in calendar year 2020 that has no Spanish name? For each of those, I just need the set code and the set's release date.
evidence: By "Spanish name" I mean the Spanish-language version of a set's name.
SQL: SELECT s.code, s.releasedate FROM sets AS s WHERE s.releasedate BETWEEN '2020-01-01' AND '2020-12-31' AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM set_translations AS t WHERE t.setcode = s.code AND t.language = 'Spanish' AND NOT t.translation IS NULL) ORDER BY s.releasedate NULLS FIRST, s.code NULLS FIRST

question: I'm cataloguing special-release printings illustrated by Rob Alexander. What is the total converted mana cost across all cards illustrated by Rob Alexander whose original release falls in 2013? Please give me just that total as a single number. By 'released in 2013' I mean the calendar year from 1 January through 31 December 2013, and a card's original release is the original release date recorded on the card itself—cards with no original release date recorded are out of scope. Each card printing counts separately in the total.
evidence: Converted mana cost: the total numeric mana value of a card, e.g. a card costing {4}{W}{W} has a converted mana cost of 6.
SQL: SELECT SUM(convertedmanacost) AS total_converted_mana_cost FROM cards WHERE artist = 'Rob Alexander' AND SUBSTRING(CAST(originalreleasedate AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) = '2013'

question: We're planning translation work for upcoming set releases and want to know how extensively a recent release year was localized. What was the average number of languages in which sets released in 2016 had their names translated? By 'released in 2016' I mean the release date falls within calendar year 2016. Every set released in 2016 counts toward the average, including any whose names were translated into no language at all (those count as zero). A language counts for a set when the set's name is rendered in that language. Please give me just that one number, rounded to two decimals.
evidence: Set name translation: the set's name rendered in another language.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(n) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_languages FROM (SELECT s.id, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN NOT st.translation IS NULL AND TRIM(CAST(st.translation AS TEXT)) <> '' THEN st.language END) AS n FROM sets AS s LEFT JOIN set_translations AS st ON s.code = st.setcode WHERE SUBSTRING(CAST(s.releasedate AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) = '2016' GROUP BY s.id) AS __photo_derived_1

question: For the blocks named exactly "Masques" and "Mirage", how widely were their sets localized? For each of these two blocks, give me one row with the block's name, how many of its sets have an official translated name, and the total number of cards in the base sets of those sets combined. Base set size means the number of cards in the set's base set, not counting supplementary cards. Nothing else, please.
SQL: SELECT s.block AS block, COUNT(DISTINCT s.code) AS translated_sets, SUM(s.basesetsize) AS total_base_set_size FROM sets AS s JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT setcode FROM set_translations) AS st ON s.code = st.setcode WHERE s.block IN ('Masques', 'Mirage') GROUP BY s.block ORDER BY s.block NULLS FIRST

question: I'm assembling a Japanese-language boros deck and want to check which cards need careful rules review. For every card that has a boros watermark and a Japanese printing, please give me: the Japanese card name, the English card type, and the total number of official rulings recorded for that card. A card is identified by its Japanese name together with its English card type - printings that share both count as one card, and if either differs they should be listed as separate cards. The ruling total should add up all ruling entries across every printing of that card, and if a card has no rulings, list it with a total of 0.
evidence: Boros watermark means the watermark is marked 'boros' on the card; a Japanese printing is the foreign data entry in Japanese; rulings are the official rules clarifications recorded for a card.
SQL: SELECT f.name AS japanese_card_name, c.type AS card_type, SUM((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM rulings AS r WHERE r.uuid = c.uuid)) AS ruling_count FROM cards AS c JOIN foreign_data AS f ON c.uuid = f.uuid WHERE c.watermark = 'boros' AND f.language = 'Japanese' GROUP BY f.name, c.type ORDER BY f.name COLLATE "C" NULLS FIRST, c.type COLLATE "C" NULLS FIRST

question: I'm putting together a localization coverage report. Among the languages into which the card sets themselves were translated (i.e., have a set translation), which language has the fewest printings whose flavor text was translated into that language? Please give me the language name and the number of such printings. If several languages tie for the fewest, list all of them, ordered alphabetically by language name.
evidence: Set translation: a card set's official release in another language.
SQL: WITH set_langs AS (SELECT DISTINCT language FROM set_translations), counts AS (SELECT fd.language, COUNT(*) AS printings FROM foreign_data AS fd WHERE fd.language IN (SELECT language FROM set_langs) AND NOT fd.flavortext IS NULL AND fd.flavortext <> '' GROUP BY fd.language) SELECT language, printings FROM counts WHERE printings = (SELECT MIN(printings) FROM counts) ORDER BY language ASC NULLS FIRST

question: I'm building a French-language cube and want some big finishers for it. How many different creature cards with power 10 or greater have at least one printing in a set whose name has a French translation? Please return just that single number. Note: a set qualifies based on its name having a French translation, no matter when it was released or what type of set it is, and a card counts if any of its printings comes from such a set.
evidence: French translation: the set's name as given in French.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT name) AS total_creature_cards FROM cards WHERE CASE WHEN (power) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((power) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END >= 10 AND CAST(types AS TEXT) LIKE '%Creature%' AND setcode IN (SELECT setcode FROM set_translations WHERE language = 'French' AND NOT translation IS NULL)

question: I'm researching the Commander banned list. Can you tell me the average mana value of the creature cards that are banned in at least one play format, considering only cards ranked in EDHRec's top 1000 most popular (ranks 1 through 1000, where rank 1 is the most popular)? Give me the average as a single number rounded to one decimal place. Keep in mind that a card printed in several sets is still just one card with one EDHRec rank and one mana value.
evidence: EDHRec rank: a card's popularity rank on EDHRec, from 1 (most popular) to 1000.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(t.cmc) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS average_mana_value FROM (SELECT c.name, c.convertedmanacost AS cmc FROM cards AS c INNER JOIN legalities AS l ON l.uuid = c.uuid WHERE POSITION('Creature' IN c.types) > 0 AND c.edhrecrank BETWEEN 1 AND 1000 AND l.status = 'Banned' GROUP BY c.name, c.convertedmanacost) AS t

question: For a stats segment on creature power creep, I want to size the middle-to-big power band: how many card printings have a power greater than 3 and at most 10? Note that 3 itself is out (strictly greater than 3), but 10 itself counts (at most 10). Just the total number of printings, please.
evidence: A printing is one printed appearance of a card in a set – the same card name appearing in different sets counts as several printings.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards WHERE CASE WHEN (power) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((power) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END > 3 AND CASE WHEN (power) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((power) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END <= 10

question: I want a single number: how many card printings originally released in 2014 belong to a set that carries a Magic: The Gathering Online code. A set counts as MTGO-available only if its MTGO code is present for that set. By 2014 I mean the calendar year 2014 of the printing's original release date. Count each printing separately, even if the same card name appears in more than one set.
evidence: Magic: The Gathering Online (MTGO) is the official digital edition of the game; a set's MTGO code identifies that set within MTGO.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS printings FROM cards AS c JOIN sets AS s ON s.code = c.setcode WHERE SUBSTRING(CAST(c.originalreleasedate AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) = '2014' AND NOT s.mtgocode IS NULL

question: I'm looking at Magic: The Gathering's localization coverage. Which foreign printing language has the fewest card printings overall, and how many printings does it have? Please count only languages in which Magic sets were officially printed—exclude one-off promotional gimmick languages. If several languages tie for the fewest, list each of them with the count.
evidence: A printing language is a language in which Magic: The Gathering sets were officially released.
SQL: WITH counts AS (SELECT f.language, COUNT(*) AS printings FROM foreign_data AS f WHERE f.language IN (SELECT DISTINCT language FROM set_translations) GROUP BY f.language) SELECT language, printings FROM counts WHERE printings = (SELECT MIN(printings) FROM counts)

question: I'm auditing how thoroughly the Coldsnap expansion was localized into Italian. How many printings in the Coldsnap set have Italian rules text? I just need that single count.
evidence: By 'printing' I mean an individual card entry of a set, and by 'Italian rules text' I mean the Italian-language rules wording recorded for that printing. Coldsnap means the set named Coldsnap.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.uuid) AS printings_with_italian_rules_text FROM foreign_data AS f JOIN cards AS c ON c.uuid = f.uuid JOIN sets AS s ON s.code = c.setcode WHERE s.name = 'Coldsnap' AND f.language = 'Italian' AND TRIM(CAST(f.text AS TEXT)) <> ''

question: Among the Commander-type expansion sets released in calendar year 2020 (1 January 2020 to 31 December 2020), I need the one with the highest total card count, so we can plan translation work. Please send me the set's id from the sets listing, its name, and the number of official languages it was released in. The total card count should include promotional and related supplemental products, but exclude Alchemy modifications. If two sets tie for the highest total card count, list each of them, ordered by set id ascending.
evidence: Commander: a multiplayer expansion type of the game. Alchemy modifications: online-only variant versions of cards.
SQL: WITH cohort AS (SELECT * FROM sets WHERE type = 'commander' AND releasedate >= '2020-01-01' AND releasedate <= '2020-12-31') SELECT c.id, c.name, COUNT(DISTINCT st.language) AS languages FROM cohort AS c LEFT JOIN set_translations AS st ON st.setcode = c.code WHERE c.totalsetsize = (SELECT MAX(totalsetsize) FROM cohort) GROUP BY c.id, c.name ORDER BY c.id ASC NULLS FIRST

question: I'm researching Magic: The Gathering's basic land card Swamp. How many foreign languages has it been printed in over its entire history? Count all printings across every set and year.
evidence: Swamp is the name of a Magic: The Gathering card.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT fd.language) AS language_count FROM foreign_data AS fd JOIN cards AS c ON fd.uuid = c.uuid WHERE c.name = 'Swamp'

question: I'm putting together a black artifact flavor-showcase section for a trade binder. How many mono-black Artifact cards have a foreign-language printing that shows flavor text in that language? By mono-black I mean black is the card's only colour, and by Artifact cards I include artifacts combined with another card type, like an Artifact Creature. I'm counting cards, not printings – a card is the same card regardless of set, print run, or language. Just give me one number.
evidence: In Magic colour notation, B denotes black, and a card is mono-black when black is its only colour.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.name) AS card_count FROM cards AS c WHERE c.colors = 'B' AND CAST(c.type AS TEXT) LIKE '%Artifact%' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM foreign_data AS f WHERE f.uuid = c.uuid AND LENGTH(CAST(f.flavortext AS TEXT)) > 0)

question: What is the display name of the user who last edited the post "Examples for teaching: Correlation does not mean causation"?
SQL: SELECT t2.displayname FROM posts AS t1 INNER JOIN users AS t2 ON t1.lasteditoruserid = t2.id WHERE t1.title = 'Examples for teaching: Correlation does not mean causation'

question: Which users made exactly one history entry on at least one post with at least 1,000 views? Return their distinct user IDs.
SQL: WITH once_per_post AS (SELECT h.postid, h.userid FROM posthistory AS h JOIN posts AS p ON p.id = h.postid WHERE p.viewcount >= 1000 AND NOT h.userid IS NULL GROUP BY h.postid, h.userid HAVING COUNT(*) = 1) SELECT DISTINCT userid FROM once_per_post ORDER BY userid NULLS FIRST

question: What is the difference in percentage points between the 2010 and 2011 shares of all Student badges, taking the 2010 share minus the 2011 share?
SQL: SELECT CASE WHEN (SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(date AS TIMESTAMP)) = '2010' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(date AS TIMESTAMP)) = '2010' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(id), 0) - CASE WHEN (SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(date AS TIMESTAMP)) = '2011' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(date AS TIMESTAMP)) = '2011' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(id), 0) FROM badges WHERE name = 'Student'

question: What percentage of posts authored by Community use the R-language tag? Round to two decimals.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN CAST(p.tags AS TEXT) LIKE '%<r>%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) FROM posts AS p JOIN users AS u ON u.id = p.owneruserid WHERE u.displayname = 'Community'

question: Which post created in 2010 had the most favorites? Return its post ID and its owner's display name.
SQL: SELECT p.id, u.displayname FROM posts AS p JOIN users AS u ON p.owneruserid = u.id WHERE SUBSTRING(CAST(p.creaiondate AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) = '2010' AND NOT p.favoritecount IS NULL ORDER BY p.favoritecount DESC NULLS LAST, p.id ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1

question: Give the view count of the post titled 'Computer game datasets' and the display name of its last editor.
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT p.viewcount, u.displayname FROM posts AS p JOIN users AS u ON u.id = p.lasteditoruserid WHERE LOWER(p.title) = LOWER('Computer game datasets')

question: Give the text and author's display name for the latest ten comments on the post titled 'Analysing wind data with R', newest comment first.
SQL: SELECT c.text, u.displayname FROM comments AS c JOIN posts AS p ON c.postid = p.id LEFT JOIN users AS u ON c.userid = u.id WHERE p.title = 'Analysing wind data with R' ORDER BY c.creationdate DESC NULLS LAST, c.id DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

question: Among all posts by the user with the highest reputation, what percentage have a score above 50? Round to two decimal places.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN score > 50 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) FROM posts WHERE owneruserid IN (SELECT id FROM users WHERE reputation = (SELECT MAX(reputation) FROM users))

question: Among comments attached to existing posts with exactly one comment record in the data, how many have a score of zero?
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM comments AS c JOIN posts AS p ON p.id = c.postid WHERE c.score = 0 AND c.postid IN (SELECT x.postid FROM comments AS x GROUP BY x.postid HAVING COUNT(*) = 1)

question: I'd like to gauge the standing of our United Kingdom contributor community on the site. Can you give me the combined reputation of the users based in the United Kingdom who have posted on the site, as a single total? Please write the country by its full name, "United Kingdom", and don't substitute abbreviations. I just need the one number, not a per-user list.
evidence: Reputation is the score the site assigns each user. A user who has posted owns at least one item in the site's post collection.
SQL: SELECT SUM(u.reputation) AS combined_reputation FROM users AS u WHERE CAST(u.location AS TEXT) LIKE '%United Kingdom%' AND u.id IN (SELECT p.owneruserid FROM posts AS p WHERE NOT p.owneruserid IS NULL)

question: I want to profile the users who drop links in comment threads. What is the average age of the users who posted a comment containing a website link? Please round it to two decimal places. That single value is all I need back.
evidence: A comment counts as containing a website if its content contains 'http://'.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(t.age) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS average_age FROM (SELECT DISTINCT t2.id, t2.age FROM comments AS t1 INNER JOIN users AS t2 ON t1.userid = t2.id WHERE CAST(t1.text AS TEXT) LIKE '%http://%') AS t

question: I'm profiling how seasoned our Organizer badge holders in Germany are. Among the users who earned the Organizer badge and are based in Germany, how many had already earned 5 badges before they got the Organizer badge? Just the count, please. Note: "before" means strictly earlier - badges earned at the same moment as the Organizer badge don't count toward the 5, and the Organizer badge itself doesn't count as one of the 5.
evidence: Organizer badge: the badge whose name is Organizer.
SQL: WITH organizer AS (SELECT userid, MIN(date) AS organizer_date FROM badges WHERE name = 'Organizer' GROUP BY userid) SELECT COUNT(*) AS user_count FROM organizer AS o JOIN users AS u ON u.id = o.userid WHERE CAST(u.location AS TEXT) LIKE '%Germany%' AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM badges AS b WHERE b.userid = o.userid AND b.date < o.organizer_date) >= 5

question: I'm putting together a report for the site owners on where people who started posting during 2010 were located, with a focus on India. Could you tell me how many of the users whose first post was created in 2010 are located in India? By 2010 I mean the calendar year 2010, and by India I mean the country itself, not any place whose name merely contains the word.
evidence: A user's first post is the earliest-created post among the posts that user owns.
SQL: WITH RECURSIVE fp AS (SELECT owneruserid AS uid, MIN(creaiondate) AS fdate FROM posts WHERE NOT owneruserid IS NULL GROUP BY owneruserid), locs AS (SELECT u.id AS uid, u.location AS loc FROM users AS u JOIN fp ON fp.uid = u.id WHERE fp.fdate >= '2010-01-01' AND fp.fdate < '2011-01-01'), parts(uid, head, tail) AS (SELECT uid, CASE WHEN POSITION(',' IN loc) > 0 THEN SUBSTRING(CAST(loc AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION(',' IN loc) - 1) ELSE loc END, CASE WHEN POSITION(',' IN loc) > 0 THEN SUBSTRING(CAST(loc AS TEXT) FROM POSITION(',' IN loc) + 1) ELSE NULL END FROM locs UNION ALL SELECT uid, CASE WHEN POSITION(',' IN tail) > 0 THEN SUBSTRING(CAST(tail AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION(',' IN tail) - 1) ELSE tail END, CASE WHEN POSITION(',' IN tail) > 0 THEN SUBSTRING(CAST(tail AS TEXT) FROM POSITION(',' IN tail) + 1) ELSE NULL END FROM parts WHERE NOT tail IS NULL) SELECT COUNT(*) AS users_in_india FROM parts WHERE TRIM(CAST(head AS TEXT)) = 'India'

question: I'm profiling the authors behind poorly received R posts to see if they tend to be low-reputation members. Can you give me the average reputation of the users who own posts tagged with the R tag that have a score below 20? Just the single number, rounded to the nearest whole number.
evidence: 'r' is the tag used on this site for the R programming language for statistical computing.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(AVG(u.reputation)) AS avg_reputation FROM users AS u WHERE u.id IN (SELECT p.owneruserid FROM posts AS p WHERE p.score < 20 AND CAST(p.tags AS TEXT) LIKE '%' || '<' || 'r' || '>' || '%')

question: I'm putting together the yearly activity report with a Germany-focused breakdown of who did the editing, covering posts created in calendar year 2012. For the 2012 posts whose last editor is a user based in Germany, I need the total score; and for all other posts created in 2012, I need their total score as well. Also, how many Germany-based users were the last editor of at least one 2012 post, and what their combined reputation is, as shown on their profiles. A user based in Germany is one whose profile location is in Germany.
evidence: A post's last editor is the user who made its most recent edit.
SQL: WITH posts_2012 AS (SELECT id, score, lasteditoruserid AS editorid FROM posts WHERE creaiondate >= '2012-01-01' AND creaiondate < '2013-01-01'), german_editors AS (SELECT DISTINCT u.id, u.reputation FROM posts_2012 AS p JOIN users AS u ON u.id = p.editorid WHERE CAST(u.location AS TEXT) LIKE '%Germany%') SELECT (SELECT SUM(p.score) FROM posts_2012 AS p JOIN german_editors AS g ON g.id = p.editorid) AS german_edited_score, (SELECT SUM(score) FROM posts_2012 WHERE editorid IS NULL OR NOT editorid IN (SELECT id FROM german_editors)) AS remaining_score, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM german_editors) AS editor_count, (SELECT SUM(reputation) FROM german_editors) AS editor_reputation

question: I'm reviewing R-language activity on the site. I'd like to gauge the standing of the community members behind the highly-rated R posts: what is the combined reputation of the users who own a post with a score of exactly 10 that carries the R programming language tag? Please return just that single number. Note that by R I mean the R programming language tag specifically, not any other tag or value that just happens to contain the letter r.
SQL: SELECT SUM(u.reputation) AS combined_reputation FROM users AS u WHERE u.id IN (SELECT p.owneruserid FROM posts AS p WHERE p.score = 10 AND CAST(p.tags AS TEXT) ILIKE '%' || '<' || 'R' || '>' || '%')

question: I'd like to gauge the standing of the community members behind the R posts on one day. Could you tell me the combined reputation of the users who own the posts tagged R that were last active on 2014-08-27? I just need that one number, covering the whole calendar day 2014-08-27.
evidence: R: the R language for statistical computing.
SQL: SELECT SUM(reputation) AS combined_reputation FROM users WHERE id IN (SELECT owneruserid FROM posts WHERE CAST(tags AS TEXT) ILIKE '%' || '<' || 'R' || '>' || '%' AND CAST(lasactivitydate AS TEXT) LIKE '2014-08-27%')

question: What is the total score of the questions tagged 'r' that link to the question titled "A Probability distribution value exceeding 1 is OK?"? I only need the total score of those linking questions.
evidence: 'r' here means the R programming language for statistical computing, not the letter on its own.
SQL: WITH target AS (SELECT id FROM posts WHERE title = 'A Probability distribution value exceeding 1 is OK?'), linkers AS (SELECT DISTINCT pl.postid AS pid FROM postlinks AS pl INNER JOIN target AS tg ON pl.relatedpostid = tg.id) SELECT SUM(p.score) AS total_score FROM linkers AS l INNER JOIN posts AS p ON p.id = l.pid WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM tags AS t WHERE t.tagname = 'r' AND CAST(p.tags AS TEXT) LIKE '%' || '<' || t.tagname || '>' || '%')

question: I'm profiling users by where they say they live. Among the users located in Germany, who has the second most badges of all time? By second most I mean the highest badge total strictly below the top holder's total. If several users tie at that total, include all of them. Please give me each such user's display name and their badge total, ordered by display name.
evidence: Badges: the badges a user has obtained, one badge award per record.
SQL: WITH per_user AS (SELECT u.id, u.displayname, COUNT(b.id) AS badge_count FROM users AS u LEFT JOIN badges AS b ON b.userid = u.id WHERE CAST(u.location AS TEXT) LIKE '%Germany%' GROUP BY u.id, u.displayname) SELECT displayname, badge_count FROM per_user WHERE badge_count = (SELECT MAX(badge_count) FROM per_user AS p2 WHERE p2.badge_count < (SELECT MAX(badge_count) FROM per_user)) ORDER BY displayname NULLS FIRST

question: I'm planning regional outreach and want to know which California-based account draws the most profile attention. Among users whose stated location shows they are based in California, give me the user id, display name, profile view count, and reputation of the user or users with the most profile views. If several such users tie for the most profile views, list every one of them with those same four values.
evidence: CA is the two-letter state code for California.
SQL: WITH ca AS (SELECT id, displayname, views, reputation FROM users WHERE POSITION(',' || 'CA' || ',' IN ',' || REPLACE(UPPER(TRIM(CAST(location AS TEXT))), ' ', '') || ',') > 0 OR POSITION(',' || UPPER('California') || ',' IN ',' || REPLACE(UPPER(TRIM(CAST(location AS TEXT))), ' ', '') || ',') > 0) SELECT id, displayname, views, reputation FROM ca WHERE views = (SELECT MAX(views) FROM ca)

question: We're profiling our most respected members by where they live, focusing on York, England (the English city itself; a location listed as just "York" counts). Who is the most influential user based there – the one with the highest reputation – and what is their age? If several users tie for the highest reputation, give me the age of each of them. Please return only the age, exactly as it stands for each user, even when an age isn't reported.
SQL: SELECT age FROM users WHERE POSITION(',' || 'York' || ',' IN ',' || location || ',') > 0 AND reputation = (SELECT MAX(reputation) FROM users WHERE POSITION(',' || 'York' || ',' IN ',' || location || ',') > 0)

question: I'm preparing a report on international participation. How many users located in India had earned a Yearling badge before 2014? 'Before 2014' should mean before 1 January 2014. I just need the single count, nothing else.
evidence: 'Yearling' is a badge a member earns for a year of activity on the site.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t1.userid) AS user_count FROM badges AS t1 INNER JOIN users AS t2 ON t1.userid = t2.id WHERE CAST(t2.location AS TEXT) LIKE '%India%' AND t1.name = 'Yearling' AND t1.date < '2014-01-01'

question: I'm putting together a summary of how active badge-holders present themselves on the site. How many different display names appear among the adult users who obtained the Supporter badge? By adult I mean age 19 to 65 inclusive, and please cover all time. I just need that one number.
evidence: NaN stands for a user who never set a display name.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN u.displayname IS NULL OR u.displayname = 'NaN' THEN NULL ELSE u.displayname END) AS different_display_names FROM users AS u INNER JOIN badges AS b ON u.id = b.userid WHERE b.name = 'Supporter' AND u.age BETWEEN 19 AND 65

question: Among all posts whose title contains the phrase 'principal component scores', which one has the most related posts linked to it? For each such post, give me the post title and the number of related posts. If several posts tie for the most, list every one of them with their counts. The count should cover related posts across the site's entire history.
evidence: A related post is another post that the community's link records connect to a given post.
SQL: WITH counts AS (SELECT p.id AS post_id, p.title AS title, COUNT(DISTINCT pl.relatedpostid) AS related_posts FROM posts AS p JOIN postlinks AS pl ON pl.postid = p.id WHERE CAST(p.title AS TEXT) LIKE '%principal component scores%' GROUP BY p.id, p.title) SELECT title, related_posts FROM counts WHERE related_posts = (SELECT MAX(related_posts) FROM counts) ORDER BY title NULLS FIRST

question: I'm auditing accounts on the stats forum. What is the id of the youngest user account whose display name is Michael? If two or more such accounts tie as the youngest, give me the smallest id.
SQL: SELECT id FROM users WHERE displayname = 'Michael' AND age = (SELECT MIN(age) FROM users WHERE displayname = 'Michael') ORDER BY id NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1

question: I'm trying to gauge how many users the bounty feature drew back when it first ran. How many users offered a bounty of 30 or more on some post between 1 January 2010 (inclusive) and 1 January 2011 (exclusive), going by the date the bounty was recorded? By the user who offered a bounty, I mean the post's owner - the owner account where one is recorded, otherwise the owner name on the post. I just need that one count.
evidence: A bounty is a reputation reward a user attaches to a post, recorded as an amount.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(CAST(p.owneruserid AS TEXT), p.ownerdisplayname)) AS users FROM votes AS v JOIN posts AS p ON v.postid = p.id WHERE v.bountyamount >= 30 AND v.creationdate >= '2010-01-01' AND v.creationdate < '2011-01-01'

question: What was the average reputation of users located in India who created a post in 2010? Please give me a single number rounded to two decimal places. Note: 'in 2010' means the calendar year 2010 based on the post's creation date, and any type of post counts. A user counts as located in India only if their location is actually India - a place that merely contains the word India (like the US state Indiana) doesn't count.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(u.reputation) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_reputation FROM users AS u WHERE (TRIM(CAST(u.location AS TEXT)) = 'India' OR (POSITION(',' IN u.location) > 0 AND TRIM(CAST(SUBSTRING(CAST(u.location AS TEXT) FROM POSITION(',' IN u.location) + 1) AS TEXT)) = 'India')) AND u.id IN (SELECT p.owneruserid FROM posts AS p WHERE p.creaiondate >= '2010-01-01' AND p.creaiondate < '2011-01-01')

question: I'm profiling our most active contributors of 2012. Among the users who created more than ten posts in 2012 (judged by each post's creation date), what is their average number of up-votes cast and their average age? Please give me a single row with both averages, each rounded to two decimal places.
evidence: Up-vote: a vote a user cast in favor of a post.
SQL: WITH active AS (SELECT owneruserid FROM posts WHERE creaiondate >= '2012-01-01' AND creaiondate < '2013-01-01' GROUP BY owneruserid HAVING COUNT(*) > 10) SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(u.upvotes) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_upvotes, ROUND(CAST(AVG(u.age) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_age FROM active AS a JOIN users AS u ON u.id = a.owneruserid

question: For each month of 2010, how many posts that have no more than two answers received a link during that month? A month with none counts as zero. Give me the average across all twelve months of 2010, rounded to two decimals.
evidence: A link is a recorded connection that associates one post with another post of the site.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(CASE WHEN (SUM(month_cnt)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(month_cnt)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END / NULLIF(12, 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS average FROM (SELECT TO_CHAR(CAST(t1.creationdate AS TIMESTAMP), 'MM') AS mon, COUNT(DISTINCT t1.postid) AS month_cnt FROM postlinks AS t1 INNER JOIN posts AS t2 ON t1.postid = t2.id WHERE t2.answercount <= 2 AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(t1.creationdate AS TIMESTAMP)) = '2010' GROUP BY mon) AS __photo_derived_1

question: I'm reviewing our 2010 content. What percentage of posts created in 2010 that have a score above 5 were NOT made by high-reputation users? By high-reputation I mean a user with a reputation of at least 1000. Please give me just the single percentage value, rounded to two decimal places. Use the post's creation date to determine that it's from calendar year 2010.
evidence: high-reputation: reputation of at least 1000
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(CASE WHEN (SUM(CASE WHEN t2.reputation >= 1000 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(CASE WHEN t2.reputation >= 1000 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(t1.id), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS percentage FROM posts AS t1 LEFT JOIN users AS t2 ON t1.owneruserid = t2.id WHERE t1.score > 5 AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(t1.creaiondate AS TIMESTAMP)) = '2010'

question: I'm reviewing the history of the question 'Why square the difference instead of taking the absolute value in standard deviation?'. For that post, who left the most edit comments, and how many did they leave? Please give me each editor's display name along with their number of edit comments on that post. If several editors are tied for the most, list each of them with their count. Also, please count every revision as its own event, even when successive revisions carry the same note.
evidence: An edit comment is the note an editor records together with a revision of a post, not a comment posted under the post.
SQL: WITH target AS (SELECT id FROM posts WHERE title = 'Why square the difference instead of taking the absolute value in standard deviation?'), counts AS (SELECT u.displayname, COUNT(*) AS n FROM posthistory AS h JOIN users AS u ON u.id = h.userid WHERE h.postid IN (SELECT id FROM target) AND NOT h.comment IS NULL AND TRIM(CAST(h.comment AS TEXT)) <> '' GROUP BY u.displayname) SELECT displayname, n FROM counts WHERE n = (SELECT MAX(n) FROM counts)

question: For each of the SME, LAM, and KAM segments, identify the CZK customer with the lowest total recorded consumption in 2013, breaking a tie by smaller customer ID. What are the differences between those customers' 2013 totals in SME minus LAM, LAM minus KAM, and KAM minus SME order? Round each to two decimals.
SQL: WITH annual AS (SELECT c.segment, c.customerid, SUM(CAST(y.consumption AS DOUBLE PRECISION)) AS total FROM customers AS c JOIN yearmonth AS y ON y.customerid = c.customerid WHERE c.currency = 'CZK' AND y.date BETWEEN '201301' AND '201312' AND NOT y.consumption IS NULL AND c.segment IN ('SME', 'LAM', 'KAM') GROUP BY c.segment, c.customerid), ranked AS (SELECT segment, total, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY segment ORDER BY total NULLS FIRST, customerid NULLS FIRST) AS rn FROM annual), chosen AS (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN segment = 'SME' THEN total END) AS sme, MAX(CASE WHEN segment = 'LAM' THEN total END) AS lam, MAX(CASE WHEN segment = 'KAM' THEN total END) AS kam FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1) SELECT ROUND(CAST(sme - lam AS DECIMAL), 2), ROUND(CAST(lam - kam AS DECIMAL), 2), ROUND(CAST(kam - sme AS DECIMAL), 2) FROM chosen

question: Among EUR-paying customers in the SME, LAM, and KAM segments, which segments had the highest and lowest percentage increase in total consumption from 2012 to 2013? Return each extreme segment and its increase percentage, rounded to two decimal places; include ties.
SQL: WITH annual AS (SELECT c.segment, SUM(CASE WHEN SUBSTRING(CAST(y.date AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) = '2012' THEN y.consumption ELSE 0 END) AS total_2012, SUM(CASE WHEN SUBSTRING(CAST(y.date AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) = '2013' THEN y.consumption ELSE 0 END) AS total_2013 FROM customers AS c JOIN yearmonth AS y ON c.customerid = y.customerid WHERE c.currency = 'EUR' AND c.segment IN ('SME', 'LAM', 'KAM') AND SUBSTRING(CAST(y.date AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) IN ('2012', '2013') GROUP BY c.segment), rates AS (SELECT segment, ROUND(CAST(100.0 * (total_2013 - total_2012) / NULLIF(NULLIF(total_2012, 0), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS increase_pct FROM annual WHERE total_2012 > 0), ranked AS (SELECT segment, increase_pct, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY increase_pct DESC NULLS LAST) AS highest_rank, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY increase_pct ASC NULLS FIRST) AS lowest_rank FROM rates) SELECT segment, increase_pct FROM ranked WHERE highest_rank = 1 OR lowest_rank = 1 ORDER BY increase_pct DESC NULLS LAST, segment NULLS FIRST

question: For the customer who paid 634.8 on 2012-08-25, what is the relative change in annual consumption from 2012 to 2013, calculated as (2013 total - 2012 total) / 2012 total and rounded to four decimal places?
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(CAST(1.0 * (SUM(CASE WHEN SUBSTRING(CAST(ym.date AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) = '2013' THEN ym.consumption ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN SUBSTRING(CAST(ym.date AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) = '2012' THEN ym.consumption ELSE 0 END)) / NULLIF(NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN SUBSTRING(CAST(ym.date AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) = '2012' THEN ym.consumption ELSE 0 END), 0), 0) AS DECIMAL(20, 8)) AS DECIMAL), 4) FROM yearmonth AS ym WHERE ym.customerid = (SELECT t.customerid FROM transactions_1k AS t WHERE t.date = '2012-08-25' AND CAST(t.price AS DECIMAL(12, 2)) = 634.80)

question: How many customers who pay in EUR and had gas consumption in 2012 also had gas consumption in 2013? I just need a single number: the count of such customers. By 2012 and 2013 I mean those calendar years, and gas consumption in any month of the year counts.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers FROM (SELECT customerid FROM yearmonth WHERE SUBSTRING(CAST(date AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) = '2012' AND customerid IN (SELECT customerid FROM customers WHERE currency = 'EUR') INTERSECT SELECT customerid FROM yearmonth WHERE SUBSTRING(CAST(date AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) = '2013') AS __photo_derived_1

question: I'm reviewing our 2012 performance and want to see which client segments hold our small-scale customers. For each client segment, can you tell me how many customers had total consumption below 30,000 over the whole of 2012? Please count only customers who used their cards at some point during 2012, and treat 30,000 as a strict limit - someone at exactly 30,000 doesn't count. I just need the client segment and the number of such customers per segment.
evidence: Consumption means the amount spent through a customer's fuel cards.
SQL: WITH yearly AS (SELECT customerid, SUM(consumption) AS total_consumption FROM yearmonth WHERE date >= '201201' AND date <= '201212' GROUP BY customerid HAVING SUM(consumption) < 30000) SELECT c.segment AS segment, COUNT(*) AS customers FROM yearly AS y INNER JOIN customers AS c ON c.customerid = y.customerid GROUP BY c.segment ORDER BY c.segment NULLS FIRST

question: I'm reviewing 2013 uptake and want to know the genuinely active cardholder base in each client segment. For each client segment, how many of that segment's customers consumed any fuel at all during the calendar year 2013? I just need the client segment and the number of customers who consumed fuel in 2013, nothing else.
evidence: A customer's consumption for a month is the amount of fuel recorded against them for that month; by 'consumed any fuel in 2013' I mean they had fuel recorded against them in at least one month of 2013.
SQL: SELECT c.segment AS segment, COUNT(DISTINCT y.customerid) AS customers_with_fuel_2013 FROM customers AS c INNER JOIN yearmonth AS y ON c.customerid = y.customerid WHERE y.date BETWEEN '201301' AND '201312' AND y.consumption > 0 GROUP BY c.segment ORDER BY c.segment NULLS FIRST

question: I want to gauge how spread out our high-value fuelling activity in the Czech Republic was over the recorded window. How many whole minutes elapsed from the first to the last fuel transaction at gas stations in the Czech Republic with a price over 1000? Please round down to whole minutes.
evidence: Czech Republic means the gas station is in the CZE country.
SQL: SELECT (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM CAST(MAX(date || ' ' || time) AS TIMESTAMP)) - EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM CAST(MIN(date || ' ' || time) AS TIMESTAMP))) / NULLIF((5 * 13 - 5), 0) AS minutes FROM transactions_1k AS t1 INNER JOIN gasstations AS t2 ON t1.gasstationid = t2.gasstationid WHERE t2.country = 'CZE' AND t1.price > 1000

question: I'm preparing a loyalty review of our steadily active customers in 2013. For each currency, I'd like to know how many customers bought fuel in every month from January through November 2013, with both January and November included. Please give me the currency and that customer count. If several currencies tie, list them all – no ranking needed.
evidence: Consumption means the total fuel a customer purchased in a month on their fuel card; a customer counts for a month if they had any consumption that month.
SQL: WITH RECURSIVE months(m) AS (SELECT '201301' UNION ALL SELECT CAST(CASE WHEN (m) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((m) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END + 1 AS TEXT) FROM months WHERE m < '201311'), steady AS (SELECT customerid FROM yearmonth WHERE date BETWEEN '201301' AND '201311' AND consumption > 0 GROUP BY customerid HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT date) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM months)) SELECT c.currency, COUNT(*) AS customers FROM steady AS s JOIN customers AS c ON c.customerid = s.customerid GROUP BY c.currency

question: I'm putting together currency-specific pricing proposals and need a sense of typical quarterly fuel consumption. Among customers who have fuel consumption recorded in the second quarter of 2013 (April, May and June 2013), what is the average amount of fuel consumed over the whole quarter by an EUR-paying customer, and the same average for a CZK-paying customer? Please round both averages to two decimal places. By EUR-paying / CZK-paying I mean a customer whose account currency is EUR / CZK.
evidence: EUR-paying / CZK-paying: a customer whose account currency is EUR / CZK
SQL: WITH q2 AS (SELECT customerid, SUM(consumption) AS total FROM yearmonth WHERE date BETWEEN '201304' AND '201306' GROUP BY customerid) SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(CASE WHEN c.currency = 'EUR' THEN q2.total END) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS eur_avg_quarter, ROUND(CAST(AVG(CASE WHEN c.currency = 'CZK' THEN q2.total END) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS czk_avg_quarter FROM customers AS c JOIN q2 ON q2.customerid = c.customerid

question: I want to see how much our busiest month grew from 2012 to 2013. What was the difference between our peak monthly total consumption in 2013 and our peak monthly total consumption in 2012, in consumption units, rounded to the nearest whole number? By total consumption in a calendar month I mean the consumption of the whole customer base that month, and the peak of a year is the calendar month with the highest total consumption in that year.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST((SELECT SUM(CAST(consumption AS DOUBLE PRECISION)) FROM yearmonth WHERE SUBSTRING(CAST(date AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) = '2013' GROUP BY SUBSTRING(CAST(date AS TEXT) FROM 5 FOR 2) ORDER BY SUM(CAST(consumption AS DOUBLE PRECISION)) DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1) - (SELECT SUM(CAST(consumption AS DOUBLE PRECISION)) FROM yearmonth WHERE SUBSTRING(CAST(date AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) = '2012' GROUP BY SUBSTRING(CAST(date AS TEXT) FROM 5 FOR 2) ORDER BY SUM(CAST(consumption AS DOUBLE PRECISION)) DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1) AS DECIMAL), 0) AS difference

question: I'm reviewing customer 15621's fuel spending on the fleet card in 2013. What was their average fuel consumption per month, counting only the months in which they actually purchased fuel? Give me the single average value rounded to two decimal places.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(SUM(consumption) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS average_monthly_consumption FROM yearmonth WHERE customerid = 15621 AND date BETWEEN '201301' AND '201312' AND consumption > 0

question: I want to compare how much a typical Czech-koruna-billed client spent versus a euro-billed client during 2012, to see whether the two currency segments behave differently. Please give me the difference between the average 2012 consumption of a CZK-paying customer and the average 2012 consumption of an EUR-paying customer, with the EUR average subtracted from the CZK average. Only include customers who had consumption in 2012 in each average, and the period is calendar year 2012. Just send me that one number, rounded to the nearest whole unit.
evidence: Consumption means the monthly consumption amount recorded per customer.
SQL: WITH per_customer AS (SELECT customerid, SUM(consumption) AS tot_2012 FROM yearmonth WHERE SUBSTRING(CAST(date AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) = '2012' GROUP BY customerid) SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(CASE WHEN c.currency = 'CZK' THEN p.tot_2012 END) - AVG(CASE WHEN c.currency = 'EUR' THEN p.tot_2012 END) AS DECIMAL), 0) AS diff FROM customers AS c JOIN per_customer AS p ON c.customerid = p.customerid

question: I'm sizing a premium offer for our heaviest corporate fuel buyers ahead of renewals. How many KAM-segment customers paying in CZK had total fuel consumption above 1 million (1,000,000) in calendar year 2013? I just need that number of customers.
evidence: KAM is one of our client segments.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM (SELECT t2.customerid FROM customers AS t1 INNER JOIN yearmonth AS t2 ON t1.customerid = t2.customerid WHERE t1.currency = 'CZK' AND t1.segment = 'KAM' AND CAST(t2.date AS TEXT) LIKE '2013%' GROUP BY t2.customerid HAVING SUM(t2.consumption) > 1000000) AS __photo_derived_1

question: For my February 2013 activity report: how many SME customers actually purchased gas in February 2013? Please give me just a single whole number - the count of SME customers who consumed gas during the calendar month of February 2013 (Feb 1-28, 2013).
evidence: By "gas" I mean gasoline (motor fuel) purchases, not natural gas.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t2.customerid) AS sme_gas_customers FROM customers AS t1 INNER JOIN yearmonth AS t2 ON t1.customerid = t2.customerid WHERE t1.segment = 'SME' AND t2.date = '201302' AND t2.consumption > 0

question: Which away teams are tied for the most away wins in the Scottish Premier League 2009/2010 season?
SQL: WITH wins AS (SELECT m.away_team_api_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM match AS m JOIN league AS l ON l.id = m.league_id WHERE l.name = 'Scotland Premier League' AND m.season = '2009/2010' AND m.away_team_goal > m.home_team_goal GROUP BY m.away_team_api_id) SELECT t.team_long_name FROM wins AS w JOIN team AS t ON t.team_api_id = w.away_team_api_id WHERE w.n = (SELECT MAX(n) FROM wins) ORDER BY t.team_api_id NULLS FIRST

question: List the long name of teams with above-average build-up play passing in 2012.
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT t4.team_long_name FROM team_attributes AS t3 INNER JOIN team AS t4 ON t3.team_api_id = t4.team_api_id WHERE SUBSTRING(CAST(t3.date AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) = '2012' AND t3.buildupplaypassing > (SELECT CASE WHEN (SUM(t2.buildupplaypassing)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(t2.buildupplaypassing)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END / NULLIF(COUNT(t1.id), 0) FROM team AS t1 INNER JOIN team_attributes AS t2 ON t1.team_api_id = t2.team_api_id WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(t2.date AS TIMESTAMP)) = '2012')

question: List the ten players taller than 180 cm with the highest mean recorded heading accuracy, highest first. Break mean ties by player API ID.
SQL: SELECT p.player_name FROM player AS p JOIN player_attributes AS a ON a.player_api_id = p.player_api_id WHERE p.height > 180 GROUP BY p.player_api_id, p.player_name ORDER BY AVG(a.heading_accuracy) DESC NULLS LAST, p.player_api_id NULLS FIRST LIMIT 10

question: List the name of leagues in which the average goals by the home team is higher than the away team in the 2009/2010 season.
SQL: SELECT t1.name FROM league AS t1 INNER JOIN match AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.league_id WHERE t2.season = '2009/2010' GROUP BY t1.name HAVING (CASE WHEN (SUM(t2.home_team_goal)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(t2.home_team_goal)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT t2.id), 0)) - (CASE WHEN (SUM(t2.away_team_goal)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(t2.away_team_goal)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT t2.id), 0)) > 0

question: Between the tallest and shortest players, who has the higher average finishing attribute across his recorded assessments? Give the player's name.
SQL: SELECT p.player_name FROM player AS p JOIN player_attributes AS a ON a.player_api_id = p.player_api_id WHERE p.height IN ((SELECT MAX(height) FROM player), (SELECT MIN(height) FROM player)) GROUP BY p.player_api_id, p.player_name ORDER BY AVG(a.finishing) DESC NULLS LAST, p.player_api_id NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1

question: What is Abdou Diallo's mean recorded ball-control score minus Aaron Appindangoye's mean recorded ball-control score?
SQL: SELECT CASE WHEN (SUM(CASE WHEN t1.player_name = 'Abdou Diallo' THEN t2.ball_control ELSE 0 END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(CASE WHEN t1.player_name = 'Abdou Diallo' THEN t2.ball_control ELSE 0 END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END / NULLIF(COUNT(CASE WHEN t1.player_name = 'Abdou Diallo' THEN t2.id ELSE NULL END), 0) - CASE WHEN (SUM(CASE WHEN t1.player_name = 'Aaron Appindangoye' THEN t2.ball_control ELSE 0 END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(CASE WHEN t1.player_name = 'Aaron Appindangoye' THEN t2.ball_control ELSE 0 END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END / NULLIF(COUNT(CASE WHEN t1.player_name = 'Aaron Appindangoye' THEN t2.id ELSE NULL END), 0) FROM player AS t1 INNER JOIN player_attributes AS t2 ON t1.player_api_id = t2.player_api_id

question: By what percentage is Ariel Borysiuk's overall rating in his latest attribute record higher than Paulin Puel's latest overall rating? Round to two decimals.
SQL: WITH latest AS (SELECT p.player_name, a.overall_rating, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.player_api_id ORDER BY a.date DESC NULLS LAST, a.id DESC NULLS LAST) AS rn FROM player AS p JOIN player_attributes AS a ON a.player_api_id = p.player_api_id WHERE p.player_name IN ('Ariel Borysiuk', 'Paulin Puel')) SELECT ROUND(CAST(100.0 * (MAX(CASE WHEN player_name = 'Ariel Borysiuk' THEN overall_rating END) - MAX(CASE WHEN player_name = 'Paulin Puel' THEN overall_rating END)) / NULLIF(NULLIF(MAX(CASE WHEN player_name = 'Paulin Puel' THEN overall_rating END), 0), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) FROM latest WHERE rn = 1

question: On what date did Kevin Constant first record his highest crossing score?
SQL: SELECT pa.date FROM player_attributes AS pa JOIN player AS p ON p.player_fifa_api_id = pa.player_fifa_api_id WHERE p.player_name = 'Kevin Constant' AND NOT pa.crossing IS NULL ORDER BY pa.crossing DESC NULLS LAST, pa.date ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1

question: Among players shorter than 180 cm, what percentage have at least one recorded overall rating above 70? Round to two decimal places.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.overall_rating > 70 THEN p.player_api_id END) / NULLIF(NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT p.player_api_id), 0), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) FROM player AS p LEFT JOIN player_attributes AS a ON a.player_api_id = p.player_api_id WHERE p.height < 180

question: What is the average height, in centimetres, of the players taller than 180 cm who have appeared in the home team's number-3 lineup slot? This should cover the whole recorded match history with no season or date restriction. 'Taller than 180' means strictly taller than 180 cm. Please round the final average to two decimal places and return just that single value.
evidence: Number-3 lineup slot: each match records a home team's starting eleven as eleven ordered player slots; the number-3 slot is the home team's third slot.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(height) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_height FROM (SELECT p.height AS height FROM player AS p JOIN match AS m ON m.home_player_3 = p.player_api_id WHERE p.height > 180 GROUP BY p.player_api_id, p.height) AS __photo_derived_1

question: I'm sizing up how defensive-minded the young generation is. Among players born after 1990 (i.e., born in 1991 or later) who have a defensive work rate rating, what share are rated high? A player counts as rated high if they've been rated high at any point in their career. Give me that share as a percentage rounded to two decimal places - nothing else.
evidence: Defensive work rate: a player's rating for defensive effort, on a low / medium / high scale.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(100.0 * (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT pa.player_api_id) FROM player AS p JOIN player_attributes AS pa ON pa.player_api_id = p.player_api_id WHERE CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(p.birthday AS TIMESTAMP))) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(p.birthday AS TIMESTAMP))) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END > 1990 AND pa.defensive_work_rate = 'high') / NULLIF((SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT pa.player_api_id) FROM player AS p JOIN player_attributes AS pa ON pa.player_api_id = p.player_api_id WHERE CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(p.birthday AS TIMESTAMP))) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(p.birthday AS TIMESTAMP))) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END > 1990 AND pa.defensive_work_rate IN ('low', 'medium', 'high')), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS share_pct

question: I've shortlisted the players whose overall rating as of 31 December 2010 was above 80 - strictly above 80, that is. How many matches did these players play on average during the 2010/2011 season? Please give me just that single average, rounded to two decimals.
SQL: WITH latest AS (SELECT player_api_id, MAX(date) AS md FROM player_attributes WHERE date <= '2010-12-31 00:00:00' GROUP BY player_api_id), shortlist AS (SELECT p.player_api_id FROM latest AS l JOIN player_attributes AS a ON a.player_api_id = l.player_api_id AND a.date = l.md JOIN player AS p ON p.player_api_id = l.player_api_id WHERE a.overall_rating > 80 GROUP BY p.player_api_id), slots AS (SELECT id, home_player_1 AS pid FROM match WHERE season = '2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_2 FROM match WHERE season = '2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_3 FROM match WHERE season = '2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_4 FROM match WHERE season = '2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_5 FROM match WHERE season = '2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_6 FROM match WHERE season = '2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_7 FROM match WHERE season = '2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_8 FROM match WHERE season = '2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_9 FROM match WHERE season = '2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_10 FROM match WHERE season = '2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_11 FROM match WHERE season = '2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_1 FROM match WHERE season = '2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_2 FROM match WHERE season = '2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_3 FROM match WHERE season = '2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_4 FROM match WHERE season = '2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_5 FROM match WHERE season = '2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_6 FROM match WHERE season = '2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_7 FROM match WHERE season = '2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_8 FROM match WHERE season = '2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_9 FROM match WHERE season = '2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_10 FROM match WHERE season = '2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_11 FROM match WHERE season = '2010/2011'), apps AS (SELECT pid, COUNT(DISTINCT id) AS matches FROM slots WHERE NOT pid IS NULL GROUP BY pid) SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(COALESCE(x.matches, 0)) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS average_matches FROM shortlist AS s LEFT JOIN apps AS x ON x.pid = s.player_api_id

question: What is the average height in centimeters of players whose current defensive work rate grade is not medium? Use each player's most recent rating record to determine their current grade, and round the result to two decimal places. I just need that single number.
evidence: Defensive work rate grades run low, medium and high.
SQL: WITH latest AS (SELECT player_api_id, defensive_work_rate, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY player_api_id ORDER BY date DESC NULLS LAST, id DESC NULLS LAST) AS rn FROM player_attributes) SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(p.height) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS average_height FROM latest AS l JOIN player AS p ON p.player_api_id = l.player_api_id WHERE l.rn = 1 AND l.defensive_work_rate IN ('low', 'high')

question: I'm preparing a report on team playing styles. First, consider only teams whose chance creation passing class was Risky at any point in the recorded history. Among those, I want the short names that are carried by more than one club. For each such short name, please give me: the short name, the number of clubs that carry it, and the average chance creation passing risk of those clubs that was in force on 19 September 2014, rounded to one decimal place. Sort the results by that average, highest first; if two averages are the same, order them alphabetically by short name.
evidence: A team's chance creation passing class is 'Risky' when chanceCreationPassingClass = 'Risky'; its chance creation passing risk is the chanceCreationPassing value in force on the date in question.
SQL: WITH risky AS (SELECT DISTINCT team_api_id FROM team_attributes WHERE chancecreationpassingclass = 'Risky'), cur AS (SELECT team_api_id, chancecreationpassing FROM team_attributes AS ta WHERE ta.date = (SELECT MAX(date) FROM team_attributes AS x WHERE x.team_api_id = ta.team_api_id AND x.date <= '2014-09-19 00:00:00')) SELECT t.team_short_name AS team_short_name, COUNT(DISTINCT t.team_api_id) AS n_teams, ROUND(CAST(AVG(c.chancecreationpassing) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS avg_passing FROM team AS t JOIN risky AS r ON r.team_api_id = t.team_api_id JOIN cur AS c ON c.team_api_id = t.team_api_id GROUP BY t.team_short_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.team_api_id) > 1 ORDER BY avg_passing DESC NULLS LAST, t.team_short_name NULLS FIRST

question: I want to gauge how tall the current medium-defensive-work players from the 1990-1995 birth cohort are. Please find the average height, in centimetres, of players born from 1990 through 1995 inclusive whose defensive work rating is medium, and round the average to two decimals. A player's rating is the grade on their most recent record that carries a grade.
evidence: The defensive work rating grades are low, medium and high.
SQL: WITH latest_grade AS (SELECT player_api_id, defensive_work_rate, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY player_api_id ORDER BY date DESC NULLS LAST, id DESC NULLS LAST) AS rn FROM player_attributes WHERE defensive_work_rate IN ('low', 'medium', 'high')) SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(p.height) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS average_height FROM player AS p JOIN latest_grade AS g ON g.player_api_id = p.player_api_id AND g.rn = 1 WHERE SUBSTRING(CAST(p.birthday AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) BETWEEN '1990' AND '1995' AND g.defensive_work_rate = 'medium'

question: What is the average weight of all left-footed players? Round the average to one decimal place.
evidence: Left-footed means the player's preferred foot when attacking is the left one.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(weight) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS average_weight FROM player WHERE player_api_id IN (SELECT player_api_id FROM player_attributes WHERE preferred_foot = 'left')

question: I'm putting together a participation report for the 2015/2016 season. For every player whose name starts with Adam and who weighs more than 170, I need the number of matches he played during that season. Please return, one row per qualifying player, the player's name and his number of matches played in the 2015/2016 season, and nothing else. The season I mean is the one labeled '2015/2016'.
