For every account held at the Tabor branch as of 31 December 1996, I need a one-row profile per account, ordered among tied ranks by ascending account id, showing: the account id; the date the account was opened; the owner's gender and their age at 31 December 1996 in whole completed years; the number of credit cards issued to the account by 31 December 1996 (0 if none); the number of loans approved to the account by 31 December 1996 (0 if none); a loan standing label; the number of transactions on the account during 1997; the total money into the account during 1997; the total money out of the account during 1997; the peak balance reached on the account during 1997 (0 if none); and the account's rank by 1997 peak balance, highest first, with ties sharing a rank and the next rank skipped (e.g. 1, 1, 3). All 'as of' figures are taken at 31 December 1996; activity figures cover the calendar year 1997. A card or loan counts as held if it was issued or approved on or before 31 December 1996. The loan standing label is: 'no loan' if the account had no loans approved by 31 December 1996; otherwise 'defaulted' if any of its loans has repayment status B; otherwise 'repaying' if any has status C or D; otherwise 'paid off'. Money in is the sum of credit transaction amounts; money out is the sum of debit and cash-withdrawal transaction amounts. The account owner is the person with the 'OWNER' disposition on the account; other dispositions are just additional users. Nothing beyond these fields, please.
evidence: Loan repayment status codes: A means the contract finished and was paid off, B means the loan was not repaid (default), C means the loan is running and being repaid, D means the loan is running and the client is in debt on it. Transaction types: a credit transaction brings money into the account, a debit transaction takes money out, and a cash withdrawal takes money out in cash.
SQL: WITH cohort AS (SELECT a.account_id, a.date AS open_date FROM account AS a JOIN district AS d ON d.district_id = a.district_id WHERE d.a2 = 'Tabor' AND a.date <= '1996-12-31'), own AS (SELECT co.account_id, co.open_date, c.gender, c.birth_date FROM cohort AS co JOIN disp AS dp ON dp.account_id = co.account_id AND dp.type = 'OWNER' JOIN client AS c ON c.client_id = dp.client_id), cards96 AS (SELECT dp.account_id, COUNT(cd.card_id) AS n_cards FROM disp AS dp JOIN card AS cd ON cd.disp_id = dp.disp_id WHERE cd.issued <= '1996-12-31' GROUP BY dp.account_id), loans96 AS (SELECT l.account_id, COUNT(*) AS n_loans, SUM(CASE WHEN l.status = 'B' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_bad, SUM(CASE WHEN l.status IN ('C', 'D') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_run FROM loan AS l WHERE l.date <= '1996-12-31' GROUP BY l.account_id), t1997 AS (SELECT t.account_id, COUNT(*) AS n_trans, SUM(CASE WHEN t.type = 'PRIJEM' THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END) AS money_in, SUM(CASE WHEN t.type <> 'PRIJEM' THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END) AS money_out, MAX(t.balance) AS max_bal FROM trans AS t WHERE t.date BETWEEN '1997-01-01' AND '1997-12-31' GROUP BY t.account_id) SELECT o.account_id, o.open_date AS date_opened, o.gender AS owner_gender, 1996 - CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(o.birth_date AS TIMESTAMP))) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(o.birth_date AS TIMESTAMP))) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END AS owner_age_at_end_1996, COALESCE(c.n_cards, 0) AS cards_by_end_1996, COALESCE(l.n_loans, 0) AS loans_by_end_1996, CASE WHEN COALESCE(l.n_loans, 0) = 0 THEN 'no loan' WHEN l.n_bad > 0 THEN 'defaulted' WHEN l.n_run > 0 THEN 'repaying' ELSE 'paid off' END AS loan_standing, COALESCE(t.n_trans, 0) AS trans_1997_count, COALESCE(t.money_in, 0) AS money_in_1997, COALESCE(t.money_out, 0) AS money_out_1997, COALESCE(t.max_bal, 0) AS max_balance_1997, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(t.max_bal, 0) DESC NULLS LAST) AS balance_rank FROM own AS o LEFT JOIN cards96 AS c ON c.account_id = o.account_id LEFT JOIN loans96 AS l ON l.account_id = o.account_id LEFT JOIN t1997 AS t ON t.account_id = o.account_id ORDER BY balance_rank NULLS FIRST, o.account_id NULLS FIRST

question: I'd like a district-by-district picture of where our classic-card-holding account owners send money outside the bank. For every district, give me: the district name, the number of clients who own an account and hold a classic credit card, the number of external accounts at other banks those clients paid through outgoing payments, and the total amount of those outgoing payments. A district means the district of the branch where the owned account is held — not the client's home district — and each client and every outgoing payment from the account they own counts toward that account's branch district. Include every district, even ones with no such clients or no such outgoing payments (show zeros). Use the whole recorded payment history. Order by total amount paid from highest to lowest, and alphabetically by district name when totals tie. Don't round the totals.
evidence: An account owner is the client recorded as 'OWNER' on the account. An outgoing payment is a transaction recorded with type 'VYDAJ' (money paid out of the account). An external account is an account held at another bank to which the account holder sends money; the receiving bank together with the receiving account number identifies it.
SQL: WITH holders AS (SELECT dp.client_id, dp.account_id, a.district_id FROM card AS c JOIN disp AS dp ON dp.disp_id = c.disp_id AND dp.type = 'OWNER' JOIN account AS a ON a.account_id = dp.account_id WHERE c.type = 'classic') SELECT d.a2 AS district, COUNT(DISTINCT h.client_id) AS classic_card_holders, COUNT(DISTINCT t.account) AS external_accounts_paid, COALESCE(SUM(t.amount), 0) AS total_amount_paid FROM district AS d LEFT JOIN holders AS h ON h.district_id = d.district_id LEFT JOIN trans AS t ON t.account_id = h.account_id AND t.type = 'VYDAJ' AND t.account > 0 GROUP BY d.district_id, d.a2 ORDER BY total_amount_paid DESC NULLS LAST, district ASC NULLS FIRST

question: I'm planning services for our older female customers. For the clients who are female and were born before 1930, please look at the branches that hold their accounts, and then the districts those branches are located in. What is the average salary of those districts? Round the result to 2 decimal places. Note: born before 1930 means calendar birth dates before 1 January 1930.
evidence: Average salary refers to the district attribute describing average salary.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(d.a11) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS average_salary FROM district AS d WHERE d.district_id IN (SELECT a.district_id FROM account AS a JOIN disp AS x ON x.account_id = a.account_id JOIN client AS c ON c.client_id = x.client_id WHERE c.gender = 'F' AND c.birth_date < '1930-01-01')

question: I'm preparing a campaign for senior female clients and want a sense of the economic profile of their home districts. Could you tell me the average of the average salaries of the districts where our female clients born before 1950 live? Please give me just that single figure, rounded to two decimal places.
evidence: Average salary means the average yearly salary recorded for a district, in CZK.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(t1.a11) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS average_salary FROM district AS t1 WHERE t1.district_id IN (SELECT t2.district_id FROM client AS t2 WHERE t2.gender = 'F' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(t2.birth_date AS TIMESTAMP)) < '1950')

question: I want to know whether our small, healthy loans are concentrated in richer or poorer districts before we decide where to grow the small-loan business. Please give me one number: the average district salary, rounded to two decimals, across the districts where the accounts holding these loans are located. The cohort is loans with an approved amount below 100,000 that are still running without issues.
evidence: Loan status C means the contract is running with no problems so far. District average salary is the average salary recorded for a district.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(d.a11) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS average_district_salary FROM district AS d WHERE d.district_id IN (SELECT a.district_id FROM account AS a WHERE a.account_id IN (SELECT l.account_id FROM loan AS l WHERE l.amount < 100000 AND l.status = 'C'))

question: I'm studying how client age relates to branch location. For each of two client cohorts, I want the cohort label and the average salary across the districts where the branches holding that cohort's accounts are located, rounded to the nearest whole number. A client's cohort is based on birth date: born 1980 or later is the young cohort, born 1919 or earlier is the old cohort. Note the district of an account is the district of its branch, not the client's home district. Give me one row per cohort, young cohort first. Nothing else.
SQL: WITH cohort_districts AS (SELECT a.district_id, CASE WHEN c.birth_date >= '1980-01-01' THEN 'young' ELSE 'old' END AS cohort FROM client AS c JOIN disp AS d ON d.client_id = c.client_id JOIN account AS a ON a.account_id = d.account_id WHERE c.birth_date >= '1980-01-01' OR c.birth_date <= '1919-12-31' GROUP BY a.district_id, CASE WHEN c.birth_date >= '1980-01-01' THEN 'young' ELSE 'old' END) SELECT cohort, CASE WHEN (ROUND(AVG(x.a11))) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((ROUND(AVG(x.a11))) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END AS avg_salary FROM cohort_districts AS cd JOIN district AS x ON x.district_id = cd.district_id GROUP BY cohort ORDER BY CASE cohort WHEN 'young' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END NULLS FIRST

question: By what percentage was Paul di Resta's fastest-lap speed in race 853 higher than in race 854? Use the speed in race 854 as the baseline and round to two decimals.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(100.0 * (MAX(CASE WHEN r.raceid = 853 THEN CAST(r.fastestlapspeed AS DECIMAL(12, 4)) END) - MAX(CASE WHEN r.raceid = 854 THEN CAST(r.fastestlapspeed AS DECIMAL(12, 4)) END)) / NULLIF(NULLIF(MAX(CASE WHEN r.raceid = 854 THEN CAST(r.fastestlapspeed AS DECIMAL(12, 4)) END), 0), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) FROM drivers AS d JOIN results AS r ON r.driverid = d.driverid WHERE d.forename = 'Paul' AND d.surname = 'di Resta' AND r.raceid IN (853, 854)

question: What percentage of Lewis Hamilton's recorded race entries from 2010 onward were not victories? Round to two decimals.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN x.positionorder <> 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) FROM results AS x JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = x.driverid JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = x.raceid WHERE d.forename = 'Lewis' AND d.surname = 'Hamilton' AND r.year >= 2010

question: Which driver won the most recorded races? Give their first name, last name, nationality, and highest recorded driver-standings points total.
SQL: WITH wins AS (SELECT driverid, COUNT(*) AS win_count FROM results WHERE positionorder = 1 GROUP BY driverid), winner AS (SELECT driverid FROM wins ORDER BY win_count DESC NULLS LAST, driverid NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1) SELECT d.forename, d.surname, d.nationality, (SELECT MAX(s.points) FROM driverstandings AS s WHERE s.driverid = d.driverid) FROM winner AS w JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = w.driverid

question: In the 1988 Australian Grand Prix, by what percentage was the winner's elapsed time shorter than the last full-distance finisher's? Use the last finisher's time as denominator and round to two decimals.
SQL: WITH finished AS (SELECT x.positionorder, x.milliseconds FROM results AS x JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = x.raceid JOIN status AS s ON s.statusid = x.statusid WHERE r.name = 'Australian Grand Prix' AND r.year = 1988 AND s.status = 'Finished' AND NOT x.milliseconds IS NULL), extremes AS (SELECT MIN(CASE WHEN positionorder = 1 THEN milliseconds END) AS winner_ms, MAX(CASE WHEN positionorder = (SELECT MAX(positionorder) FROM finished) THEN milliseconds END) AS last_ms FROM finished) SELECT ROUND(CAST(100.0 * (last_ms - winner_ms) / NULLIF(NULLIF(last_ms, 0), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) FROM extremes

question: What percentage of Japanese-driver race entries from 2007 through 2009 matched their race winner's recorded lap count? Round to two decimals.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN x.laps = (SELECT y.laps FROM results AS y WHERE y.raceid = x.raceid AND y.positionorder = 1 ORDER BY y.resultid NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) FROM results AS x JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = x.raceid JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = x.driverid WHERE d.nationality = 'Japanese' AND r.year BETWEEN 2007 AND 2009

question: For each year before 1975 with recorded winner times, what was the mean race winner elapsed time in seconds? Round the exact mean to two decimal places; if it is exactly halfway, round away from zero. Order by year.
SQL: SELECT r.year, FLOOR((SUM(x.milliseconds) + 5 * COUNT(*)) / NULLIF((10 * COUNT(*)), 0)) / NULLIF(100.0, 0) FROM results AS x JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = x.raceid WHERE r.year < 1975 AND x.positionorder = 1 AND NOT x.milliseconds IS NULL GROUP BY r.year ORDER BY r.year NULLS FIRST

question: From 2000 through 2005, what percentage of race results were by drivers born before 1985 who completed more than 50 laps?
SQL: SELECT CASE WHEN (SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(t3.dob AS TIMESTAMP)) < '1985' AND t1.laps > 50 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(t3.dob AS TIMESTAMP)) < '1985' AND t1.laps > 50 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) FROM results AS t1 INNER JOIN races AS t2 ON t1.raceid = t2.raceid INNER JOIN drivers AS t3 ON t1.driverid = t3.driverid WHERE t2.year BETWEEN 2000 AND 2005

question: Which constructor scored most points from Monaco Grand Prix between 1980 and 2010? List the score, name and nationality of this team.
SQL: SELECT SUM(t1.points), t2.name, t2.nationality FROM constructorresults AS t1 INNER JOIN constructors AS t2 ON t1.constructorid = t2.constructorid INNER JOIN races AS t3 ON t3.raceid = t1.raceid WHERE t3.name = 'Monaco Grand Prix' AND t3.year BETWEEN 1980 AND 2010 GROUP BY t2.name, t2.nationality ORDER BY SUM(t1.points) DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1

question: Who recorded the fastest Q3 qualifying time at Marina Bay Street Circuit in 2008? Give the driver's first and last name.
SQL: SELECT t2.forename, t2.surname FROM qualifying AS t1 INNER JOIN drivers AS t2 ON t1.driverid = t2.driverid INNER JOIN races AS t3 ON t1.raceid = t3.raceid WHERE NOT q3 IS NULL AND t3.year = 2008 AND t3.circuitid IN (SELECT circuitid FROM circuits WHERE name = 'Marina Bay Street Circuit') ORDER BY CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST(q3 AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION(':' IN q3) - 1)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST(q3 AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION(':' IN q3) - 1)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END * 60 + CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST(q3 AS TEXT) FROM POSITION(':' IN q3) + 1 FOR POSITION('.' IN q3) - POSITION(':' IN q3) - 1)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST(q3 AS TEXT) FROM POSITION(':' IN q3) + 1 FOR POSITION('.' IN q3) - POSITION(':' IN q3) - 1)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END + CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST(q3 AS TEXT) FROM POSITION('.' IN q3) + 1)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST(q3 AS TEXT) FROM POSITION('.' IN q3) + 1)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END / NULLIF(1000, 0) ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1

question: Which 20 drivers recorded the shortest single lap times in Formula 1 races? Give their full names, shortest lap first.
SQL: WITH per_driver AS (SELECT driverid, MIN(milliseconds) AS fastest_ms FROM laptimes WHERE milliseconds > 0 GROUP BY driverid) SELECT d.forename || ' ' || d.surname AS full_name FROM per_driver AS p JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = p.driverid ORDER BY p.fastest_ms NULLS FIRST, d.driverid NULLS FIRST LIMIT 20

question: For each Formula 1 circuit in Italy with recorded laps, give the circuit name and its fastest recorded lap time in minutes:seconds.milliseconds format.
SQL: WITH ranked_laps AS (SELECT c.circuitid, c.name AS circuit_name, l.time AS lap_record, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.circuitid ORDER BY l.milliseconds NULLS FIRST, l.raceid NULLS FIRST, l.driverid NULLS FIRST, l.lap NULLS FIRST) AS rn FROM laptimes AS l JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = l.raceid JOIN circuits AS c ON c.circuitid = r.circuitid WHERE c.country = 'Italy' AND l.milliseconds > 0) SELECT circuit_name, lap_record FROM ranked_laps WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY circuit_name NULLS FIRST, circuitid NULLS FIRST

question: I'm comparing pit stop activity at the newer Grand Prix weekends. Among the 2017 races that were not hosted in 2000, what was the average number of pit stops per race? Please take the average of all of those races and round it to two decimal places.
evidence: Hosted in 2000 means the race was on the 2000 race calendar.
SQL: WITH cohort AS (SELECT raceid FROM races WHERE year = 2017 AND NOT name IN (SELECT name FROM races WHERE year = 2000)) SELECT ROUND(CAST(1.0 * (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pitstops WHERE raceid IN (SELECT raceid FROM cohort)) / NULLIF((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cohort), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_pit_stops_per_race

question: I'm writing a retrospective on German F1 drivers born between 1971 and 1985, and I'd like to quantify how often each of them reached the final part of qualifying. For every German driver born in 1971 through 1985 inclusive, over their entire career (every race on record), please give me their forename, surname, Wikipedia page link, date of birth, and the number of Q3 times they set. Sort the list from most Q3 times to fewest, and where two drivers have the same number, put the older one (by date of birth) first.
evidence: Q3 is the third and final part of the qualifying session that sets the starting grid; a driver's Q3 time is the lap time recorded for them in that part.
SQL: SELECT d.forename, d.surname, d.url, d.dob, COUNT(NULLIF(q.q3, '')) AS q3_times FROM drivers AS d LEFT JOIN qualifying AS q ON q.driverid = d.driverid WHERE d.nationality = 'German' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(d.dob AS TIMESTAMP)) BETWEEN '1971' AND '1985' GROUP BY d.driverid ORDER BY q3_times DESC NULLS LAST, d.dob ASC NULLS FIRST

question: I'm writing a retrospective on the 1995 Japanese Grand Prix and want to highlight how far off the pace the slowest qualifier was. Could you tell me who set the slowest time in the first qualifying session (Q1) of that race? For that driver (or drivers, if two share the same slowest time, please list them all), I'd like their short reference name, nationality, birthday, and their Q1 time. To be clear, I mean the race named 'Japanese Grand Prix' in the 1995 season. Nothing else needed.
evidence: By 'reference name' I mean the short driver code like 'hamilton'; by 'Q1' I mean the first of the three qualifying sessions; by 'birthday' I mean the driver's date of birth.
SQL: WITH t AS (SELECT d.driverref AS driverref, d.nationality AS nationality, d.dob AS dob, q.q1 AS q1 FROM qualifying AS q INNER JOIN races AS r ON q.raceid = r.raceid INNER JOIN drivers AS d ON q.driverid = d.driverid WHERE r.name = 'Japanese Grand Prix' AND r.year = 1995 AND NOT q.q1 IS NULL AND q.q1 <> '') SELECT a.driverref, a.nationality, a.dob, a.q1 FROM t AS a WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM t AS b WHERE CASE WHEN (b.q1) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((b.q1) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END > CASE WHEN (a.q1) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((a.q1) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END OR (CASE WHEN (b.q1) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((b.q1) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END = CASE WHEN (a.q1) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((a.q1) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END AND b.q1 > a.q1))

question: For qualifying at the 1995 Japanese Grand Prix, I need the nationality of the driver who set the slowest time in Q1. If two drivers tie for the slowest Q1 time, give me each of their nationalities. I only want the nationality value(s), nothing else.
SQL: WITH t AS (SELECT d.nationality, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY CASE WHEN (REPLACE(SUBSTRING(CAST(q.q1 AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION(':' IN q.q1)), ':', '')) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((REPLACE(SUBSTRING(CAST(q.q1 AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION(':' IN q.q1)), ':', '')) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END DESC NULLS LAST, CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST(q.q1 AS TEXT) FROM POSITION(':' IN q.q1) + 1)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST(q.q1 AS TEXT) FROM POSITION(':' IN q.q1) + 1)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END DESC NULLS LAST) AS rnk FROM qualifying AS q JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = q.driverid JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = q.raceid WHERE r.year = 1995 AND r.name = 'Japanese Grand Prix' AND NOT q.q1 IS NULL AND q.q1 <> '') SELECT nationality FROM t WHERE rnk = 1

question: Who set the fastest time in Q1 at the 1995 Japanese Grand Prix, and what was that time? Please give me the driver's forename and surname, and the Q1 time. By '1995 Japanese Grand Prix' I mean the race of the 1995 season named 'Japanese Grand Prix'. If two drivers tied for the fastest Q1 time, list them all.
evidence: Q1: the time a driver set in the first qualifying session.
SQL: SELECT d.forename, d.surname, q.q1 FROM qualifying AS q JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = q.driverid JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = q.raceid WHERE r.year = 1995 AND r.name = 'Japanese Grand Prix' AND NOT q.q1 IS NULL ORDER BY CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST(q.q1 AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION(':' IN q.q1) - 1)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST(q.q1 AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION(':' IN q.q1) - 1)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END ASC NULLS FIRST, CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST(q.q1 AS TEXT) FROM POSITION(':' IN q.q1) + 1)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST(q.q1 AS TEXT) FROM POSITION(':' IN q.q1) + 1)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1

question: For the 2010 Formula 1 season, how many drivers did Lucas di Grassi qualify ahead of? I want a single number: the count of drivers he out-qualified over the whole season. By 'qualify ahead of' I mean recording a better qualifying position than that driver in the same race, with a lower position number being better. The 2010 season means the races held in the year 2010.
evidence: qualifying position: the starting slot a driver earns in the qualifying session before a race
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t2.driverid) AS drivers_qualified_ahead_of FROM qualifying AS t1 JOIN qualifying AS t2 ON t2.raceid = t1.raceid AND t2.position > t1.position JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = t1.driverid JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = t1.raceid WHERE d.forename = 'Lucas' AND d.surname = 'di Grassi' AND r.year = 2010

question: I'm writing a recap of the 2017 Italian Grand Prix and want to credit the country of the quickest driver in the second qualifying session. Can you give me the nationality of the driver who set the fastest Q2 lap time in qualifying for the 2017 edition of the Italian Grand Prix? If two or more drivers tied for the fastest Q2 lap time, give me the nationality of each of them. I just need that nationality (or nationalities, in case of a tie), and nothing else.
evidence: Q2: the second of the knockout qualifying sessions of a Grand Prix weekend.
SQL: SELECT t2.nationality FROM qualifying AS t1 INNER JOIN races AS t3 ON t3.raceid = t1.raceid INNER JOIN drivers AS t2 ON t2.driverid = t1.driverid WHERE t3.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND t3.year = 2017 AND NOT t1.q2 IS NULL AND t1.q2 <> '' AND t1.q2 = (SELECT MIN(q2) FROM qualifying WHERE raceid = t1.raceid AND NOT q2 IS NULL AND q2 <> '')

question: I'm writing an article about the Italian Grand Prix and want to know which first names recur among the drivers who finished second in that race. For every forename carried by two or more runners-up of the Italian Grand Prix across all its editions in the data, please give me one row with the forename and the number of runners-up who carried it. Order the rows from the most runners-up to the fewest, and alphabetically by forename when two forenames are tied. Leave out any forename held by only one runner-up.
evidence: A runner-up is the driver who finished second in an edition of the Italian Grand Prix.
SQL: SELECT d.forename AS forename, COUNT(DISTINCT d.driverid) AS runner_ups FROM races AS r INNER JOIN results AS x ON x.raceid = r.raceid INNER JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = x.driverid WHERE r.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND x.position = 2 GROUP BY d.forename HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT d.driverid) > 1 ORDER BY runner_ups DESC NULLS LAST, d.forename NULLS FIRST

question: Who won the 2017 Azerbaijan Grand Prix? I'd like the winner's forename and surname, the local clock time (hours:minutes:seconds.milliseconds) at the circuit at which he crossed the finish line, and the url of his information page, so I can compare the moment the race ended with the TV coverage.
evidence: A driver's race time is the duration from the start of the race to the moment he crosses the finish line.
SQL: SELECT d.forename, d.surname, TO_CHAR(CAST(r.time AS TIME) + CAST('0' || res.time AS INTERVAL), 'HH24:MI:SS') || '.' || RIGHT(CAST(res.time AS TEXT), 3) AS finish_time, d.url FROM races AS r JOIN results AS res ON res.raceid = r.raceid JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = res.driverid WHERE r.year = 2017 AND r.name = 'Azerbaijan Grand Prix' AND res.positionorder = 1

question: For the 2017 Italian Grand Prix, I'd like to identify the drivers who completed the second qualifying session (Q2) but were knocked out and did not reach Q3. Please list every such driver - no ranking, cutoff or tie-break, just all of them - showing each driver's reference name, nationality and birthday, and nothing else.
evidence: Formula 1 qualifying is run in three timed sessions, Q1, Q2 and Q3; completing a session means the driver recorded a lap time in that session, and only drivers who complete a session move on to the next. The reference name is the driver's short identifier.
SQL: SELECT t2.driverref, t2.nationality, t2.dob FROM qualifying AS t1 INNER JOIN drivers AS t2 ON t1.driverid = t2.driverid INNER JOIN races AS r ON t1.raceid = r.raceid WHERE r.year = 2017 AND r.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND NOT t1.q2 IS NULL AND t1.q2 <> '' AND (t1.q3 IS NULL OR t1.q3 = '')

question: For the 2017 Italian Grand Prix qualifying, what is the nationality of the driver with the second fastest Q2 time? Only drivers who took part in Q2 count, and by second fastest I mean the second smallest Q2 time. If several drivers share that time, list each of their nationalities.
evidence: Q2 is the second qualifying session of a Grand Prix weekend, after Q1.
SQL: WITH q2times AS (SELECT d.nationality, q.q2 FROM qualifying AS q JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = q.driverid JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = q.raceid WHERE r.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND r.year = 2017 AND NOT q.q2 IS NULL AND q.q2 <> '') SELECT DISTINCT t.nationality FROM q2times AS t WHERE t.q2 = (SELECT MIN(q2) FROM q2times WHERE q2 > (SELECT MIN(q2) FROM q2times))

question: For qualifying at the 2017 Italian Grand Prix, how many drivers set a time in the second qualifying session (Q2) faster than 1:40.000? I just need the count of drivers as a single number.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT q.driverid) AS driver_count FROM qualifying AS q JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = q.raceid WHERE r.year = 2017 AND r.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND NOT q.q2 IS NULL AND q.q2 <> '' AND q.q2 < '1:40.000'

question: I'm reviewing the longest service pauses in races across the sport's whole history. Which racetrack saw the longest single pit stop ever? Please give me the racetrack name, location, country, the season year of that race, and the pit stop length. Consider all seasons in the data, and if several pit stops tie for the longest, give me one row for each of them.
evidence: pit stop: a recorded pit-stop entry in a race; pit stop length: how long that pit stop lasted
SQL: SELECT c.name AS racetrack, c.location, c.country, r.year AS season_year, ps.duration AS pit_stop_length FROM pitstops AS ps JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = ps.raceid JOIN circuits AS c ON c.circuitid = r.circuitid WHERE ps.milliseconds = (SELECT MAX(milliseconds) FROM pitstops) ORDER BY c.name NULLS FIRST

question: I'm researching the generation of drivers born in the 1980s and want to know how much final-session qualifying that generation actually did as a whole cohort. How many Q3 lap times did a driver born between 1981 and 1991 set on average? Count every driver born in that period in the average, including any who never set a Q3 lap time. Please give me the average rounded to two decimal places.
evidence: Q3: the third and final qualifying session of a race weekend, whose times decide the top starting grid positions.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(COUNT(q.q3 > '' OR NULL) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT d.driverid), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_q3_times_per_driver FROM drivers AS d LEFT JOIN qualifying AS q ON q.driverid = d.driverid WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(d.dob AS TIMESTAMP)) BETWEEN '1981' AND '1991'

question: I'm profiling drivers whose first name alone doesn't identify them. Across all races in the dataset throughout Formula 1 history, how many qualifying 1 times slower than two minutes were set by drivers who share their first name with at least one other driver and who have no code? I want just that single count.
evidence: A driver's code is their three-letter abbreviation (e.g. 'HAM'); having no code means no such abbreviation is on record for them. The qualifying 1 time is the time a driver set in the first qualifying session of a race, one per race they took part in.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM qualifying AS q JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = q.driverid WHERE d.code IS NULL AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM drivers AS o WHERE o.forename = d.forename AND o.driverid <> d.driverid) AND NOT q.q1 IS NULL AND (CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST(q.q1 AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION(':' IN q.q1) - 1)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST(q.q1 AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION(':' IN q.q1) - 1)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END > 2 OR (CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST(q.q1 AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION(':' IN q.q1) - 1)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST(q.q1 AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION(':' IN q.q1) - 1)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END = 2 AND CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST(q.q1 AS TEXT) FROM POSITION(':' IN q.q1) + 1)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST(q.q1 AS TEXT) FROM POSITION(':' IN q.q1) + 1)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END > 0))

question: I'm checking how much of the championship points for drivers named Robert came from races covered by the lap-by-lap timing archive. For every driver whose forename is Robert, I need their reference name and the total points they scored in races where lap-by-lap timing data exists for that driver in that race. The totals should cover all seasons and races on record.
evidence: The reference name is the driver's short identifier, and points are championship points recorded for that driver's race result.
SQL: SELECT d.driverref AS reference_name, COALESCE(SUM(r.points), 0) AS total_points FROM drivers AS d LEFT JOIN results AS r ON r.driverid = d.driverid AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laptimes AS l WHERE l.raceid = r.raceid AND l.driverid = d.driverid) WHERE d.forename = 'Robert' GROUP BY d.driverid, d.driverref ORDER BY total_points DESC NULLS LAST, reference_name NULLS FIRST

question: For every edition of the French Grand Prix from the 1990 season through the most recent edition, I'd like to know which drivers set a fastest lap of the race slower than 90 seconds. For each such driver, give me the date of the edition, the driver's forename and surname, and their fastest lap time of that race in m:ss.mmm form. If several drivers in an edition clear that 90-second mark, list one row per driver. If an edition has no driver over 90 seconds, still show the edition with its date, but no driver or lap time. Please order the rows from the earliest edition date to the latest, and within an edition by driver surname alphabetically - if two drivers share the same fastest-lap time, order them by forename alphabetically.
evidence: A driver's fastest lap in an edition means the shortest time they took to complete any single lap of that race, measured from the start of that lap; the 90-second threshold applies to that fastest lap, not to an average.
SQL: WITH editions AS (SELECT raceid, date FROM races WHERE name = 'French Grand Prix' AND year >= 1990), best AS (SELECT raceid, driverid, MIN(milliseconds) AS best FROM laptimes GROUP BY raceid, driverid) SELECT e.date, d.forename, d.surname, lt.time FROM editions AS e LEFT JOIN best AS b ON b.raceid = e.raceid AND b.best > 90 * 1000 LEFT JOIN laptimes AS lt ON lt.raceid = b.raceid AND lt.driverid = b.driverid AND lt.milliseconds = b.best LEFT JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = b.driverid ORDER BY e.date NULLS FIRST, d.surname NULLS FIRST, d.forename NULLS FIRST

question: I'm putting together a trivia fact about Italian drivers in Formula 1. Who holds the fastest lap time set in Q3 - the third and final part of qualifying - by an Italian driver, across the sport's entire history? Please give me the driver's forename, surname, and the fastest Q3 lap time exactly as it appears in the data. Only consider drivers who have a Q3 lap time recorded for some race, and if several Italian drivers share the exact same fastest Q3 time, list all of them.
evidence: Q3 is the third and final part of qualifying.
SQL: SELECT d.forename, d.surname, q.q3 AS q3_time FROM qualifying AS q JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = q.driverid WHERE d.nationality = 'Italian' AND q.q3 <> '' AND q.q3 = (SELECT MIN(q2.q3) FROM qualifying AS q2 JOIN drivers AS d2 ON d2.driverid = q2.driverid WHERE d2.nationality = 'Italian' AND q2.q3 > '')

question: I'm writing a piece on the new generation of British Formula 1 talent. Among British F1 drivers born after 1980, who set the fastest Q3 qualifying time, what was that time, and at which race and in which year was it set? Please give me the driver's full name, the race name, the race year, and the Q3 time. By 'born after 1980' I mean the year of birth is later than 1980. If two qualifying results tie for the fastest Q3 time, I'd like a row for each.
evidence: Q3 is the final part of the qualifying session that decides the front of the starting grid.
SQL: WITH cohort AS (SELECT q.driverid, q.raceid, q.q3 FROM drivers AS d JOIN qualifying AS q ON d.driverid = q.driverid WHERE d.nationality = 'British' AND CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(d.dob AS TIMESTAMP))) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(d.dob AS TIMESTAMP))) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END > 1980 AND NOT q.q3 IS NULL AND TRIM(CAST(q.q3 AS TEXT)) <> '') SELECT d.forename || ' ' || d.surname AS driver_name, r.name AS race_name, r.year AS race_year, c.q3 AS q3_time FROM cohort AS c JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = c.driverid JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = c.raceid WHERE c.q3 = (SELECT MIN(q3) FROM cohort)

question: We're writing a piece on F1's younger generation and want a number for it: how many drivers born in 1976 or later (born from 1 January 1976 onwards) have ever set the second-fastest lap of a race at any point in the history covered by the data? I just need the single count of such drivers.
evidence: By second-fastest lap of a race I mean the driver's own fastest lap in that race was the second quickest among all drivers in that race.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t1.driverid) AS driver_count FROM results AS t1 INNER JOIN drivers AS t2 ON t1.driverid = t2.driverid WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(t2.dob AS TIMESTAMP)) >= '1976' AND t1.rank = 2

question: Who set the fastest time in Q3 (the final qualifying session) at the 2017 Italian Grand Prix? Please give me the driver's reference name (the short identifier like 'hamilton') as the result. If two drivers set the same fastest Q3 time, give me both of their reference names.
evidence: Q3: the final qualifying session of a Grand Prix weekend
SQL: SELECT d.driverref FROM qualifying AS q JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = q.driverid JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = q.raceid WHERE r.year = 2017 AND r.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND NOT q.q3 IS NULL AND q.q3 <> '' AND q.q3 = (SELECT MIN(q3) FROM qualifying WHERE raceid = q.raceid AND NOT q3 IS NULL AND q3 <> '')

question: Can you rank the Italian Formula 1 constructors by career points and give me the three highest-placed ones? For each, I'd like the constructor name, their career points, and their introduction website. Career points means the total of the points the constructor finished each season with (a season being one calendar year of racing). Constructors with no points still count, ranked with 0. If there are ties, they share a rank and the next rank is skipped (so 1, 1, 3), and I'd like every constructor within the top three ranks returned.
SQL: WITH season AS (SELECT cs.constructorid, cs.points, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY cs.constructorid, r.year ORDER BY cs.raceid DESC NULLS LAST) AS rn FROM constructorstandings AS cs JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = cs.raceid), career AS (SELECT constructorid, SUM(points) AS pts FROM season WHERE rn = 1 GROUP BY constructorid), ranked AS (SELECT c.name, COALESCE(cr.pts, 0) AS pts, c.url, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(cr.pts, 0) DESC NULLS LAST) AS rnk FROM constructors AS c LEFT JOIN career AS cr ON cr.constructorid = c.constructorid WHERE c.nationality = 'Italian') SELECT name, pts, url FROM ranked WHERE rnk <= 3 ORDER BY rnk NULLS FIRST, pts DESC NULLS LAST, name NULLS FIRST

question: I'm writing a piece about how the same common forenames recur across Formula 1 history. Could you tell me how many different drivers named Peter have ever won a Formula 1 race, and the same for drivers named John? Please give me one count per forename, so I can compare the two — if they turn out to be equal, just report both counts side by side. Nothing else needed.
evidence: A race win means the driver finished first in that race.
SQL: SELECT t1.forename, COUNT(DISTINCT t1.driverid) AS winner_drivers FROM drivers AS t1 INNER JOIN results AS t2 ON t2.driverid = t1.driverid WHERE t2.positionorder = 1 AND t1.forename IN ('John', 'Peter') GROUP BY t1.forename ORDER BY t1.forename NULLS FIRST

question: I'm working on a story about qualifying records. Across all races, which driver set the fastest time in Q3 (the final part of qualifying)? I'd like the nationality of that driver - and if more than one driver shares the fastest Q3 time, please give me every such driver's nationality. I don't need anything else, just the nationality or nationalities.
evidence: Q3: the third and final part of the qualifying session.
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT d.nationality FROM qualifying AS q JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = q.driverid WHERE TRIM(CAST(q.q3 AS TEXT)) = (SELECT MIN(q3) FROM qualifying WHERE NOT q3 IS NULL AND TRIM(CAST(q3 AS TEXT)) <> '')

question: I'm putting together a historical note on constructor nationalities in Formula 1. For each constructor nationality, how many constructors from that nationality have recorded the fastest lap of a race? Please include every nationality in the result, with a count of 0 for nationalities where no constructor has done so. Count a constructor only when it is officially credited with the quickest single lap time in a race's recorded result - don't compute lap times yourself.
evidence: Fastest lap: the constructor officially credited with the quickest single lap time in a race's recorded result.
SQL: SELECT c.nationality, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN r.rank = 1 THEN c.constructorid END) AS num_constructors FROM constructors AS c LEFT JOIN results AS r ON c.constructorid = r.constructorid GROUP BY c.nationality ORDER BY num_constructors DESC NULLS LAST, c.nationality NULLS FIRST

question: I'm studying how pit stop activity changed across the refuelling-rule change for Australia's F1 drivers. For each season from 2002 through 2013, can you give me the total number of pit stops made at the races of that season where, after the race, at least one Australian driver was placed better than 20th in the driver standings? I'd like the season year and the total pit stop count for each season. The pit stop total should cover every driver who pitted at those races, not just the Australian drivers.
evidence: Better than 20th in the driver standings means a position of 1 through 19 after that race. A pit stop is any recorded pit stop made by any driver at the race.
SQL: WITH oz_races AS (SELECT DISTINCT r.raceid, r.year FROM races AS r INNER JOIN driverstandings AS ds ON ds.raceid = r.raceid INNER JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = ds.driverid WHERE d.nationality = 'Australian' AND ds.position <= 19 AND r.year BETWEEN 2002 AND 2013) SELECT oz.year AS season, COUNT(ps.stop) AS pit_stops FROM oz_races AS oz LEFT JOIN pitstops AS ps ON ps.raceid = oz.raceid GROUP BY oz.year ORDER BY oz.year NULLS FIRST

question: For the 1995 season (races held in the calendar year 1995), how many drivers set a Q1 lap time of more than two minutes - i.e., strictly longer than 2:00.000? I just need the number of drivers.
evidence: Q1: the first of the qualifying sessions; a Q1 time is the lap time a driver set in that session.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t1.driverid) FROM qualifying AS t1 INNER JOIN races AS t2 ON t2.raceid = t1.raceid WHERE t2.year = 1995 AND (LENGTH(CAST(t1.q1 AS TEXT)) > LENGTH(CAST('2:00.000' AS TEXT)) OR t1.q1 > '2:00.000')

question: For my monthly recap I need the fastest pit stop made during any F1 race held in September 2016. Please tell me the driver's full name, the pit stop time, the name of the race where it happened, the circuit name, and the circuit location. If two or more pit stops share the fastest time, list each of them with its own driver, race, circuit name and circuit location.
evidence: By pit stop time I mean the elapsed time of a pit stop, from the car arriving at its pit to rejoining the race.
SQL: WITH scope AS (SELECT ps.driverid, ps.duration, ps.milliseconds, r.raceid FROM pitstops AS ps JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = ps.raceid WHERE r.date >= '2016-09-01' AND r.date < '2016-10-01') SELECT d.forename || ' ' || d.surname AS driver_name, s.duration AS pit_stop_time, r.name AS race_name, c.name AS circuit_name, c.location AS circuit_location FROM scope AS s JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = s.driverid JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = s.raceid JOIN circuits AS c ON c.circuitid = r.circuitid WHERE s.milliseconds = (SELECT MIN(milliseconds) FROM scope)

question: I'm profiling the oldest driver ever to win a Formula 1 race. Please identify the winning driver with the earliest date of birth - if two winning drivers share that birth date, use the one whose full name (forename then surname) comes first alphabetically. For that driver, return his full name (forename then surname), his nationality, the name and date of the first race he won (the earliest date; if two of his wins share that date, the one whose race name comes first alphabetically), and the total number of races he started over his entire career. A win means finishing in position 1 in a race. The career covers every race in the database, from 1950 through 2017. Return a single row.
evidence: Grand Prix: any race event in the database, whatever its name is; some race names do not contain the words 'Grand Prix'.
SQL: WITH winner AS (SELECT d.driverid, d.forename, d.surname, d.nationality FROM drivers AS d WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM results AS res WHERE res.driverid = d.driverid AND res.position = 1) ORDER BY d.dob ASC NULLS FIRST, d.forename ASC NULLS FIRST, d.surname ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1) SELECT w.forename || ' ' || w.surname AS full_name, w.nationality, (SELECT r.name FROM results AS res JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = res.raceid WHERE res.driverid = w.driverid AND res.position = 1 ORDER BY r.date ASC NULLS FIRST, r.name ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1) AS first_win_race, (SELECT r.date FROM results AS res JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = res.raceid WHERE res.driverid = w.driverid AND res.position = 1 ORDER BY r.date ASC NULLS FIRST, r.name ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1) AS first_win_date, (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT res.raceid) FROM results AS res WHERE res.driverid = w.driverid) AS races_started FROM winner AS w

question: Across the history of the Canadian Grand Prix, how many runnings of the race have had at least one car retire with an accident? Please note that a crash in which the driver was killed is recorded as its own status and should not count as an accident here. I just need the single number of runnings, nothing else.
evidence: accident: a car's race ends because of a crash
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t1.raceid) FROM results AS t1 INNER JOIN races AS t2 ON t1.raceid = t2.raceid INNER JOIN status AS t3 ON t1.statusid = t3.statusid WHERE t3.status = 'Accident' AND t2.name = 'Canadian Grand Prix'

question: For the 2017 Italian Grand Prix, which driver set the second-fastest time in the second qualifying session (Q2), and which constructor did he drive for that weekend? By second-fastest I mean the driver whose Q2 time comes next after the quickest one, counting every driver who took part in that session. If two drivers tie on Q2 time, the one who started the race higher up the grid counts as the faster of the two. Please give me the driver's forename, the driver's surname, and the constructor name.
evidence: Q2: the second of the weekend's qualifying sessions; its times are measured to the thousandth of a second.
SQL: WITH t AS (SELECT d.driverid, d.forename, d.surname, co.name AS constructor, q.q2, q.position, CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST(q.q2 AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION(':' IN q.q2) - 1)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST(q.q2 AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION(':' IN q.q2) - 1)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END AS mins, CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST(q.q2 AS TEXT) FROM POSITION(':' IN q.q2) + 1)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST(q.q2 AS TEXT) FROM POSITION(':' IN q.q2) + 1)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END AS secs FROM qualifying AS q JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = q.raceid JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = q.driverid JOIN constructors AS co ON co.constructorid = q.constructorid WHERE r.year = 2017 AND r.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND NOT q.q2 IS NULL AND q.q2 <> '') SELECT forename, surname, constructor FROM t ORDER BY mins ASC NULLS FIRST, secs ASC NULLS FIRST, position ASC NULLS FIRST, driverid ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1

question: I'm writing a season review piece and need the outright quickest Q2 time of the 2017 Formula One season – the fastest single Q2 time set at any race that year. Please give me the surname of the driver who set it and the name of the race where it was set. If two drivers share that fastest Q2 time, list every one of them along with the race names.
evidence: Q2: the second of the three qualifying sessions of a Grand Prix weekend.
SQL: WITH t AS (SELECT d.surname AS surname, r.name AS race_name, q.driverid AS driverid, q.q2 AS q2 FROM qualifying AS q JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = q.driverid JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = q.raceid WHERE r.year = 2017 AND CAST(q.q2 AS TEXT) LIKE '%:%.%'), m AS (SELECT MIN(q2) AS q2 FROM t) SELECT t.surname, t.race_name FROM t JOIN m ON m.q2 = t.q2 ORDER BY t.driverid ASC NULLS FIRST

question: I'm writing a race report and need to name the pole-sitter by their permanent race number. Who set the fastest Q3 qualifying time at the 2017 Italian Grand Prix (the race named 'Italian Grand Prix' in the 2017 season)? Please give me just that driver's permanent number. If two or more drivers share that fastest time, give me the numbers of all of them and nothing else.
evidence: Q3 is the final part of qualifying, whose times decide the top starting positions; the fastest Q3 time earns pole position.
SQL: SELECT d.number FROM qualifying AS q JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = q.raceid JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = q.driverid WHERE r.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND r.year = 2017 AND NOT q.q3 IS NULL AND q.q3 <> '' AND q.q3 = (SELECT MIN(q2.q3) FROM qualifying AS q2 JOIN races AS r2 ON r2.raceid = q2.raceid WHERE r2.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND r2.year = 2017 AND NOT q2.q3 IS NULL AND q2.q3 <> '')

question: For the 2017 Italian Grand Prix, who set the fastest lap time in Q3 (the final qualifying session), and what was that time? Give me the driver code along with the fastest Q3 time. If two or more drivers tie for the fastest Q3 time, list every tied driver.
evidence: Q3: the third and final qualifying session; a driver's Q3 time is the lap time that driver set in that session
SQL: SELECT t2.code, t1.q3 FROM qualifying AS t1 INNER JOIN drivers AS t2 ON t2.driverid = t1.driverid WHERE t1.raceid = (SELECT raceid FROM races WHERE year = 2017 AND name = 'Italian Grand Prix') AND t1.q3 <> '' AND t1.q3 = (SELECT MIN(q3) FROM qualifying WHERE raceid = (SELECT raceid FROM races WHERE year = 2017 AND name = 'Italian Grand Prix') AND q3 <> '')

question: I'm writing a report on the 2017 Italian Grand Prix (the one held in the 2017 season). Could you tell me the nationality of the driver who set the fastest time in Q3, the final part of qualifying? If several drivers share the same fastest Q3 time, please give each of their nationalities.
evidence: Q3 is the third and final part of the qualifying session.
SQL: SELECT d.nationality FROM qualifying AS q JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = q.raceid JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = q.driverid WHERE r.year = 2017 AND r.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND NOT q.q3 IS NULL AND q.q3 <> '' AND q.q3 = (SELECT MIN(q2.q3) FROM qualifying AS q2 JOIN races AS r2 ON r2.raceid = q2.raceid WHERE r2.year = 2017 AND r2.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND NOT q2.q3 IS NULL AND q2.q3 <> '')

question: Which Chinese Grand Prix edition from the 2000s (2000–2009 seasons) had the earliest scheduled local start time? Give me the season year of that edition and the runner-up's time gap to the winner (the runner-up being the driver classified second at the finish). If several editions share the earliest scheduled local start time, use the most recent one.
evidence: Scheduled local start time: the time of day the race was scheduled to start, local to the circuit.
SQL: SELECT r.year, res.time AS runner_up_gap FROM races AS r JOIN results AS res ON res.raceid = r.raceid WHERE r.name = 'Chinese Grand Prix' AND r.year BETWEEN 2000 AND 2009 AND res.positionorder = 2 AND NOT r.time IS NULL AND r.time = (SELECT MIN(r2.time) FROM races AS r2 WHERE r2.name = 'Chinese Grand Prix' AND r2.year BETWEEN 2000 AND 2009 AND NOT r2.time IS NULL) ORDER BY r.year DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1

question: I'm writing a qualifying report. Can you give me the driver codes of all drivers who set a time in the third qualifying session at the 2017 Italian Grand Prix? One row per driver who set such a time, and please list the codes in alphabetical order. Nothing else needed.
evidence: The third qualifying session is the final segment of the race weekend's qualifying, in which only the fastest drivers take part.
SQL: SELECT d.code FROM qualifying AS q JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = q.raceid JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = q.driverid WHERE r.year = 2017 AND r.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND NOT q.q3 IS NULL AND q.q3 <> '' ORDER BY d.code NULLS FIRST

question: I'm writing about how the Canadian Grand Prix moved to early-evening starts. Could you find the editions of the Canadian Grand Prix from 2007 through 2017 (both years included) that began at 17:00 local time or earlier - a race that began exactly at 17:00 counts. For each one, give me the race year, the winner's forename, the winner's surname, and the winner's finish time. The winner is the single driver classified first at the finish. Nothing else, please.
evidence: An edition is one running of the Canadian Grand Prix in a given year; local start time is the clock time of day, local to the circuit, at which the race began, on the 24-hour clock.
SQL: SELECT r.year, d.forename, d.surname, res.time AS finish_time FROM races AS r JOIN results AS res ON res.raceid = r.raceid AND res.positionorder = 1 JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = res.driverid WHERE r.name = 'Canadian Grand Prix' AND r.year BETWEEN 2007 AND 2017 AND CAST(r.time AS TIME) <= TIME '17:00' ORDER BY r.year NULLS FIRST

question: I'm writing a retrospective on the 2017 Italian Grand Prix at Monza. For the Q3 session of that race's qualifying, can you give me the permanent career race number and surname of every driver whose Q3 lap time was strictly faster than 1 minute 38.000 seconds? I want all drivers under that mark, not just the fastest, and no particular order. Note that by permanent career race number I mean the number a driver carries throughout his career, not a one-off entry number for that weekend.
evidence: Q3 is the third and final qualifying session; a driver only has a Q3 time if he actually took part in that session.
SQL: WITH mark(t) AS (SELECT '1' || ':' || '38.000') SELECT d.number, d.surname FROM qualifying AS q INNER JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = q.raceid INNER JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = q.driverid WHERE r.year = 2017 AND r.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND CAST(q.q3 AS TEXT) LIKE '%:%' AND q.q3 < (SELECT t FROM mark) ORDER BY d.number NULLS FIRST

question: Across all seasons in the database, which circuit's Grand Prix started earliest in the day, and which started latest? I'd like the circuit reference name of the earliest one, the circuit reference name of the latest one, and the gap between those two start times in seconds. Include every season, and if several circuits share the earliest start time, list them all - same for the latest.
evidence: By "start time of the day" I mean the local clock time at the venue at which the race started.
SQL: WITH per_circuit AS (SELECT c.circuitref AS circuitref, MIN(CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM CAST(r.time AS TIME))) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM CAST(r.time AS TIME))) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END) AS earliest_start_seconds, MAX(CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM CAST(r.time AS TIME))) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM CAST(r.time AS TIME))) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END) AS latest_start_seconds FROM races AS r JOIN circuits AS c ON c.circuitid = r.circuitid WHERE NOT r.time IS NULL GROUP BY c.circuitref) SELECT STRING_AGG(circuitref, ', ') AS earliest_circuitref, (SELECT STRING_AGG(circuitref, ', ') FROM per_circuit WHERE latest_start_seconds = (SELECT MAX(latest_start_seconds) FROM per_circuit)) AS latest_circuitref, (SELECT MAX(latest_start_seconds) - MIN(earliest_start_seconds) FROM per_circuit) AS gap_seconds FROM per_circuit WHERE earliest_start_seconds = (SELECT MIN(earliest_start_seconds) FROM per_circuit)

question: I'm looking into fastest race laps recorded by drivers born in the 1980s. Can you tell me which three drivers born between 1980 and 1990 reached the highest single fastest-lap speed at any point in their career? I'd like their first and last names, ranked from the highest career-high speed down, and if two drivers are tied on that speed, list the one born earlier first, and then the one whose last name comes first alphabetically. Please give me just the three names, nothing else.
evidence: Fastest lap speed: the average speed, in km/h, that a driver recorded on their single fastest lap of a race. A driver's career-high speed is based on that one lap, not an average across their laps.
SQL: SELECT d.forename, d.surname FROM drivers AS d JOIN results AS r ON r.driverid = d.driverid WHERE SUBSTRING(CAST(d.dob AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) BETWEEN '1980' AND '1990' AND NOT r.fastestlapspeed IS NULL GROUP BY d.driverid, d.forename, d.surname, d.dob ORDER BY MAX(CASE WHEN (r.fastestlapspeed) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((r.fastestlapspeed) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END) DESC NULLS LAST, d.dob NULLS FIRST, d.surname NULLS FIRST LIMIT 3

question: For the 2017 Italian Grand Prix, I need the list of drivers who were eliminated after the first qualifying session. Give me one row per eliminated driver with their reference name, ordered by their first-segment time from slowest to fastest. If two eliminated drivers have the same first-segment time, list the one with the lower driverId first.
evidence: Eliminated after the first qualifying session means the driver took part in qualifying but did not go out in the second qualifying session.
SQL: SELECT d.driverref FROM qualifying AS q JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = q.raceid JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = q.driverid WHERE r.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND r.year = 2017 AND NOT q.q1 IS NULL AND (q.q2 IS NULL OR q.q2 = '') ORDER BY q.q1 DESC NULLS LAST, d.driverid NULLS FIRST

question: For my retrospective on the 1962 British Grand Prix – the race named 'British Grand Prix' in the 1962 season – how many drivers withdrew from that race? I just need a single whole number.
evidence: A driver who withdrew from a race is recorded with the status 'Withdrew'.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT x.driverid) AS num_withdrawn_drivers FROM results AS x JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = x.raceid JOIN status AS s ON s.statusid = x.statusid WHERE r.name = 'British Grand Prix' AND r.year = 1962 AND s.status = 'Withdrew'

question: For the 1957 British Grand Prix, what percentage of the drivers who took part in the race were classified finishers, rounded to two decimals? By classified finisher I mean a driver whose race record shows them finishing the race, whether on the lead lap or one or more laps behind the winner. I just need the one percentage figure.
evidence: classified finisher: a driver whose race record shows them finishing the race, whether on the lead lap or one or more laps behind the winner
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN NOT x.position IS NULL THEN x.driverid END) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT x.driverid), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS finisher_percentage FROM races AS r JOIN results AS x ON x.raceid = r.raceid WHERE r.year = 1957 AND r.name = 'British Grand Prix'

question: What was Elijah Allen's mean total expense per event for expenses dated in September or October? Round to two decimals.
SQL: WITH per_event AS (SELECT b.link_to_event, SUM(e.cost) AS event_spend FROM expense AS e JOIN member AS m ON m.member_id = e.link_to_member JOIN budget AS b ON b.budget_id = e.link_to_budget WHERE m.first_name = 'Elijah' AND m.last_name = 'Allen' AND SUBSTRING(CAST(e.expense_date AS TEXT) FROM 6 FOR 2) IN ('09', '10') AND NOT b.link_to_event IS NULL GROUP BY b.link_to_event) SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(event_spend) AS DECIMAL), 2) FROM per_event

question: What is the total amount spent on Student Club events in 2019 minus the total spent on events in 2020?
SQL: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN SUBSTRING(CAST(t1.event_date AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) = '2019' THEN t2.spent ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN SUBSTRING(CAST(t1.event_date AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) = '2020' THEN t2.spent ELSE 0 END) AS num FROM event AS t1 INNER JOIN budget AS t2 ON t1.event_id = t2.link_to_event

question: What note was recorded for the fundraising proceeds received on September 14, 2019?
SQL: SELECT notes FROM income WHERE source = 'Fundraising' AND date_received = '2019-09-14'

question: What is the ratio of the Advertisement budget for the Yearly Kickoff meeting to that for the October Meeting?
SQL: SELECT CASE WHEN (SUM(CASE WHEN t2.event_name = 'Yearly Kickoff' THEN t1.amount ELSE 0 END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(CASE WHEN t2.event_name = 'Yearly Kickoff' THEN t1.amount ELSE 0 END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN t2.event_name = 'October Meeting' THEN t1.amount ELSE 0 END), 0) FROM budget AS t1 INNER JOIN event AS t2 ON t1.link_to_event = t2.event_id WHERE t1.category = 'Advertisement' AND t2.type = 'Meeting'

question: Which closed events are tied for the highest ratio of total spending to total budget amount?
SQL: WITH ratios AS (SELECT e.event_id, e.event_name, CAST(SUM(b.spent) AS DECIMAL(20, 4)) / NULLIF(NULLIF(SUM(b.amount), 0), 0) AS ratio FROM event AS e JOIN budget AS b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE e.status = 'Closed' GROUP BY e.event_id, e.event_name HAVING SUM(b.amount) > 0) SELECT event_name FROM ratios WHERE ratio = (SELECT MAX(ratio) FROM ratios)

question: List the name of students that have attended more than 7 events.
SQL: SELECT t1.first_name, t1.last_name FROM member AS t1 INNER JOIN attendance AS t2 ON t1.member_id = t2.link_to_member GROUP BY t2.link_to_member, t1.first_name, t1.last_name HAVING COUNT(t2.link_to_event) > 7

question: Which members incurred at least one expense above the overall average expense cost? Give each member's first name, last name, and phone number as separate fields.
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT t3.first_name, t3.last_name, t3.phone FROM expense AS t1 INNER JOIN budget AS t2 ON t1.link_to_budget = t2.budget_id INNER JOIN member AS t3 ON t3.member_id = t1.link_to_member WHERE t1.cost > (SELECT AVG(t1.cost) FROM expense AS t1 INNER JOIN budget AS t2 ON t1.link_to_budget = t2.budget_id INNER JOIN member AS t3 ON t3.member_id = t1.link_to_member)

question: I'm putting together a review of last fall's activities and want to see how the Women's Soccer game compared to a typical event that semester. Please give me one row with: the number of students who attended the Women's Soccer event, the average number of students who attended events held in fall 2019 rounded to one decimal place, and a verdict of 'more', 'fewer' or 'equal' comparing the Women's Soccer head count to that average. Fall 2019 means events from 1 September 2019 through 30 November 2019 inclusive, and every event that semester counts toward the average even if nobody attended it. The verdict should compare the Women's Soccer head count to the rounded average: above it is 'more', below is 'fewer', exactly equal is 'equal'.
evidence: Women's Soccer is an event name; attendance at an event is the number of members who attended it.
SQL: WITH fall_events AS (SELECT e.event_id, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM attendance AS a WHERE a.link_to_event = e.event_id) AS attendees FROM event AS e WHERE e.event_date >= '2019-09-01' AND e.event_date < '2019-12-01'), agg AS (SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(attendees) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS avg_att FROM fall_events), soccer AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS head_count FROM attendance AS a JOIN event AS e ON e.event_id = a.link_to_event WHERE e.event_name = 'Women''s Soccer') SELECT s.head_count AS soccer_attendance, g.avg_att AS average_attendance, CASE WHEN s.head_count > g.avg_att THEN 'more' WHEN s.head_count < g.avg_att THEN 'fewer' ELSE 'equal' END AS verdict FROM soccer AS s CROSS JOIN agg AS g

question: I'm reviewing our roster against the catalog and want to see how much of the College of Humanities and Social Sciences' coverage our members actually hold, department by department. For each department in that college, give me: the department's name, the majors it offers, the majors held by at least one of our members, and the average members per major it offers, rounded to two decimals. Membership is as currently listed in the member records, and count a department as belonging to the college when any of its majors sits in the college.
evidence: College of Humanities and Social Sciences: one of the colleges that houses departments offering majors.
SQL: SELECT m.department, COUNT(DISTINCT m.major_id) AS majors_offered, COUNT(DISTINCT mem.link_to_major) AS majors_held, ROUND(CAST(1.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT mem.member_id) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT m.major_id), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_members_per_major FROM major AS m LEFT JOIN member AS mem ON mem.link_to_major = m.major_id WHERE m.college = 'College of Humanities and Social Sciences' GROUP BY m.department

question: I'm putting together our yearly report and need a breakdown of our 2019 events by event type. For each type of event we held in 2019, please give me: the event type, how many members attended that type's events during 2019, and the total amount budgeted for that type's events in dollars. A few notes: 2019 means the calendar year; the budgeted amount is the planned amount, not what was actually spent. If nothing was budgeted for a type's events, or no member attended them, just show zero. Please list one row per event type, in alphabetical order by event type.
SQL: SELECT e.type AS event_type, (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) FROM attendance AS a JOIN event AS e2 ON e2.event_id = a.link_to_event WHERE e2.type = e.type AND SUBSTRING(CAST(e2.event_date AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) = '2019') AS members_who_attended, CASE WHEN (COALESCE((SELECT SUM(b.amount) FROM budget AS b JOIN event AS e3 ON e3.event_id = b.link_to_event WHERE e3.type = e.type AND SUBSTRING(CAST(e3.event_date AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) = '2019'), 0)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((COALESCE((SELECT SUM(b.amount) FROM budget AS b JOIN event AS e3 ON e3.event_id = b.link_to_event WHERE e3.type = e.type AND SUBSTRING(CAST(e3.event_date AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) = '2019'), 0)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END AS total_budgeted FROM event AS e WHERE SUBSTRING(CAST(e.event_date AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) = '2019' GROUP BY e.type ORDER BY e.type NULLS FIRST

question: I'm putting together a financial overview for the college that houses the Electrical and Computer Engineering Department. For each department of that college, can you tell me the total dues the club actually received from that department's enrolled members who took part in the club's events, in dollars? Please include every department of the college, showing zero if we received no such dues from it. Just the department name and the total dues per department.
evidence: 'Dues' is the income source label for membership dues a member pays to the club; 'Member' is the club position of an enrolled member, as opposed to officer or inactive positions.
SQL: SELECT m.department, COALESCE(SUM(i.amount), 0) AS total_dues_received FROM major AS m LEFT JOIN member AS mb ON mb.link_to_major = m.major_id AND mb.position = 'Member' LEFT JOIN income AS i ON i.link_to_member = mb.member_id AND i.source = 'Dues' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM attendance AS a WHERE a.link_to_member = mb.member_id) WHERE m.college IN (SELECT college FROM major WHERE department = 'Electrical and Computer Engineering Department') GROUP BY m.department ORDER BY m.department NULLS FIRST

question: For the mid-year budget review: I need to see, for each member who had to spend more than fifty dollars on an expense, how much room was still left in the budget lines those purchases were charged against. Please give me, per member, their first name, last name, and the total amount left across those budget lines in dollars rounded to two decimals. Order the results from the largest total down to the smallest; if two members have the same total, list them alphabetically by last name and then first name. The totals should cover all expenses on record, and if a budget line ended up overdrawn, its negative remaining amount should count toward the total.
evidence: Spending more than fifty dollars on an expense means the expense's dollar cost is over 50. The amount left in a budget line is the amount budgeted for that line minus the amount spent against it.
SQL: SELECT m.first_name, m.last_name, ROUND(CAST(SUM(b.remaining) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS remaining_total FROM member AS m JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT link_to_member, link_to_budget FROM expense WHERE cost > 50) AS e ON e.link_to_member = m.member_id JOIN budget AS b ON b.budget_id = e.link_to_budget GROUP BY m.member_id, m.first_name, m.last_name ORDER BY remaining_total DESC NULLS LAST, m.last_name ASC NULLS FIRST, m.first_name ASC NULLS FIRST

question: I'm putting together our year-end budget summary. How much did we collect in membership dues, in total dollars, from the students who attended the Football game? Membership dues are the payments recorded under the source 'Dues'.
evidence: membership dues: payments recorded under the source 'Dues'
SQL: SELECT SUM(i.amount) AS total_dues FROM income AS i WHERE i.source = 'Dues' AND i.link_to_member IN (SELECT a.link_to_member FROM attendance AS a INNER JOIN event AS e ON a.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE e.event_name = 'Football game')

question: How many majors offered by the college that offers Tyler Hewitt's major currently have no enrolled members in the club? Count every major that college offers, by major name.
evidence: Enrolled members are the people recorded in the club's membership list.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS num_majors_without_members FROM major AS m WHERE m.college = (SELECT t2.college FROM member AS t1 INNER JOIN major AS t2 ON t1.link_to_major = t2.major_id WHERE t1.first_name = 'Tyler' AND t1.last_name = 'Hewitt') AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM member AS mm WHERE mm.link_to_major = m.major_id)

question: For our end-of-year report, I need one figure: the average number of members who attended each event that carried a budget line for advertising, covering every such event across the club's records regardless of when it took place. Please give it as a single number rounded to two decimal places.
evidence: A budget line for advertising means a budget entry whose category is advertising.
SQL: WITH att AS (SELECT link_to_event, COUNT(DISTINCT link_to_member) AS members FROM attendance GROUP BY link_to_event) SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(COALESCE(att.members, 0)) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS average_attendance FROM event AS t1 INNER JOIN budget AS t2 ON t2.link_to_event = t1.event_id AND t2.category = 'Advertisement' LEFT JOIN att ON att.link_to_event = t1.event_id

question: For every budget review event the club has held, can you give me the event name, its location, and the number of members who attended? I need this for the year-end report.
evidence: 'Budget' is the club's event type for its budget review events, such as the Fall Budget Review and the Spring Budget Review.
SQL: SELECT e.event_name, e.location, COUNT(a.link_to_member) AS attended FROM event AS e LEFT JOIN attendance AS a ON e.event_id = a.link_to_event WHERE e.type = 'Budget' GROUP BY e.event_id, e.event_name, e.location

question: I'm planning study-partner pairings around our biggest social-attendance event. Can you tell me which academic majors were most represented among the members who attended the football game? For each major, give me the major name and the number of attendees in that major. If several majors tie for the highest attendee count, list all of them, ordered alphabetically by major name.
evidence: Football game: the event named 'Football game'
SQL: WITH cnt AS (SELECT mj.major_name AS major_name, COUNT(DISTINCT m.member_id) AS attendees FROM event AS e JOIN attendance AS a ON a.link_to_event = e.event_id JOIN member AS m ON m.member_id = a.link_to_member JOIN major AS mj ON mj.major_id = m.link_to_major WHERE e.event_name = 'Football game' GROUP BY mj.major_id, mj.major_name) SELECT major_name, attendees FROM cnt WHERE attendees = (SELECT MAX(attendees) FROM cnt) ORDER BY major_name NULLS FIRST

question: I want to gauge how much of the university's range of academic programs our club is failing to reach. Out of every major offered by the university - including majors where we have no members - what percentage have no club member studying them? Please give me just that single percentage, between 0 and 100, rounded to two decimal places.
evidence: Major: an academic program offered by the university, as listed in the club's records of majors.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(CASE WHEN ((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM major AS m WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM member AS mem WHERE mem.link_to_major = m.major_id))) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST(((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM major AS m WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM member AS mem WHERE mem.link_to_major = m.major_id))) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END * 100 / NULLIF((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM major), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS percentage

question: Our officer team wants to settle a debate about whether we pull more weight than the rest of the club, so we need the attendance numbers before the next meeting. Could you tell us two things: the average number of events attended per officer, and the average number of events attended per other student, each rounded to two decimal places? To be clear on who counts where: officers are the members holding the position of President, Vice President, Secretary, or Treasurer, and everyone else in the club counts as an other student. Each average should cover every member of its group, and include every event in the club's records - there's no date cutoff.
SQL: WITH t AS (SELECT m.member_id, m.position, COUNT(a.link_to_event) AS cnt FROM member AS m LEFT JOIN attendance AS a ON a.link_to_member = m.member_id GROUP BY m.member_id, m.position) SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(CASE WHEN t.position IN ('President', 'Vice President', 'Secretary', 'Treasurer') THEN t.cnt END) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS officer_avg, ROUND(CAST(AVG(CASE WHEN NOT t.position IN ('President', 'Vice President', 'Secretary', 'Treasurer') THEN t.cnt END) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS other_students_avg FROM t

question: I'm finalizing the semester wrap-up report and need one number: how many different kinds of things the club bought for events that went over budget this semester. A few things to keep in mind: an event counts as over budget if, in at least one of its budgeted categories, we spent more than we budgeted for that category - the budgeted amount minus what was actually spent came out below zero. Also, a single purchase can cover several kinds of things at once, and the purchase description lists what it bought, so make sure each kind is counted. The answer should cover the whole semester shown in the records, and I just need the single integer count, nothing else.
evidence: went over budget: a budgeted category of the event ended with more spent than was budgeted for it, i.e. the amount budgeted minus the amount spent is below zero; kind of thing: a type of item bought, like water, pizza or posters
SQL: WITH RECURSIVE over_budget_events AS (SELECT DISTINCT link_to_event FROM budget WHERE amount - spent < 0), purchases AS (SELECT ex.expense_description AS d FROM expense AS ex JOIN budget AS b ON ex.link_to_budget = b.budget_id WHERE b.link_to_event IN (SELECT link_to_event FROM over_budget_events)), items(item, rest) AS (SELECT TRIM(CAST(SUBSTRING(CAST(d || ',' AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION(',' IN d || ',') - 1) AS TEXT)), SUBSTRING(CAST(d || ',' AS TEXT) FROM POSITION(',' IN d || ',') + 1) FROM purchases UNION ALL SELECT TRIM(CAST(SUBSTRING(CAST(rest AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION(',' IN rest) - 1) AS TEXT)), SUBSTRING(CAST(rest AS TEXT) FROM POSITION(',' IN rest) + 1) FROM items WHERE rest <> '') SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT LOWER(item)) AS kinds FROM items WHERE item <> ''

question: For every event in our records that had at least one attendee, I need the amount spent per attendee on bottled drinking water, in dollars and cents rounded to two decimals. Give me one row per event with the event name and that amount; if an attended event had no water purchases, show 0.00, and if two events share a name, list them separately. Include all events regardless of status, across the club's entire history. A purchase that included water along with other items counts fully toward water.
evidence: water: bottled drinking water bought for attendees
SQL: WITH water AS (SELECT b.link_to_event AS event_id, SUM(e.cost) AS total_cost FROM expense AS e JOIN budget AS b ON e.link_to_budget = b.budget_id WHERE CAST(e.expense_description AS TEXT) ILIKE '%water%' GROUP BY b.link_to_event), att AS (SELECT link_to_event AS event_id, COUNT(*) AS attendees FROM attendance GROUP BY link_to_event) SELECT ev.event_name, ROUND(CAST((COALESCE(w.total_cost, 0) * 1.0) / NULLIF(a.attendees, 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS water_cost_per_attendee FROM event AS ev JOIN att AS a ON a.event_id = ev.event_id LEFT JOIN water AS w ON w.event_id = ev.event_id GROUP BY ev.event_id, ev.event_name, a.attendees, w.total_cost ORDER BY ev.event_name NULLS FIRST

question: For my report on the club's academic makeup, could you tell me how many members on the club roster major in a department of the College of Humanities and Social Sciences, and how many members do not? The two counts together should cover every member on the roster, with each member counted in exactly one of the two groups. A member counts as majoring in the college only if the department offering their major belongs to the College of Humanities and Social Sciences.
evidence: The College of Humanities and Social Sciences is a college made up of certain departments; membership in the college is determined by which department offers a member's major.
SQL: WITH flag AS (SELECT m.member_id, CASE WHEN b.college = 'College of Humanities and Social Sciences' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS in_college FROM member AS m LEFT JOIN major AS b ON m.link_to_major = b.major_id) SELECT SUM(in_college) AS members_in_college, COUNT(*) - SUM(in_college) AS members_not_in_college FROM flag

question: For our snack budget planning: among the events that spent money on chips, which event has the highest budget amount? By budget amount I mean a single budget line, not a total across lines - compare events by their largest single budgeted line. If several events tie on that largest line, list all of their names. Please just give me the event name(s).
SQL: WITH chip_events AS (SELECT DISTINCT b.link_to_event AS event_id FROM budget AS b INNER JOIN expense AS x ON x.link_to_budget = b.budget_id WHERE CAST(x.expense_description AS TEXT) LIKE '%chips%') SELECT e.event_name FROM event AS e INNER JOIN budget AS b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE e.event_id IN (SELECT event_id FROM chip_events) AND b.amount = (SELECT MAX(amount) FROM budget WHERE link_to_event IN (SELECT event_id FROM chip_events))
