question: What is the date of the Vice President's most recent expense on record, and what is the total cost of all expenses incurred on that date? Consider all expenses on record with no earlier cut-off, and give the total exactly as it appears in the records, without rounding.
evidence: Vice President is a position of the Student Club.
SQL: SELECT e.expense_date, SUM(e.cost) AS total_cost FROM expense AS e JOIN member AS m ON m.member_id = e.link_to_member WHERE m.position = 'Vice President' AND e.expense_date = (SELECT MAX(e2.expense_date) FROM expense AS e2 JOIN member AS m2 ON m2.member_id = e2.link_to_member WHERE m2.position = 'Vice President') GROUP BY e.expense_date

question: I'm reviewing member engagement for our club's events in MU 215. Can you give me, for each event category of events held at MU 215, the number of club members who attended those events? Please count events regardless of their status (planning, open, or closed), and make sure every category that had events at MU 215 shows up, even if none of its events had any attendees.
evidence: MU 215: the room name as the event location.
SQL: SELECT e.type AS event_category, COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) AS attended_members FROM event AS e LEFT JOIN attendance AS a ON a.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE e.location = 'MU 215' GROUP BY e.type

question: I'm putting together a recruitment report for the colleges and want to know which parts of the university our club's membership actually draws from. For every person on the roster-regardless of their position in the club-look at their major, and the college that houses the department offering that major. Which college or colleges do the most majors on our roster come from, and how many majors is that? If there's a tie at the top, give me every college tied at that count. Please list the colleges in alphabetical order by college name, and return just each college's name and its number of majors.
evidence: Major: a field of study offered by a department housed in a college.
SQL: WITH cnt AS (SELECT mj.college AS college, COUNT(DISTINCT mj.major_id) AS majors FROM member AS m JOIN major AS mj ON mj.major_id = m.link_to_major GROUP BY mj.college) SELECT college, majors FROM cnt WHERE majors = (SELECT MAX(majors) FROM cnt) ORDER BY college NULLS FIRST

question: I want to review what the money actually went on for the well-funded events, by venue. For events that had a budget line of more than forty dollars, how many different things were bought for them at each location? Please give me, for each location, the location of the event and the number of different things bought for such events at that location, and nothing else. Note that a budget line of more than forty dollars means a single budgeted amount strictly over 40 dollars, and all qualifying events held at a location should be pooled together.
SQL: WITH RECURSIVE split(item, rest, loc) AS (SELECT '', x.expense_description || ',', e.location FROM expense AS x JOIN budget AS b ON b.budget_id = x.link_to_budget JOIN event AS e ON e.event_id = b.link_to_event WHERE b.amount > 40 UNION ALL SELECT TRIM(CAST(SUBSTRING(CAST(rest AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION(',' IN rest) - 1) AS TEXT)), SUBSTRING(CAST(rest AS TEXT) FROM POSITION(',' IN rest) + 1), loc FROM split WHERE rest <> '') SELECT loc AS location, COUNT(DISTINCT item) AS things_bought FROM split WHERE item <> '' GROUP BY loc ORDER BY loc NULLS FIRST

question: I'm reconciling what we budgeted for September events against what we actually spent. Can you give me the total amount budgeted for the September 2019 events that served pizza? By September 2019 I mean events dated September 1 through September 30, 2019. An event counts as having served pizza if pizza was among the expenses booked to it. Please include every budget line for those events, whatever the category - not just the food lines. All I need back is the single dollar figure for that total.
evidence: A pizza expense means an expense whose description is Pizza.
SQL: WITH pizza_events AS (SELECT DISTINCT b.link_to_event AS event_id FROM expense AS e JOIN budget AS b ON e.link_to_budget = b.budget_id WHERE e.expense_description = 'Pizza'), sept_events AS (SELECT event_id FROM event WHERE event_date >= '2019-09-01' AND event_date < '2019-10-01') SELECT ROUND(CAST(SUM(b.amount) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS total_budgeted FROM budget AS b JOIN sept_events AS s ON s.event_id = b.link_to_event WHERE b.link_to_event IN (SELECT event_id FROM pizza_events)

question: Hi - I need one overall figure for the budget next year: what's the average total amount we've actually spent per event, counting all budget categories, across every event we've ever recorded? Please give me the average in dollars, rounded to two decimal places, with no date restriction.
SQL: WITH per_event AS (SELECT e.event_id, COALESCE(SUM(b.spent), 0) AS total_spent FROM event AS e LEFT JOIN budget AS b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id GROUP BY e.event_id) SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(total_spent) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS average_total_spent_per_event FROM per_event

question: Among our closed events that stayed within budget (total spending not exceeding total budget), which one had the most purchases? Please give me just that event's name. Consider every closed event that didn't go over budget, including events with no purchases at all. If two events tie for the most purchases, report only the one with the alphabetically first event ID.
evidence: A purchase is a single item recorded on an expense record; one expense record may list several items. Total budget is the sum of budgeted amounts across all budget lines of the event; total spending is the sum of spent amounts across all budget lines of the event.
SQL: WITH budget_totals AS (SELECT link_to_event, SUM(spent) AS total_spending, SUM(amount) AS total_budget FROM budget GROUP BY link_to_event), items AS (SELECT b.link_to_event, SUM(LENGTH(CAST(x.expense_description AS TEXT)) - LENGTH(CAST(REPLACE(x.expense_description, ',', '') AS TEXT)) + 1) AS purchases FROM expense AS x JOIN budget AS b ON b.budget_id = x.link_to_budget GROUP BY b.link_to_event) SELECT e.event_name FROM event AS e LEFT JOIN budget_totals AS bt ON bt.link_to_event = e.event_id LEFT JOIN items AS i ON i.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE e.status = 'Closed' AND (bt.total_budget IS NULL OR bt.total_spending <= bt.total_budget) GROUP BY e.event_id, e.event_name ORDER BY COALESCE(MAX(i.purchases), 0) DESC NULLS LAST, e.event_id NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1

question: For our year-end review, I want to know which event formats bring in the most people. Looking at our whole club year (every event from September 2019 through May 2020), which event type was attended by the most members, and how many members attended that type's events? If several event types tie for the most, list every one of them. Just give me the event type and the number of members for it - nothing else.
evidence: By "attended" I mean a member coming to an event; event type is the kind of event, e.g. Meeting, Social, Game, Election, Community Service.
SQL: WITH member_counts AS (SELECT e.type AS event_type, COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) AS members FROM event AS e LEFT JOIN attendance AS a ON a.link_to_event = e.event_id GROUP BY e.type) SELECT event_type, members FROM member_counts WHERE members = (SELECT MAX(members) FROM member_counts) ORDER BY event_type NULLS FIRST

question: I'm putting together next semester's purchasing plan and want to know which food and drink item the club buys most often. Among purchases made under the food budget only, which single item appears on the most purchase records, and how many purchase records mention it? If two items are tied, go with the one whose name comes first alphabetically. Please give me just the item's name and that record count.
evidence: A purchase record is an entry in the club's expense records for money spent on a purchase.
SQL: WITH RECURSIVE items(expense_id, item, rest) AS (SELECT e.expense_id, '', e.expense_description || ',' FROM expense AS e JOIN budget AS b ON e.link_to_budget = b.budget_id WHERE b.category = 'Food' UNION ALL SELECT expense_id, TRIM(CAST(SUBSTRING(CAST(rest AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION(',' IN rest) - 1) AS TEXT)), SUBSTRING(CAST(rest AS TEXT) FROM POSITION(',' IN rest) + 1) FROM items WHERE rest <> '') SELECT item AS item_name, COUNT(DISTINCT expense_id) AS record_count FROM items WHERE item <> '' GROUP BY item ORDER BY record_count DESC NULLS LAST, item NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1

question: I'm wrapping up the October Meeting and need the final numbers broken down by what we actually bought, not just by budget category. For every item bought with approved money for the October Meeting, can you give me: the item's name, the budget category of the purchase that included the item, and the total cost in dollars of the approved October Meeting purchases that included the item? Only expenses marked as approved count - an expense without an approval mark doesn't. If an item was included in approved purchases recorded under more than one budget category, give me one row per category. Costs should be plain sums in US dollars with no rounding, and please sort the list by category and then by item name.
evidence: An item is a single thing bought with club money, such as water, pizza or posters. A purchase is an expense recorded for the event.
SQL: WITH RECURSIVE split AS (SELECT link_to_budget AS bid, cost, '' AS item, expense_description || ',' AS rest FROM expense WHERE approved = 'true' UNION ALL SELECT bid, cost, TRIM(CAST(SUBSTRING(CAST(rest AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION(',' IN rest) - 1) AS TEXT)), SUBSTRING(CAST(rest AS TEXT) FROM POSITION(',' IN rest) + 1) FROM split WHERE rest <> '') SELECT s.item AS item, b.category AS category, SUM(s.cost) AS total_cost FROM split AS s JOIN budget AS b ON s.bid = b.budget_id JOIN event AS e ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE s.item <> '' AND e.event_name = 'October Meeting' GROUP BY s.item, b.category ORDER BY b.category COLLATE "C" NULLS FIRST, s.item COLLATE "C" NULLS FIRST

question: For every event in the club's records, can you give me the event name, event date, total amount budgeted for the event, and the number of members who attended it? Please sort the list by event name, then by event date, both in ascending order.
SQL: SELECT e.event_name, e.event_date, COALESCE(b.total_budgeted_amount, 0) AS total_budgeted_amount, COALESCE(a.attendee_count, 0) AS attendee_count FROM event AS e LEFT JOIN (SELECT link_to_event, SUM(amount) AS total_budgeted_amount FROM budget GROUP BY link_to_event) AS b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id LEFT JOIN (SELECT link_to_event, COUNT(*) AS attendee_count FROM attendance GROUP BY link_to_event) AS a ON a.link_to_event = e.event_id ORDER BY e.event_name ASC NULLS FIRST, e.event_date ASC NULLS FIRST

question: I'm preparing the year-end audit of club spending. For each item Sacha Harrison bought with club money, I need the item name and how many times she bought it. Can you give me that list?
evidence: By "item" I mean an individual thing named in a record of what money was spent for.
SQL: WITH RECURSIVE split(rest, item) AS (SELECT expense_description || ',', '' FROM expense WHERE link_to_member = (SELECT member_id FROM member WHERE first_name = 'Sacha' AND last_name = 'Harrison') UNION ALL SELECT SUBSTRING(CAST(rest AS TEXT) FROM POSITION(',' IN rest) + 1), TRIM(CAST(SUBSTRING(CAST(rest AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION(',' IN rest) - 1) AS TEXT)) FROM split WHERE rest <> '') SELECT item, COUNT(*) AS times FROM split WHERE item <> '' GROUP BY item ORDER BY item COLLATE "C" NULLS FIRST

question: I'm putting together the end-of-term spending review. Who bought the most different kinds of items in October or November 2019? Please give me that member's full name, how many different kinds of items they bought in those two months, and their total spending in dollars over the same period. If two members tie for the most kinds, list every tied member with their kind count and spending.
evidence: An item is one of the individual things a purchase covered, such as a pizza or a bottle of water.
SQL: WITH RECURSIVE split AS (SELECT link_to_member, expense_description AS rest FROM expense WHERE expense_date BETWEEN '2019-10-01' AND '2019-11-30' UNION ALL SELECT link_to_member, SUBSTRING(CAST(rest AS TEXT) FROM POSITION(',' IN rest || ',') + 1) FROM split WHERE rest <> ''), items AS (SELECT link_to_member, TRIM(CAST(SUBSTRING(CAST(rest AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION(',' IN rest || ',') - 1) AS TEXT)) AS item FROM split WHERE rest <> ''), kinds AS (SELECT link_to_member, COUNT(DISTINCT item) AS kind_count FROM items GROUP BY link_to_member), spend AS (SELECT link_to_member, SUM(cost) AS total_spending FROM expense WHERE expense_date BETWEEN '2019-10-01' AND '2019-11-30' GROUP BY link_to_member) SELECT m.first_name || ' ' || m.last_name AS full_name, k.kind_count, s.total_spending FROM kinds AS k JOIN spend AS s ON s.link_to_member = k.link_to_member JOIN member AS m ON m.member_id = k.link_to_member WHERE k.kind_count = (SELECT MAX(kind_count) FROM kinds)

question: For our department report, I need to know how many different fields of study our club members from the Political Science Department represent. Only count members of the Political Science Department - members from other departments don't count. Just give me the number of different majors studied by those members.
evidence: A major is a field of study offered by a department.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t2.major_id) AS different_majors FROM member AS t1 INNER JOIN major AS t2 ON t1.link_to_major = t2.major_id WHERE t2.department = 'Political Science Department'

question: Among Marvel Comics superheroes with a known eye colour, rank the eye colours by number of superheroes. Give each colour, its hero count, and its rank, most common first; break display-order ties alphabetically.
SQL: WITH colour_counts AS (SELECT c.colour AS eye_colour, COUNT(*) AS hero_count FROM superhero AS s JOIN colour AS c ON c.id = s.eye_colour_id JOIN publisher AS p ON p.id = s.publisher_id WHERE p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' AND c.colour <> 'No Colour' GROUP BY c.colour) SELECT eye_colour, hero_count, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY hero_count DESC NULLS LAST) AS popularity_rank FROM colour_counts ORDER BY hero_count DESC NULLS LAST, eye_colour NULLS FIRST

question: List the superheroes from Marvel Comics who have the super power of 'Super Strength'.
SQL: SELECT superhero_name FROM superhero AS t1 WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM hero_power AS t2 INNER JOIN superpower AS t3 ON t2.power_id = t3.id WHERE t3.power_name = 'Super Strength' AND t1.id = t2.hero_id) AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM publisher AS t4 WHERE t4.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' AND t1.publisher_id = t4.id)

question: What percentage of all superheroes have Neutral alignment, and how many of those Neutral superheroes were published by Marvel Comics? Round the percentage to two decimals.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN a.alignment = 'Neutral' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2), SUM(CASE WHEN a.alignment = 'Neutral' AND p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM superhero AS s LEFT JOIN alignment AS a ON a.id = s.alignment_id LEFT JOIN publisher AS p ON p.id = s.publisher_id

question: Between Marvel Comics and DC Comics, which publisher has more superheroes, and by how many?
SQL: WITH counts AS (SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS marvel_count, SUM(CASE WHEN p.publisher_name = 'DC Comics' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dc_count FROM superhero AS s JOIN publisher AS p ON p.id = s.publisher_id) SELECT CASE WHEN marvel_count > dc_count THEN 'Marvel Comics' WHEN dc_count > marvel_count THEN 'DC Comics' ELSE 'Tie' END, ABS(marvel_count - dc_count) FROM counts

question: Among superheroes from 170 through 190 cm tall whose recorded eye-colour category is unknown, list their names.
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT t1.superhero_name FROM superhero AS t1 INNER JOIN colour AS t2 ON t1.eye_colour_id = t2.id WHERE t1.height_cm BETWEEN 170 AND 190 AND t2.colour = 'No Colour'

question: Among all superheroes with recorded height from 150 through 180 cm, what percentage were published by Marvel Comics? Round to two decimals.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) FROM superhero AS s LEFT JOIN publisher AS p ON p.id = s.publisher_id WHERE s.height_cm BETWEEN 150 AND 180

question: What known full names belong to superheroes tied for the highest strength attribute value?
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT s.full_name FROM superhero AS s JOIN hero_attribute AS ha ON ha.hero_id = s.id JOIN attribute AS a ON a.id = ha.attribute_id WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Strength' AND ha.attribute_value = (SELECT MAX(ha2.attribute_value) FROM hero_attribute AS ha2 JOIN attribute AS a2 ON a2.id = ha2.attribute_id WHERE a2.attribute_name = 'Strength') AND NOT s.full_name IS NULL AND s.full_name <> '-' ORDER BY s.full_name ASC NULLS FIRST

question: List superheroes whose known eye, hair and skin colours are all the same, along with any recorded publisher name.
SQL: SELECT s.superhero_name, p.publisher_name FROM superhero AS s LEFT JOIN publisher AS p ON p.id = s.publisher_id JOIN colour AS c ON c.id = s.eye_colour_id WHERE s.eye_colour_id = s.hair_colour_id AND s.eye_colour_id = s.skin_colour_id AND c.colour <> 'No Colour'

question: Among all female superheroes, what percentage have blue skin? Round to two decimals.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN co.colour = 'Blue' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) FROM superhero AS s JOIN gender AS g ON g.id = s.gender_id LEFT JOIN colour AS co ON co.id = s.skin_colour_id WHERE g.gender = 'Female'

question: Among all female superheroes, what percentage were published by Marvel Comics? Round to two decimal places.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) FROM superhero AS s JOIN gender AS g ON s.gender_id = g.id LEFT JOIN publisher AS p ON s.publisher_id = p.id WHERE g.gender = 'Female'

question: Which publisher has more superheroes, DC Comics or Marvel Comics, and by how many? Return Tie if their counts are equal.
SQL: WITH counts AS (SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN p.publisher_name = 'DC Comics' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dc, SUM(CASE WHEN p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS marvel FROM superhero AS s JOIN publisher AS p ON p.id = s.publisher_id) SELECT CASE WHEN dc > marvel THEN 'DC Comics' WHEN marvel > dc THEN 'Marvel Comics' ELSE 'Tie' END, ABS(dc - marvel) FROM counts

question: I'm comparing Marvel and DC rosters and want to quantify how tall Marvel's roster is for characters whose abilities DC cannot match. What is the average height, in centimetres, of Marvel Comics characters who have at least one power that no DC Comics character has? Only characters with a measured height count.
evidence: A "power" is any single ability listed for a character in the database.
SQL: SELECT AVG(CAST(s.height_cm AS DOUBLE PRECISION)) AS average_height_cm FROM superhero AS s JOIN publisher AS p ON s.publisher_id = p.id WHERE p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' AND s.height_cm > 0 AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM hero_power AS hp WHERE hp.hero_id = s.id AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM hero_power AS hp2 JOIN superhero AS s2 ON s2.id = hp2.hero_id JOIN publisher AS p2 ON p2.id = s2.publisher_id WHERE p2.publisher_name = 'DC Comics' AND hp2.power_id = hp.power_id))

question: For a segment on strength heroes, I want to know how many superpowers are held only by heroes who have Super Strength. A power counts as held only if at least one hero who has Super Strength holds it, and Super Strength itself should be included if it meets that condition. Just give me the count.
evidence: Super Strength is a super power name.
SQL: WITH strength_heroes AS (SELECT hp.hero_id FROM hero_power AS hp INNER JOIN superpower AS sp ON hp.power_id = sp.id WHERE sp.power_name = 'Super Strength') SELECT COUNT(*) AS power_count FROM superpower AS s WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM hero_power AS hp WHERE hp.power_id = s.id AND hp.hero_id IN (SELECT hero_id FROM strength_heroes)) AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM hero_power AS hp2 WHERE hp2.power_id = s.id AND NOT hp2.hero_id IN (SELECT hero_id FROM strength_heroes))

question: I'm setting a typical weight for a green-skinned creature class. Can you tell me the average weight in kg of the heroes with green skin? Count only heroes whose weight is known, and give me one number rounded to one decimal place.
evidence: Green skin means the hero's skin colour is green.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(t1.weight_kg) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS average_weight_kg FROM superhero AS t1 INNER JOIN colour AS t2 ON t1.skin_colour_id = t2.id WHERE t2.colour = 'Green' AND t1.weight_kg > 0

question: I'm writing an article about heroes who fall outside the classic good-versus-evil divide. How many superheroes in the database have an alignment that is neither good nor bad? Please give me just that count. Note that this should cover all superheroes in the database.
evidence: good: a superhero whose alignment is Good; bad: a superhero whose alignment is Bad; alignment: the moral category assigned to a superhero
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS neither_good_nor_bad FROM superhero AS s LEFT JOIN alignment AS a ON s.alignment_id = a.id WHERE a.alignment IS NULL OR NOT a.alignment IN ('Good', 'Bad')

question: I'm building a fact box on Marvel heroes' civilian identities. Among Marvel Comics superheroes whose full name (their civilian identity, like 'Richard Milhouse Jones') is known, which superpower is the most common, and how many of those heroes have it? If several superpowers tie for most common, list all of them with their counts. Just give me the superpower name(s) and the counts.
SQL: WITH pc AS (SELECT sp.power_name, COUNT(DISTINCT hp.hero_id) AS hero_count FROM hero_power AS hp JOIN superpower AS sp ON hp.power_id = sp.id JOIN superhero AS s ON hp.hero_id = s.id JOIN publisher AS p ON s.publisher_id = p.id WHERE p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' AND NOT s.full_name IS NULL AND s.full_name <> '-' GROUP BY sp.power_name) SELECT power_name, hero_count FROM pc WHERE hero_count = (SELECT MAX(hero_count) FROM pc) ORDER BY power_name NULLS FIRST

question: I want to profile the cohort of heroes whose Intelligence score matches Abomination's Intelligence score. What is their average measured weight in kg? Please round the average to two decimals.
evidence: Intelligence is one of the six attribute scores a hero has (Intelligence, Strength, Speed, Durability, Power, Combat)
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(CASE WHEN s.weight_kg > 0 THEN s.weight_kg END) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS average_weight_kg FROM superhero AS s JOIN hero_attribute AS ha ON ha.hero_id = s.id JOIN attribute AS a ON a.id = ha.attribute_id WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Intelligence' AND ha.attribute_value = (SELECT abom_ha.attribute_value FROM superhero AS abom JOIN hero_attribute AS abom_ha ON abom_ha.hero_id = abom.id JOIN attribute AS abom_a ON abom_a.id = abom_ha.attribute_id WHERE abom.superhero_name = 'Abomination' AND abom_a.attribute_name = 'Intelligence')

question: I'm putting together a trivia page profiling blue-haired heroes by their abilities. For each gender, male and female, how many blue-haired superheroes have at least ten listed powers? I need the count for both groups, and by 'at least ten' I mean ten or more.
evidence: Listed powers: the superpowers recorded for a hero.
SQL: SELECT g.gender AS gender, COUNT(s.id) AS superhero_count FROM gender AS g LEFT JOIN superhero AS s ON s.gender_id = g.id AND s.hair_colour_id = (SELECT id FROM colour WHERE colour = 'Blue') AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hero_power AS hp WHERE hp.hero_id = s.id) >= 10 WHERE g.gender IN ('Male', 'Female') GROUP BY g.gender ORDER BY g.gender NULLS FIRST

question: I'm putting together a comparison of the heaviest brick-strength characters. What is the average weight, in kilograms, of all superheroes whose Strength score equals the Hulk's? I just need a single integer rounded to the nearest kilogram. Include every superhero in the database, no restrictions on publisher or alignment. If a hero's weight is unknown, leave them out and average only over the heroes whose weight has actually been measured.
evidence: Strength is one of the six measured hero attributes, each scored on a 1-100 scale; the Hulk is the superhero named 'Hulk'; weight is the superhero's weight in kilograms.
SQL: SELECT CASE WHEN (ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg))) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg))) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END AS average_weight_kg FROM superhero AS s INNER JOIN hero_attribute AS ha ON ha.hero_id = s.id INNER JOIN attribute AS a ON a.id = ha.attribute_id WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Strength' AND ha.attribute_value = (SELECT ha2.attribute_value FROM superhero AS s2 INNER JOIN hero_attribute AS ha2 ON ha2.hero_id = s2.id INNER JOIN attribute AS a2 ON a2.id = ha2.attribute_id WHERE s2.superhero_name = 'Hulk' AND a2.attribute_name = 'Strength') AND s.weight_kg > 0

question: For my 'giants of the genre' feature, I want to headline how varied the abilities of the tallest heroes are. How many different superpowers appear among the ten tallest superheroes? Rank heroes by height and take the top ten; if several heroes tie at the tenth-tallest height, include all of them. A hero counts among the ten tallest even if no powers are on file for them. Please give me just that single number.
evidence: superpower = an ability such as Agility or Accelerated Healing, as named in the superpower list
SQL: WITH top10 AS (SELECT id FROM superhero ORDER BY height_cm DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t3.power_name) AS superpowers FROM top10 JOIN hero_power AS t2 ON top10.id = t2.hero_id JOIN superpower AS t3 ON t2.power_id = t3.id

question: How many characters published by A-Bomb's publisher have no race listed? I just need a single count. (By A-Bomb's publisher, I mean the publisher that publishes the character A-Bomb.)
evidence: race: the character's race or group, e.g. Human, Alien, Mutant
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS character_count FROM superhero WHERE publisher_id = (SELECT publisher_id FROM superhero WHERE superhero_name = 'A-Bomb') AND (race_id IS NULL OR race_id = (SELECT id FROM race WHERE race = '-'))

question: Hey, following up on my count of the God / Eternal heroes – among those who are male, what's the average number of superpowers per hero? Just give me the average rounded to two decimal places.
evidence: A superpower is any power linked to a hero.
SQL: WITH power_counts AS (SELECT s.id, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hero_power AS hp WHERE hp.hero_id = s.id) AS power_count FROM superhero AS s INNER JOIN race AS r ON s.race_id = r.id INNER JOIN gender AS g ON s.gender_id = g.id WHERE r.race = 'God / Eternal' AND g.gender = 'Male') SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(power_count) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS average_superpowers FROM power_counts

question: For my cryokinesis page, I want to know how broad the power portfolios are around ice-powered heroes. Consider all heroes who share at least one superpower with a cryokinesis holder - including the cryokinesis holders themselves, since they share cryokinesis with each other. What is the average number of superpowers these heroes have, rounded to one decimal place? Please send back just that single number.
evidence: Cryokinesis is the superpower to generate and control ice.
SQL: WITH sharers AS (SELECT DISTINCT hp2.hero_id FROM hero_power AS hp1 JOIN hero_power AS hp2 ON hp2.power_id = hp1.power_id WHERE hp1.hero_id IN (SELECT hero_id FROM hero_power WHERE power_id = (SELECT id FROM superpower WHERE power_name = 'Cryokinesis'))), counts AS (SELECT hero_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM hero_power WHERE hero_id IN (SELECT hero_id FROM sharers) GROUP BY hero_id) SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(cnt) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS avg_superpower_count FROM counts

question: What is the average weight in kilograms of the DC Comics heroes whose eye colour is also shared by at least one Marvel Comics hero? Leave out any heroes whose weight is unknown, round the result to the nearest kilogram, and treat 'No Colour' as an eye colour like any other when matching between publishers. I just want that single number.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN s.weight_kg > 0 THEN s.weight_kg END)) AS average_weight_kg FROM superhero AS s JOIN publisher AS p ON s.publisher_id = p.id WHERE p.publisher_name = 'DC Comics' AND s.eye_colour_id IN (SELECT s2.eye_colour_id FROM superhero AS s2 JOIN publisher AS p2 ON s2.publisher_id = p2.id WHERE p2.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics')

question: I'm researching heroes like A-Bomb. What is the average height in centimetres of the superheroes in A-Bomb's group? Please give me just that single number, rounded to one decimal place. Note that A-Bomb itself belongs to its group and should be included, and only heroes whose height is actually on record should count toward the average-anyone without a recorded height should be left out rather than counted as some height.
evidence: In this request, "group" refers to race.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(CASE WHEN height_cm > 0 THEN height_cm END) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS average_height_cm FROM superhero WHERE race_id = (SELECT race_id FROM superhero WHERE superhero_name = 'A-Bomb')

question: What is the average weight, in kg, of the heroes who belong to races in which no hero is female? Heroes whose weight is not recorded should not count toward the average. I just need that single value.
evidence: female: the hero's gender is female
SQL: SELECT AVG(CAST(t1.weight_kg AS DOUBLE PRECISION)) AS average_weight_kg FROM superhero AS t1 INNER JOIN race AS t2 ON t1.race_id = t2.id WHERE t1.weight_kg > 0 AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM superhero AS t3 INNER JOIN gender AS t4 ON t3.gender_id = t4.id WHERE t3.race_id = t2.id AND t4.gender = 'Female')

question: I'm writing a piece about which real publishing companies have put out very tall heroes. How many publishers in the database have released at least one hero taller than 200 cm? Note that taller than 200 cm means strictly more than 200 cm, and it counts if even one of their heroes is that tall. I just need the number of publishers, nothing else.
evidence: A hero's publisher being 'released' means the publisher the hero is attributed to in the database.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t1.publisher_id) AS publisher_count FROM superhero AS t1 INNER JOIN publisher AS t2 ON t1.publisher_id = t2.id WHERE t1.height_cm > 200 AND t2.publisher_name <> ''

question: For a licensing survey of non-DC heroic characters, I need a single total count of superheroes whose alignment is Good and who are not published by DC Comics. Just that one number, please.
evidence: Good means the hero's alignment is Good; DC Comics means the publisher named DC Comics.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS hero_count FROM superhero AS t1 INNER JOIN alignment AS t2 ON t1.alignment_id = t2.id WHERE t2.alignment = 'Good' AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM publisher AS t3 WHERE t3.id = t1.publisher_id AND t3.publisher_name = 'DC Comics')

question: I'm comparing superhero body weights to typical human weights for an article. What is the average weight in kilograms of superheroes published by DC Comics, rounded to one decimal place, and how many DC Comics superheroes is that average based on? Only superheroes with a known weight should count toward the average, so the count should be the number of superheroes it's based on. DC Comics means the publisher named DC Comics.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(s.weight_kg) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS avg_weight_kg, COUNT(*) AS hero_count FROM superhero AS s JOIN publisher AS p ON s.publisher_id = p.id WHERE p.publisher_name = 'DC Comics' AND s.weight_kg > 0

question: How many heroes published by Blackwulf's publisher have an eye colour that at least one hero from a different publisher also has? By "that publisher's heroes" I mean all of its heroes, not just Blackwulf. A different publisher means any other publisher, and heroes with no publisher listed shouldn't count as coming from a different publisher. I just want that single count back.
evidence: Eye colour: the colour of a hero's eyes as catalogued for that hero.
SQL: WITH blk AS (SELECT publisher_id AS pid FROM superhero WHERE superhero_name = 'Blackwulf') SELECT COUNT(*) AS hero_count FROM superhero AS m WHERE m.publisher_id = (SELECT pid FROM blk) AND m.eye_colour_id IN (SELECT d.eye_colour_id FROM superhero AS d WHERE NOT d.publisher_id IS NULL AND d.publisher_id <> (SELECT pid FROM blk))

question: Which race is the most common among the superheroes published by the same publisher as the superhero whose full name is Charles Chandler? I'd like, for that publisher's superheroes only, the name of the most common race and the count of that publisher's superheroes of that race. Ignore any superhero with no race recorded. If several races tie for most common, list every tied race with its count.
evidence: Race: the superhero's species or type, e.g. Human, Mutant, Alien.
SQL: WITH counts AS (SELECT r.race AS race, COUNT(*) AS hero_count FROM superhero AS s INNER JOIN race AS r ON s.race_id = r.id WHERE s.publisher_id = (SELECT publisher_id FROM superhero WHERE full_name = 'Charles Chandler') AND r.race <> '-' GROUP BY r.id, r.race) SELECT race, hero_count FROM counts WHERE hero_count = (SELECT MAX(hero_count) FROM counts)

question: What is the average weight in kg of the Female heroes in the database? Round it to two decimal places, and skip any heroes whose weight is unknown. I just need that single number.
evidence: kg: kilograms
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(weight_kg) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS average_weight_kg FROM superhero WHERE gender_id = (SELECT id FROM gender WHERE gender = 'Female') AND weight_kg > 0

question: I'm writing a power-profile feature on heroes with super speed or death touch. Can you give me one number: the average intelligence score of the superheroes who have either of those powers? Round it to one decimal place, and only count the heroes who actually have an intelligence score in the database.
evidence: "Super speed" and "death touch" are superpower names as used in the database; "intelligence" is the hero attribute by that name.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(v) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS average_intelligence FROM (SELECT DISTINCT t1.id, t4.attribute_value AS v FROM superhero AS t1 INNER JOIN hero_power AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.hero_id INNER JOIN superpower AS t3 ON t2.power_id = t3.id INNER JOIN hero_attribute AS t4 ON t4.hero_id = t1.id INNER JOIN attribute AS t5 ON t4.attribute_id = t5.id WHERE t3.power_name IN ('Super Speed', 'Death Touch') AND t5.attribute_name = 'Intelligence') AS __photo_derived_1

question: I'm comparing how power-rich male and female heroes are. For all male heroes and all female heroes that have a documented real full name, what is the average number of superpowers per hero for each gender? Please compute each average over the entire hero population of that gender, not just the heroes that happen to have power records. Give me both averages, each rounded to two decimal places, and nothing else.
evidence: Full name: the hero's real, full personal name (first name plus last name, and optionally middle names); single names such as mononyms or aliases are not a full name.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(CASE WHEN (SUM(CASE WHEN g.gender = 'Male' THEN COALESCE(pc.cnt, 0) ELSE 0 END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(CASE WHEN g.gender = 'Male' THEN COALESCE(pc.cnt, 0) ELSE 0 END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN g.gender = 'Male' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_superpowers_male, ROUND(CAST(CASE WHEN (SUM(CASE WHEN g.gender = 'Female' THEN COALESCE(pc.cnt, 0) ELSE 0 END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(CASE WHEN g.gender = 'Female' THEN COALESCE(pc.cnt, 0) ELSE 0 END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN g.gender = 'Female' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_superpowers_female FROM superhero AS s INNER JOIN gender AS g ON s.gender_id = g.id LEFT JOIN (SELECT hero_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM hero_power GROUP BY hero_id) AS pc ON pc.hero_id = s.id WHERE CAST(s.full_name AS TEXT) LIKE '% %'

question: I'm putting together a physical profile of the green-skinned villain corner of the universe for a fan wiki page. Could you tell me the average height in centimetres and the average weight in kilograms of the green-skinned villains? Please average only over the characters whose measurement is actually on record - a character with no recorded height or weight shouldn't drag the average down - and round each average to two decimals. I just need those two numbers.
evidence: By 'villain' I mean a character whose alignment is Bad, and by 'green-skinned' I mean a character whose skin colour is Green. Height in centimetres and weight in kilograms are the character's height_cm and weight_kg as commonly understood physical measurements.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(CASE WHEN t1.height_cm > 0 THEN t1.height_cm END) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_height_cm, ROUND(CAST(AVG(CASE WHEN t1.weight_kg > 0 THEN t1.weight_kg END) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_weight_kg FROM superhero AS t1 INNER JOIN alignment AS t2 ON t1.alignment_id = t2.id INNER JOIN colour AS t3 ON t1.skin_colour_id = t3.id WHERE t2.alignment = 'Bad' AND t3.colour = 'Green'

question: I'm profiling publisher rosters and now want to look at the physical build of George Lucas's heroes. What is the average height of the heroes he created, in centimetres, and their average weight, in kilograms? Please round each average to one decimal place, and only include heroes whose height (for the height average) or weight (for the weight average) is actually known.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(CASE WHEN s.height_cm > 0 THEN s.height_cm END) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS average_height_cm, ROUND(CAST(AVG(CASE WHEN s.weight_kg > 0 THEN s.weight_kg END) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS average_weight_kg FROM superhero AS s INNER JOIN publisher AS p ON s.publisher_id = p.id WHERE p.publisher_name = 'George Lucas'

question: I'd like to know how tall the heroes are who share at least one superpower with 3-D Man. Can you give me the average height in centimetres of those heroes, rounded to one decimal place? Please leave 3-D Man himself out of it, and don't count heroes whose height isn't known.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(s.height_cm) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS avg_height_cm FROM superhero AS s WHERE s.height_cm > 0 AND s.id <> (SELECT id FROM superhero WHERE superhero_name = '3-D Man') AND s.id IN (SELECT hp2.hero_id FROM hero_power AS hp2 WHERE hp2.power_id IN (SELECT power_id FROM hero_power WHERE hero_id = (SELECT id FROM superhero WHERE superhero_name = '3-D Man')))

question: I'm writing an article about green-skinned flying villains and need a body-statistics fact. What is the average weight, in kilograms, of all green-skinned villains who can fly? By villain I mean a character whose moral affiliation is Bad. Please include only characters whose weight was actually measured-any character whose weight was never measured should be left out of the average. Give me just the single number, rounded to the nearest kilogram.
evidence: Flight: the power to fly.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN s.weight_kg > 0 THEN s.weight_kg END)) AS average_weight_kg FROM superhero AS s INNER JOIN alignment AS a ON s.alignment_id = a.id INNER JOIN colour AS c ON s.skin_colour_id = c.id INNER JOIN hero_power AS hp ON hp.hero_id = s.id INNER JOIN superpower AS sp ON sp.id = hp.power_id WHERE a.alignment = 'Bad' AND c.colour = 'Green' AND sp.power_name = 'Flight'

question: I'm doing a physical-profile breakdown of the George Lucas catalogue. For the heroes published by George Lucas that have at least one superpower in the database, what is their average weight in kilograms, counting only the heroes whose weight is recorded? Please give me just that one number, rounded to two decimal places.
evidence: George Lucas refers to the publisher name.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(CASE WHEN s.weight_kg > 0 THEN s.weight_kg END) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_weight_kg FROM superhero AS s INNER JOIN publisher AS p ON s.publisher_id = p.id WHERE p.publisher_name = 'George Lucas' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM hero_power AS hp WHERE hp.hero_id = s.id)

question: For the article I'm writing on heroic female characters, I'd like a physique stat for the trivia box: what is the average weight in kilograms of female superheroes whose alignment is good? Only count superheroes whose weight is known. Please round the result to two decimal places.
evidence: Alignment: the superhero's moral category, e.g. good, bad, neutral.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(s.weight_kg) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS average_weight_kg FROM superhero AS s JOIN gender AS g ON g.id = s.gender_id JOIN alignment AS a ON a.id = s.alignment_id WHERE g.gender = 'Female' AND a.alignment = 'Good' AND s.weight_kg > 0

question: I'm picking powers for a lightweight male hero archetype. How many different superpowers are held by at least one male superhero who weighs under 70 kilograms? Heroes whose weight isn't recorded shouldn't count as weighing under 70.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT hp.power_id) AS power_count FROM superhero AS s JOIN hero_power AS hp ON hp.hero_id = s.id JOIN superpower AS sp ON sp.id = hp.power_id JOIN gender AS g ON g.id = s.gender_id WHERE g.gender = 'Male' AND s.weight_kg > 0 AND s.weight_kg < 70

question: I'm putting together a trivia fact box on tiny heroes. Could you tell me the hair colour of the shortest human superhero? Please treat heroes with no recorded height as unmeasured rather than as being the shortest. I just need the colour, nothing else.
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT c.colour FROM superhero AS s INNER JOIN race AS r ON s.race_id = r.id INNER JOIN colour AS c ON s.hair_colour_id = c.id WHERE r.race = 'Human' AND s.height_cm = (SELECT MIN(x.height_cm) FROM superhero AS x INNER JOIN race AS y ON x.race_id = y.id WHERE y.race = 'Human' AND x.height_cm > 0)

question: I want to know about the lightest superhero whose weight has actually been recorded. Among all heroes sharing that lightest weight, give me the largest number of superpowers any of them has. If such a hero has no powers, that counts as 0. Please return just that one number.
evidence: A superpower is one power a hero has, identified by its name.
SQL: SELECT MAX(cnt) AS power_count FROM (SELECT COUNT(hp.power_id) AS cnt FROM superhero AS h LEFT JOIN hero_power AS hp ON h.id = hp.hero_id WHERE h.weight_kg = (SELECT MIN(weight_kg) FROM superhero WHERE weight_kg > 0) GROUP BY h.id) AS __photo_derived_1

question: I'm auditing identity info on our hero profile pages. How many neutral-alignment heroes have a known full name? Just give me the count.
evidence: By "full name" I mean the hero's real-world identity name, not the superhero/costume name.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS neutral_heroes_with_known_full_name FROM superhero AS t1 INNER JOIN alignment AS t2 ON t1.alignment_id = t2.id WHERE t2.alignment = 'Neutral' AND NOT t1.full_name IS NULL AND t1.full_name <> '-'

question: I'm building a profile page crediting the fastest characters. Among all superheroes that share the top Speed attribute value (everyone tied at the highest Speed value counts), can you list the ones whose real name is known? For each, I need the superhero name and the full name — the civilian identity behind the mask — and nothing else. Please leave out anyone whose real name isn't identifiable.
SQL: SELECT s.superhero_name, s.full_name FROM superhero AS s JOIN hero_attribute AS h ON h.hero_id = s.id JOIN attribute AS a ON a.id = h.attribute_id WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Speed' AND h.attribute_value = (SELECT MAX(h2.attribute_value) FROM hero_attribute AS h2 JOIN attribute AS a2 ON a2.id = h2.attribute_id WHERE a2.attribute_name = 'Speed') AND NOT s.full_name IS NULL AND s.full_name <> '-' ORDER BY s.superhero_name NULLS FIRST

question: I'm looking at how designers pair hair and eye colours. For every eye colour that appears on at least one brown-haired hero, how many heroes have that eye colour while their hair is NOT brown? Just give me each eye colour and that count, listing the eye colour with the highest count first. If two eye colours have the same count, the one whose name comes first alphabetically should come first.
evidence: By a brown-haired hero I mean a hero whose hair colour is Brown.
SQL: WITH cohort AS (SELECT DISTINCT s.eye_colour_id AS eid FROM superhero AS s INNER JOIN colour AS h ON s.hair_colour_id = h.id WHERE h.colour = 'Brown') SELECT c.colour AS eye_colour, COUNT(CASE WHEN h.colour <> 'Brown' THEN 1 END) AS heroes FROM cohort AS t INNER JOIN colour AS c ON c.id = t.eid LEFT JOIN superhero AS s ON s.eye_colour_id = t.eid LEFT JOIN colour AS h ON h.id = s.hair_colour_id GROUP BY c.colour ORDER BY heroes DESC NULLS LAST, eye_colour NULLS FIRST

question: I'm preparing a report on Marvel's roster and want to gauge how heroic their catalogued heroes are. Among Marvel Comics superheroes whose civilian full name is documented, what percentage are good? Please give me just that single percentage, rounded to two decimal places. Note: the percentage should be taken over all Marvel Comics superheroes with a known full name - those whose moral alignment is unknown still count toward the total, just not as good.
evidence: Good refers to alignment = 'Good'. A full name means the hero's real-world civilian identity, i.e. an actual person's name such as 'Charles Chandler' or 'Richard Milhouse Jones'.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(CASE WHEN (SUM(CASE WHEN t3.alignment = 'Good' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(CASE WHEN t3.alignment = 'Good' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS percentage FROM superhero AS t1 INNER JOIN publisher AS t2 ON t1.publisher_id = t2.id LEFT JOIN alignment AS t3 ON t1.alignment_id = t3.id WHERE t2.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' AND NOT t1.full_name IS NULL AND t1.full_name <> '-'

question: What percentage of Marvel Comics superheroes with a recorded superpower are classified as good? Round the percentage to two decimal places, and give me just that single value.
evidence: Good means alignment 'Good'; superpower refers to a hero's recorded power.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(CASE WHEN (SUM(CASE WHEN a.alignment = 'Good' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(CASE WHEN a.alignment = 'Good' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS good_percentage FROM superhero AS s JOIN publisher AS p ON s.publisher_id = p.id LEFT JOIN alignment AS a ON s.alignment_id = a.id WHERE p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM hero_power AS hp WHERE hp.hero_id = s.id)

question: I'm comparing the builds of heroes whose power sets overlap with 3-D Man's. What is the average weight in kg of the heroes other than 3-D Man that share at least one superpower with him? Please round it to two decimal places, leave out any heroes whose weight isn't recorded, and return just that single number.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(weight_kg) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS average_weight_kg FROM superhero WHERE superhero_name <> '3-D Man' AND weight_kg > 0 AND id IN (SELECT hero_id FROM hero_power WHERE power_id IN (SELECT power_id FROM hero_power WHERE hero_id = (SELECT id FROM superhero WHERE superhero_name = '3-D Man')))

question: Among superheroes whose weight is not recorded, how many more have the 'No Colour' eye category than have blue eyes? I want a single whole number: the count of 'No Colour' eyes minus the count of blue eyes in that group - it can be negative if blue is more common. Please give me just that one number, with no other results or breakdowns.
evidence: 'No Colour' is an eye category meaning the hero's eye colour is unspecified.
SQL: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN co.colour = 'No Colour' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN co.colour = 'Blue' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS diff FROM superhero AS s JOIN colour AS co ON co.id = s.eye_colour_id WHERE s.weight_kg = 0 OR s.weight_kg IS NULL

question: Among distinct patients with at least one uric-acid result above the sex-specific upper limit, what is the ratio of male to female patients?
evidence: For this task, the uric-acid upper limit is 8.0 for males and 6.5 for females.
SQL: SELECT CASE WHEN (SUM(CASE WHEN p.sex = 'M' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(CASE WHEN p.sex = 'M' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END / NULLIF(NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN p.sex = 'F' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0), 0) FROM patient AS p WHERE (p.sex = 'M' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND l.ua > 8.0)) OR (p.sex = 'F' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND l.ua > 6.5))

question: Across laboratory records with PLT > 400 for female patients whose patient profile lists an SLE diagnosis, what is the average ALB value rounded to four decimal places?
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(CAST(l.alb AS DECIMAL(10, 4))) AS DECIMAL), 4) FROM patient AS p JOIN laboratory AS l ON l.id = p.id WHERE l.plt > 400 AND (CAST((',' || REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(COALESCE(p.diagnosis, ''), CHR(13), ','), CHR(10), ','), CHR(29), ','), CHR(11), ','), '  ', ','), ' ', '') || ',') AS TEXT) LIKE '%,SLE,%' OR CAST((',' || REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(COALESCE(p.diagnosis, ''), CHR(13), ','), CHR(10), ','), CHR(29), ','), CHR(11), ','), '  ', ','), ' ', '') || ',') AS TEXT) LIKE '%,SLE(%') AND p.sex = 'F'

question: How many distinct patients with a triglyceride result of at least 200 were older than 50 on 2026-10-09?
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM patient AS p WHERE p.birthday < '1976-10-09' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND l.tg >= 200)

question: List patient IDs, sex, and completed age on 2026-10-09 for patients with at least one laboratory record showing glucose at least 180 and total cholesterol below 250.
SQL: SELECT p.id, p.sex, (CAST(SUBSTRING(CAST(CAST('2026-10-09' AS CHAR(10)) AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) AS DECIMAL(4, 0)) - CAST(SUBSTRING(CAST(CAST(p.birthday AS CHAR(10)) AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) AS DECIMAL(4, 0)) - CASE WHEN SUBSTRING(CAST(CAST('2026-10-09' AS CHAR(10)) AS TEXT) FROM 6 FOR 5) < SUBSTRING(CAST(CAST(p.birthday AS CHAR(10)) AS TEXT) FROM 6 FOR 5) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS age FROM patient AS p WHERE NOT p.birthday IS NULL AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND l.glu >= 180 AND l."T-CHO" < 250) ORDER BY p.id NULLS FIRST

question: List the IDs and completed ages on 2026-10-09 of patients with at least two laboratory results having hematocrit of 52 or higher.
SQL: SELECT p.id, (CAST(SUBSTRING(CAST(CAST('2026-10-09' AS CHAR(10)) AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) AS DECIMAL(4, 0)) - CAST(SUBSTRING(CAST(CAST(p.birthday AS CHAR(10)) AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) AS DECIMAL(4, 0)) - CASE WHEN SUBSTRING(CAST(CAST('2026-10-09' AS CHAR(10)) AS TEXT) FROM 6 FOR 5) < SUBSTRING(CAST(CAST(p.birthday AS CHAR(10)) AS TEXT) FROM 6 FOR 5) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS age FROM patient AS p JOIN (SELECT id FROM laboratory WHERE hct >= 52 GROUP BY id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2) AS qualified ON qualified.id = p.id WHERE NOT p.birthday IS NULL ORDER BY p.id NULLS FIRST

question: Among patients older than 55 on 2026-10-09 who have at least one abnormal PT result, what percentage are female? Round to two decimals.
evidence: For this task, PT of at least 14 is abnormal.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN p.sex = 'F' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) FROM patient AS p WHERE p.birthday < '1971-10-09' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND l.pt >= 14)

question: How many distinct patients have at least one positive CRP laboratory result and no recorded patient description?
evidence: Plus-marked CRP results indicate positivity.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) FROM patient AS p JOIN laboratory AS l ON l.id = p.id WHERE CAST(l.crp AS TEXT) LIKE '%+' AND p.description IS NULL

question: How many distinct female patients have a normal anti-Scl-70 result and no recorded non-null symptom on any examination?
evidence: Normal anti-Scl-70 is recorded as 'negative' or '0'.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM patient AS p WHERE p.sex = 'F' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND l.sc170 IN ('negative', '0')) AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM examination AS e WHERE e.id = p.id AND NOT e.symptoms IS NULL)

question: Among patients in the thrombosis registry born between 1930 and 1940 inclusive who had laboratory tests, what percentage were inpatients? Please give me just the percentage rounded to two decimal places.
evidence: An inpatient is a patient who was admitted to the hospital; an outpatient is a patient who was followed at the outpatient clinic.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(CASE WHEN (SUM(CASE WHEN admission = '+' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(CASE WHEN admission = '+' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS percentage FROM patient WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(birthday AS TIMESTAMP)) BETWEEN '1930' AND '1940' AND id IN (SELECT id FROM laboratory)

question: Among the lab tests with the strongest anti-ribonuclear protein result (i.e., the highest result value), find the highest total bilirubin level and give me that test's total bilirubin level, the date of the lab test, the patient's ID, sex, and birthday. If several of those tests share the highest total bilirubin level, list each of them, one row per test.
evidence: Anti-ribonuclear protein refers to the anti-RNP antibody lab test; total bilirubin refers to the total serum bilirubin lab test (a liver marker).
SQL: SELECT t2."T-BIL", t2.date, t1.id, t1.sex, t1.birthday FROM patient AS t1 INNER JOIN laboratory AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.id WHERE CASE WHEN (t2.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((t2.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END = (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN (rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END) FROM laboratory) AND t2."T-BIL" = (SELECT MAX("T-BIL") FROM laboratory WHERE CASE WHEN (rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END = (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN (rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END) FROM laboratory))

question: I'm describing our young-patient group and want to show how unusual a raised RNP antibody is in these patients. Could you tell me how many patients in the thrombosis cohort born after 1 January 1960 never had a raised RNP antibody result? A few points: the group should cover every patient born after that date, including patients with no laboratory results at all - they count as never having had a raised result. "Raised" means a result strictly above 10, so a result of exactly 10 doesn't count, and a result of "negative" (no antibody detected) is never raised. Please return just one row with a single integer: the number of these patients.
evidence: RNP: anti-ribonuclear protein antibody; a result of "negative" means no antibody was detected. A raised RNP result is a laboratory result strictly above 10.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM patient AS p WHERE p.birthday > '1960-01-01' AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND NOT l.rnp IS NULL AND l.rnp <> 'negative' AND CASE WHEN (l.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END > 10)

question: Among patients followed at the outpatient clinic who ever had an abnormal anti-SSA result, which one showed the highest anti-RNP titer? Please give me the patient's ID and the anti-RNP titer value. This should cover the hospital's full records across all years, and if several patients tie for the highest anti-RNP titer, list every one of them.
evidence: Abnormal anti-SSA means any SSA result other than negative or 0. "Followed at the outpatient clinic" is the admission status marked with a minus sign. Anti-RNP titer is the strength of the anti-ribonuclear protein result.
SQL: WITH cohort AS (SELECT DISTINCT t1.id FROM patient AS t1 JOIN laboratory AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.id WHERE t1.admission = '-' AND NOT t2.ssa IS NULL AND NOT t2.ssa IN ('negative', '0')), titers AS (SELECT t.id, t.rnp FROM laboratory AS t JOIN cohort AS c ON t.id = c.id WHERE NOT t.rnp IS NULL AND t.rnp <> 'negative') SELECT DISTINCT id, rnp FROM titers WHERE CASE WHEN (rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END = (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN (rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END) FROM titers)

question: I'm studying antibody and platelet profiles in mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD). Can you tell me how many patients diagnosed with MCTD alone - meaning MCTD is their only recorded diagnosis - have had at least one platelet reading within the normal range and at least one anti-RNP antibody level above 5 (strictly greater than 5)? I just need the patient count.
evidence: A platelet level within the normal range means from 100 to 400, both ends included; below 100 or above 400 is outside the normal range.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t1.id) AS patient_count FROM patient AS t1 WHERE t1.diagnosis = 'MCTD' AND t1.id IN (SELECT id FROM laboratory WHERE plt BETWEEN 100 AND 400) AND t1.id IN (SELECT id FROM laboratory WHERE CASE WHEN (rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END > 5)

question: As part of the data-completeness review, I'd like to know how much laboratory follow-up our never-examined patients actually have, split by sex. Could you give me, for each sex (F and M), the average number of laboratory test dates recorded for the patients of that sex who have no examination record at all? Please cover the whole registry, all years, and round the averages to two decimal places. Nothing else needed beyond the two averages.
evidence: F denotes a female patient and M denotes a male patient. A laboratory test date is a date on which laboratory tests were recorded for a patient.
SQL: SELECT p.sex, ROUND(CAST(AVG(COALESCE(c.n_dates, 0)) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_lab_test_dates FROM patient AS p LEFT JOIN (SELECT id, COUNT(*) AS n_dates FROM laboratory GROUP BY id) AS c ON c.id = p.id WHERE p.sex IN ('F', 'M') AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM examination WHERE examination.id = p.id) GROUP BY p.sex

question: I'm reviewing autoimmune antibody profiles in our thrombosis registry. Among the female patients who were admitted to the hospital as inpatients, I need to find the laboratory test record with the highest anti-DNA antibody level, for a case review. Please give me the patient ID, the laboratory test date of that record, and the anti-DNA antibody level reported in it - nothing else. Order the results by patient ID, and if several lab test records share the highest level, list each of them.
evidence: Anti-DNA antibody level means the anti-DNA test result recorded in the laboratory tests.
SQL: SELECT p.id, l.date, l.dna AS anti_dna FROM patient AS p JOIN laboratory AS l ON l.id = p.id WHERE p.sex = 'F' AND p.admission = '+' AND NOT l.dna IS NULL AND CASE WHEN (l.dna) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l.dna) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END = (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN (l2.dna) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l2.dna) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END) FROM laboratory AS l2 JOIN patient AS p2 ON p2.id = l2.id WHERE p2.sex = 'F' AND p2.admission = '+' AND NOT l2.dna IS NULL) ORDER BY p.id NULLS FIRST

question: Among patients who have ever had an anti-ribonuclear protein (anti-RNP) antibody result above 16 on any laboratory reading, whenever it was taken, how many were admitted to the hospital and how many were followed at the outpatient clinic? Please give one row per care setting, using '+' for admitted to the hospital and '-' for followed at the outpatient clinic, showing the number of such patients in each setting.
SQL: SELECT p.admission AS care_setting, COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS patients FROM patient AS p WHERE p.admission IN ('+', '-') AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND CASE WHEN (l.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END > 16) GROUP BY p.admission ORDER BY p.admission COLLATE "C" NULLS FIRST

question: Among the thrombosis registry patients followed at the outpatient clinic, how many have a non-normal hematocrit and an anti-ribonuclear protein measurement above 16? I need a single count. A patient counts if they have at least one hematocrit reading outside the normal range, regardless of test date, and at least one anti-ribonuclear protein reading above 16, regardless of test date. Include every patient in the registry, not only those with a recorded thrombosis event.
evidence: Hematocrit is normal when the value lies strictly between 29 and 52; outside that range it is abnormal. A negative anti-ribonuclear protein result means none was detected.
SQL: WITH cohort AS (SELECT DISTINCT p.id FROM patient AS p JOIN laboratory AS l ON p.id = l.id WHERE p.admission = '-' AND (l.hct >= 52 OR l.hct <= 29)) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT l.id) AS patient_count FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id IN (SELECT id FROM cohort) AND NOT l.rnp IS NULL AND CASE WHEN (l.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END > 16

question: For the patients followed at our thrombosis unit's outpatient clinic, what is the highest anti-ribonuclear protein value on record? I just need that single highest value for my review.
evidence: Anti-ribonuclear protein (anti-RNP) is a blood antibody test result recorded for patients.
SQL: SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN (l.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END) AS highest_anti_ribonuclear_protein_value FROM laboratory AS l INNER JOIN patient AS p ON p.id = l.id WHERE p.admission = '-'

question: I'm studying patients who carry exactly the rheumatoid arthritis and Sjögren's syndrome overlap. Please look at each patient's own record and find those whose record names exactly rheumatoid arthritis and Sjögren's syndrome, in either order, and no other disease – a disease recorded only as suspected does not count as a diagnosis. For those patients, considering their whole recorded laboratory history regardless of date, I need two numbers: how many have had at least one laboratory result showing a normal platelet level, and how many have never had a laboratory result showing a normal platelet level – count a patient with no laboratory results at all as never having had a normal platelet result.
evidence: Rheumatoid arthritis is recorded as the code RA and Sjögren's syndrome as the code SJS. A normal platelet level means a platelet count above 100 and below 400.
SQL: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND l.plt > 100 AND l.plt < 400) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS had_normal_platelet_result, SUM(CASE WHEN NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND l.plt > 100 AND l.plt < 400) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS never_normal_platelet_result FROM patient AS p WHERE LENGTH(CAST(LOWER(REPLACE(p.diagnosis, ' ', '')) AS TEXT)) - LENGTH(CAST(REPLACE(LOWER(REPLACE(p.diagnosis, ' ', '')), ',', '') AS TEXT)) = 1 AND REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(LOWER(REPLACE(p.diagnosis, ' ', '')), 'ra', ''), 'sjs', ''), ',', '') = ''

question: I'm writing a report section on abnormal total protein in female SLE patients and need one summary figure. Among the laboratory records of female patients diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus at an examination visit, where total protein is above the normal bound of 8.5, what is the average deviation of total protein from that bound across all qualifying records, rounded to three decimal places? A few points: an examination visit counts as an SLE diagnosis when systemic lupus erythematosus is among the diseases that visit's diagnosis lists, whether it's the only one or appears alongside others; the normal bound is 8.5, and a record counts as above the bound only when its TP is greater than 8.5; a record's deviation is its TP minus 8.5; and the average should cover all qualifying laboratory records across all dates.
evidence: SLE: systemic lupus erythematosus.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(l.tp - 8.5) AS DECIMAL), 3) AS avg_tp_deviation FROM patient AS p INNER JOIN laboratory AS l ON l.id = p.id WHERE p.sex = 'F' AND l.tp > 8.5 AND p.id IN (SELECT id FROM examination WHERE CAST(diagnosis AS TEXT) LIKE '%SLE%')

question: What percentage of patients in the registry with a diagnosis of psoriatic arthritis were born in 1960 or later? Please give a single percentage rounded to one decimal place.
evidence: Psoriatic arthritis is a rheumatologic diagnosis recorded for patients in the registry.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(CASE WHEN (SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(birthday AS TIMESTAMP)) >= '1960' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(birthday AS TIMESTAMP)) >= '1960' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS percentage FROM patient WHERE LOWER(TRIM(CAST(diagnosis AS TEXT))) = 'psoriatic arthritis'

question: I'm putting together a demographic summary of our low-albumin patients. Could you tell me how many patients with an albumin measurement below 3.5 are female and how many are male? I'd like one row per sex group showing the sex (F or M) and the number of patients in that group.
evidence: F stands for female and M stands for male.
SQL: SELECT t1.sex AS sex, COUNT(DISTINCT t1.id) AS patient_count FROM patient AS t1 INNER JOIN laboratory AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.id WHERE t2.alb < 3.5 AND t1.sex IN ('F', 'M') GROUP BY t1.sex ORDER BY t1.sex NULLS FIRST

question: I'm preparing a department audit on how often anti-ribonuclear protein testing comes back clearly elevated among the women in the thrombosis cohort. Among the women in the cohort, what percentage of those with an available anti-ribonuclear protein test result had a clearly elevated result? Please give me the percentage rounded to two decimal places on the 0-100 scale. Note: elevated means a titer strictly above 1:64. Patients never tested for anti-ribonuclear protein should be excluded from both the numerator and the denominator, while a negative reading counts as an available result and is never elevated.
evidence: Anti-ribonuclear protein is a serology test reported as a titer reading; a negative reading is a result of zero titer.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(CASE WHEN (SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND CASE WHEN (l.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END > 64) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND CASE WHEN (l.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END > 64) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS pct FROM patient AS p WHERE p.sex = 'F' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND NOT l.rnp IS NULL)

question: What was the average age of the register's patients in 1999, considering all patients who ever had marked or worse proteinuria on a lab test? Age in 1999 means 1999 minus the patient's year of birth. Marked or worse proteinuria means grade 3 or 4 on the original scale, or 300, 1000 or above on the scale used since 1987; traces and grades 1 and 2 don't count. I just need the one average number, in years.
evidence: U-PRO = proteinuria result of a laboratory test; TR = traces of proteinuria.
SQL: SELECT AVG(CAST('1999' - CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(birthday AS TIMESTAMP))) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(birthday AS TIMESTAMP))) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END AS DOUBLE PRECISION)) AS average_age FROM patient WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM laboratory WHERE "U-PRO" IN ('3', '4') OR CASE WHEN (REPLACE("U-PRO", '>=', '')) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((REPLACE("U-PRO", '>=', '')) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END >= 300)

question: I'm looking at patients whose anti-ribonuclear protein antibody measurement came out higher than 32. Of those patients, how many were women and how many were men? Note that 'higher than 32' means strictly above 32, not equal to it, and a patient qualifies if any of their laboratory measurements exceeded 32.
evidence: A woman means a patient recorded as F, and a man means a patient recorded as M.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t1.sex = 'F' THEN t1.id END) AS women, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t1.sex = 'M' THEN t1.id END) AS men FROM patient AS t1 INNER JOIN laboratory AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.id WHERE CASE WHEN (t2.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((t2.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END > 32

question: I'm studying how early in life a patient in the thrombosis cohort can show a high anti-ribonuclear protein (RNP) reading. Please tell me the youngest age, in whole years, at which a patient had a laboratory test showing an anti-RNP result of at least 64. Age in whole years means the year of the test minus the year of birth. If several patients or tests share that youngest age, report that age once. I just need that single youngest age value, nothing else.
evidence: Anti-ribonuclear protein (RNP): an antibody measured in the laboratory panel, reported as a titer number or as negative.
SQL: SELECT MIN(EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(t2.date AS TIMESTAMP)) - EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(t1.birthday AS TIMESTAMP))) AS youngest_age FROM patient AS t1 INNER JOIN laboratory AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.id WHERE CASE WHEN (t2.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((t2.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END >= 64

question: For the patients in the registry with a diagnosis of psoriatic arthritis, I'd like to know: (1) the total number of laboratory tests recorded for these patients, counting tests from all dates, and (2) how many of these patients have no laboratory tests recorded at all (i.e., patients with no laboratory record count as having no laboratory tests).
evidence: Psoriatic arthritis: a rheumatic disease diagnosis.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(l.id) AS total_tests, SUM(CASE WHEN l.id IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS no_test_patients FROM patient AS p LEFT JOIN laboratory AS l ON l.id = p.id WHERE LOWER(p.diagnosis) = 'psoriatic arthritis'

question: For our annual report, I need the count of patients in the thrombosis cohort who showed thrombosis at any examination performed between 01/01/1997 and 12/31/1997, inclusive. Please give me just that number of patients.
evidence: Thrombosis refers to the formation of blood clots, recorded at each examination as a graded finding.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT id) AS patient_count FROM examination WHERE "Examination Date" BETWEEN '1997-01-01' AND '1997-12-31' AND thrombosis > 0

question: I'm putting together a monitoring checklist for SLE patients. Among the thrombotic episodes recorded for patients diagnosed with SLE, which single symptom appears most frequently? I just need the symptom name back. Please count all recorded episodes with no date restriction. If two symptoms are equally frequent, give the one that comes first alphabetically. Note that a patient counts as having SLE only if their own diagnosis record names SLE among their diseases.
evidence: SLE: systemic lupus erythematosus, an autoimmune disease. Thrombotic episode: an episode in which the patient experienced thrombosis.
SQL: WITH episodes AS (SELECT e.symptoms FROM examination AS e JOIN patient AS p ON e.id = p.id WHERE POSITION('SLE' IN p.diagnosis) > 0 AND e.thrombosis > 0) SELECT symptoms FROM episodes GROUP BY symptoms HAVING COUNT(*) = (SELECT MAX(n) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM episodes GROUP BY symptoms) AS __photo_derived_1) ORDER BY symptoms NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1

question: In our autoimmune disease cohort, what percentage of thrombosis patients were diagnosed with SLE at the examination visit? I need the percentage on a 0-100 scale, rounded to two decimal places. Please use the diagnosis recorded at the examination visit, not the diagnosis on the patient's overall file. This is for a write-up on which diagnoses accompany thrombotic events in this cohort.
evidence: SLE: systemic lupus erythematosus, an autoimmune disease; thrombosis: formation of a blood clot within a blood vessel
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(CASE WHEN (COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN CAST(diagnosis AS TEXT) LIKE '%SLE%' THEN id END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN CAST(diagnosis AS TEXT) LIKE '%SLE%' THEN id END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT id), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS percentage FROM examination WHERE thrombosis > 0

question: For the thrombosis cohort, I need to describe how long admitted patients typically wait from their first hospital visit until their first examination. Please give me the average delay in days across admitted patients, based on each patient's own first visit and first examination, rounded to the nearest whole number. A patient counts as admitted whenever her admission entry carries a plus sign, regardless of anything else in that entry.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(gap) AS DECIMAL), 0) AS average_days FROM (SELECT t1.id, MIN((EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM CAST(t3."Examination Date" AS TIMESTAMP)) / 86400.0)) - (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM CAST(t1."First Date" AS TIMESTAMP)) / 86400.0) AS gap FROM patient AS t1 INNER JOIN examination AS t3 ON t1.id = t3.id WHERE CAST(t1.admission AS TEXT) LIKE '%+%' GROUP BY t1.id) AS __photo_derived_1

question: For a demographics summary of our 1994 laboratory cohort: how many female patients and how many male patients had a normal AST glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase (GOT) index on laboratory tests done during the calendar year 1994? Please give me the patient count for each sex (F and M) and nothing else. The calendar year 1994 means laboratory test dates from 1994-01-01 through 1994-12-31.
evidence: AST glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase (GOT) index within normal range means a value below 60.
SQL: SELECT p.sex, COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS patient_count FROM patient AS p INNER JOIN laboratory AS l ON p.id = l.id WHERE l.got < 60 AND l.date BETWEEN '1994-01-01' AND '1994-12-31' AND p.sex IN ('F', 'M') GROUP BY p.sex

question: I'm reviewing thrombosis ward patients and need a chart-review list. Can you give me, for every patient who had a single lab visit where the panel showed both an LDH result strictly between 600 and 800 and urine protein of 300 mg/dL or more, the patient ID and their completed age in years as of 2026-10-09? If any one visit's panel shows both findings, that patient qualifies. Please note that a proteinuria result reported as "at least" a level counts at that stated level (e.g., "at least 300" counts as 300 mg/dL or more), and a plain number is in mg/dL. Nothing else needed, just patient ID and completed age.
evidence: Proteinuria result codes: '-' means negative, 'TR' means trace.
SQL: SELECT p.id, CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST('2026-10-09' AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST('2026-10-09' AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END - CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST(CAST(p.birthday AS CHAR(10)) AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST(CAST(p.birthday AS CHAR(10)) AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END - CASE WHEN SUBSTRING(CAST('2026-10-09' AS TEXT) FROM 6 FOR 5) < SUBSTRING(CAST(CAST(p.birthday AS CHAR(10)) AS TEXT) FROM 6 FOR 5) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS age FROM patient AS p WHERE NOT p.birthday IS NULL AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND l.ldh > 600 AND l.ldh < 800 AND CASE WHEN (REPLACE(REPLACE(CAST(l."U-PRO" AS TEXT), '>', ''), '=', '')) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((REPLACE(REPLACE(CAST(l."U-PRO" AS TEXT), '>', ''), '=', '')) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END >= 300) ORDER BY p.id NULLS FIRST

question: For the RA patients whose urea nitrogen was within the normal index, how many more women are there than men? Please give me a single integer: the count of women minus the count of men. Women means sex F and men means sex M, and the difference may be negative.
evidence: Within the UN normal index means UN < 30; RA means a Diagnosis of RA.
SQL: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN sex = 'F' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN sex = 'M' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS women_minus_men FROM patient WHERE diagnosis = 'RA' AND id IN (SELECT id FROM laboratory WHERE un < 30)

question: I'm reviewing renal function in the thrombosis cohort and want to compare how often creatinine runs out of the normal range between men and women.
