For each sex (M and F), please give me: the number of patients of that sex with at least one creatinine result out of the normal range, the total number of patients of that sex, and the share those patients represent of that sex's total as a percentage rounded to one decimal place. Rules: out of the normal range means a creatinine result of 1.5 or higher; the total per sex counts every patient of that sex on file whether or not any lab result exists for them.
evidence: Creatinine out of the normal range: a CRE value of 1.5 or higher. Male is SEX = 'M'; female is SEX = 'F'.
SQL: SELECT p.sex AS sex, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN l.cre >= 1.5 THEN p.id END) AS out_of_range_patients, COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS total_patients, ROUND(CAST(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN l.cre >= 1.5 THEN p.id END) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT p.id), 0) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS share_pct FROM patient AS p LEFT JOIN laboratory AS l ON p.id = l.id WHERE p.sex IN ('M', 'F') GROUP BY p.sex ORDER BY p.sex NULLS FIRST

question: In this cohort, I want to compare the most extreme total cholesterol (T-CHO) readings between patients admitted to the hospital and those followed at the outpatient clinic. Please give me, for each of the two groups, the single highest T-CHO reading, along with the admission status ('+' admitted, '-' outpatient) and the patient ID whose reading is the group's highest. List the admitted group's row first, then the outpatient group's. If several patients tie at a group's highest reading, list each of them.
evidence: T-CHO: total cholesterol. '+': the patient was admitted to the hospital. '-': the patient was followed at the outpatient clinic.
SQL: SELECT l."T-CHO" AS "T-CHO", p.admission AS status, p.id FROM patient AS p JOIN laboratory AS l ON l.id = p.id JOIN (SELECT p2.admission AS adm, MAX(l2."T-CHO") AS mx FROM patient AS p2 JOIN laboratory AS l2 ON l2.id = p2.id WHERE p2.admission IN ('+', '-') GROUP BY p2.admission) AS t ON t.adm = p.admission AND t.mx = l."T-CHO" ORDER BY CASE p.admission WHEN '+' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END NULLS FIRST, p.id NULLS FIRST

question: Among patients whose first visit to the hospital was in 1991, which patients mounted the strongest anti-ribonuclear protein (RNP) response? Please give me the patient ID and anti-RNP level for every patient tied at the highest recorded level. Only consider patients for whom a level was actually recorded.
evidence: anti-ribonuclear protein (RNP): an antibody titer; a higher titer means a higher level.
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT t1.id, t2.rnp FROM patient AS t1 INNER JOIN laboratory AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.id WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(t1."First Date" AS TIMESTAMP)) = '1991' AND NOT t2.rnp IS NULL AND CASE WHEN (t2.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((t2.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END = (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN (l.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END) FROM patient AS p INNER JOIN laboratory AS l ON p.id = l.id WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(p."First Date" AS TIMESTAMP)) = '1991' AND NOT l.rnp IS NULL)

question: I'm reviewing the 1991 lab records of the thrombosis cohort, checking whether heavy proteinuria went hand in hand with lower hematocrit that year, as a sign of anemia in kidney involvement. Among the laboratory tests done in 1991 that reported proteinuria of at least 300 mg/dL, what was the average hematocrit value? Please note: proteinuria levels are measured in mg/dL; a proteinuria result reported only as a lower bound that the reading reached or exceeded still counts as being at least that level; a trace result is below 30 mg/dL; and tests without a hematocrit reading should be left out of the average.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(hct) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS average_hematocrit FROM laboratory WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(date AS TIMESTAMP)) = '1991' AND CASE WHEN (REPLACE("U-PRO", '>=', '')) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((REPLACE("U-PRO", '>=', '')) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END >= 300

question: I'm putting together a care-setting summary of severe SLE cases for the rheumatology department. Among patients diagnosed with SLE, considering only those whose only diagnosis is SLE and who had abnormally high proteinuria, how many were admitted to the hospital and how many were followed at the outpatient clinic? Please count each patient based on their full history at the hospital.
evidence: Abnormally high proteinuria means a proteinuria level of 30 or higher.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t1.admission = '+' THEN t1.id END) AS admitted_to_hospital, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t1.admission = '-' THEN t1.id END) AS followed_at_outpatient_clinic FROM patient AS t1 INNER JOIN laboratory AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.id WHERE t1.diagnosis = 'SLE' AND CASE WHEN (t2."U-PRO") IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((t2."U-PRO") AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END >= 30

question: How many patients in our thrombosis ward are followed at the outpatient clinic (rather than admitted) with a normal Rheumatoid Factor and no positive measure of degree of coagulation? Please give me a single number. For context: a normal Rheumatoid Factor is '-' or '+-', a positive measure of degree of coagulation is '+' on any of the coagulation measures (KCT, RVVT, LAC), and an outpatient-clinic patient is one with Admission = '-'. If a patient has no recorded coagulation measure, count them as having no positive measure.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t1.id) AS patient_count FROM patient AS t1 WHERE t1.admission = '-' AND t1.id IN (SELECT id FROM laboratory WHERE ra IN ('-', '+-')) AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM examination AS e WHERE e.id = t1.id AND (e.kct = '+' OR e.rvvt = '+' OR e.lac = '+'))

question: I'm reviewing our cohort and need to identify patients whose most recent laboratory sample on file was collected after 1 January 1997 (strictly later than that date) and whose most recent anti-Scl-70 result on file was normal. Please return only the patient IDs for these patients.
evidence: anti-Scl-70: anti-topoisomerase I antibody, an autoantibody measured in the laboratory. A normal anti-Scl-70 result is a result of 'negative' or 0.
SQL: WITH lab AS (SELECT id, MAX(date) AS lastdate FROM laboratory GROUP BY id), last_sc AS (SELECT s.id AS id, s.sc170 AS sc170 FROM laboratory AS s WHERE NOT s.sc170 IS NULL AND s.date = (SELECT MAX(s2.date) FROM laboratory AS s2 WHERE s2.id = s.id AND NOT s2.sc170 IS NULL)) SELECT l.id FROM lab AS l JOIN last_sc AS c ON c.id = l.id WHERE l.lastdate > '1997-01-01' AND c.sc170 IN ('negative', '0') ORDER BY l.id NULLS FIRST

question: I'd like to know how many patients on record have both an abnormal anti-SSA antibody result and a positive proteinuria finding at some point in their record. Abnormal anti-SSA means any recorded test result other than negative or zero. Proteinuria counts as positive if any urine test on file returned a result other than negative or none. The two findings don't need to come from the same visit – I'm looking across each patient's entire record. Please just give me the number of such patients.
evidence: anti-SSA: anti-SSA antibody laboratory test; proteinuria: protein found in the urine
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM patient AS t1 WHERE t1.id IN (SELECT id FROM laboratory WHERE NOT ssa IS NULL AND NOT ssa IN ('negative', '0')) AND t1.id IN (SELECT id FROM laboratory WHERE NOT "U-PRO" IS NULL AND NOT "U-PRO" IN ('-', '0'))

question: For a study of laboratory test patterns, I need to size a cohort. How many female patients have at least one anti-DNA antibody level below 8 (the upper bound of the normal range)? Any laboratory visit of the patient qualifies; there is no time scope. I just need that single count back.
evidence: anti-DNA level: the anti-DNA antibody concentration measured in the laboratory tests
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t1.id) AS patient_count FROM patient AS t1 INNER JOIN laboratory AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.id WHERE t1.sex = 'F' AND CASE WHEN (t2.dna) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((t2.dna) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END < 8

question: For patients admitted to the hospital, how many never had an alkaliphosphatase level above the normal ceiling in their lab results? I just need that single count.
evidence: A patient is admitted when their status is anything other than the outpatient-clinic code; the outpatient-clinic code is '-' and admitted is '+'. A normal alkaliphosphatase level is below 300; a level of 300 or more is above the normal ceiling.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS admitted_never_high_alp FROM patient WHERE admission <> '-' AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory WHERE laboratory.id = patient.id AND alp >= 300)

question: Among patients in the thrombosis prediction database whose creatinine level is normal (below 1.5), what is the highest anti-RNP antibody level recorded? Please return just that single number; if several measurements tie for the highest, the tied value is the answer.
evidence: Anti-RNP antibody = anti-ribonuclear protein antibody, measured by the laboratory panel.
SQL: SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN (t2.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((t2.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END) AS max_rnp_level FROM patient AS t1 INNER JOIN laboratory AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.id WHERE t2.cre < 1.5

question: I'd like to see how severe anemia is distributed across the sexes in the registry. Please give me, for each sex, the number of patients of that sex who ever showed severe anemia on any lab test, with the rows labeled 'female' and 'male'.
evidence: Severe anemia means a hemoglobin value below 7.0 g/dL on a lab test.
SQL: SELECT CASE p.sex WHEN 'F' THEN 'female' WHEN 'M' THEN 'male' END AS sex, COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS severe_anemia_patients FROM patient AS p INNER JOIN laboratory AS l ON l.id = p.id WHERE l.hgb < 7.0 GROUP BY p.sex HAVING p.sex IN ('F', 'M')

question: Among the laboratory tests whose AST glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase (GOT) index was above the normal range (60 or higher), I want to find the test with the highest anti-ribonuclear protein reading. Please give me the patient's identification, the date of the laboratory test, and the anti-ribonuclear protein reading for that test. If several tests tie for the highest anti-ribonuclear protein reading, list every one of them. The date should be the date the laboratory test was performed.
evidence: AST glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase (GOT) index: a liver enzyme measurement; values of 60 or higher are considered above the normal range.
SQL: SELECT id, date, rnp FROM laboratory WHERE got >= 60 AND CASE WHEN (rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END = (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN (rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END) FROM laboratory WHERE got >= 60)

question: I'm screening our thrombosis cohort for a study and need an eligibility count. How many patients born after 1980-01-01 had at least one abnormal fibrinogen result or at least one severe proteinuria result? A fibrinogen result is abnormal if it's below 150 or above 450; the normal range 150-450 is inclusive. Severe proteinuria means 300 mg/dl or more on the urinalysis scale, i.e., dipstick 3+ or 4+; trace, 1+ and 2+ are not severe. I just need the single count, nothing else.
evidence: Urinalysis protein scale: '-' and '0' mean no protein, 'TR' means trace, grades '1','2','3','4' mean 1+ to 4+, where 3+ is about 300 mg/dl and 4+ about 1000 mg/dl or more; a plain number is a reading in mg/dl, and a '>=' prefix means 'or more'.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS patient_count FROM patient AS p JOIN laboratory AS l ON p.id = l.id WHERE p.birthday > '1980-01-01' AND ((l.fg < 150 OR l.fg > 450) OR (l."U-PRO" IN ('3', '4') OR CASE WHEN (REPLACE(l."U-PRO", '>=', '')) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((REPLACE(l."U-PRO", '>=', '')) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END >= 300))

question: In the thrombosis and autoimmune-disease cohort, I want to compare how often lactate dehydrogenase stays in the normal range between patients admitted to the hospital and patients followed at the outpatient clinic. Please give me one row per patient group showing the number of lactate dehydrogenase measurements within the normal range recorded for that group, with the admitted group's row first. Label the rows 'admitted to the hospital' for the Admission = '+' group and 'followed at the outpatient clinic' for the Admission = '-' group. Every laboratory measurement recorded for those patients across the whole study period counts. Nothing else is needed.
evidence: The normal range for lactate dehydrogenase means a value below 500.
SQL: SELECT CASE WHEN p.admission = '+' THEN 'admitted to the hospital' ELSE 'followed at the outpatient clinic' END AS patient_group, COUNT(*) AS normal_ldh_measurements FROM patient AS p JOIN laboratory AS l ON p.id = l.id WHERE p.admission IN ('+', '-') AND l.ldh < 500 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY patient_group

question: For patients whose sex is not recorded in the registry, I need two counts for the annual quality report: how many have at least one laboratory result on file, and of those, how many have at least one laboratory result showing elevated total bilirubin. The report covers all dates.
evidence: A patient's sex is not recorded when the registry holds no sex entry for that patient. Total bilirubin of 2.0 or higher counts as elevated.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t2.id) AS patients_with_lab_results, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t2."T-BIL" >= 2.0 THEN t2.id END) AS patients_with_elevated_bilirubin FROM patient AS t1 INNER JOIN laboratory AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.id WHERE t1.sex IS NULL OR t1.sex = ''

question: For an audit, I need the number of admitted female patients born between 1945 and 1989 (inclusive) who have an ANA examination where the observed pattern is exactly P, with no other pattern alongside it. Please return just that single count.
evidence: ANA pattern: the pattern observed in the ANA examination, e.g. 'P' or 'P,S'; the admission mark starting with a plus indicates the patient was admitted.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t1.id) FROM patient AS t1 INNER JOIN examination AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.id WHERE CAST(t1.admission AS TEXT) LIKE '+%' AND t1.sex = 'F' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(t1.birthday AS TIMESTAMP)) BETWEEN '1945' AND '1989' AND t2."ANA Pattern" = 'P'

question: I'm screening outpatient clinic patients with anemia for rheumatologic autoimmunity. Among patients who were followed as outpatients (rather than admitted to the hospital) and who ever had a hemoglobin value below 10 on any lab test, who showed the strongest anti-ribonuclear protein antibody response? Please return, for every patient whose anti-ribonuclear protein antibody level reached the highest point ever recorded on their lab tests (list all of them if several share that highest level): the patient ID, the patient's sex, and that highest-ever recorded anti-ribonuclear protein antibody level. Nothing else.
evidence: Anti-ribonuclear protein refers to the antibody measured in the laboratory tests (anti-RNP).
SQL: SELECT p.id, p.sex, MAX(CASE WHEN (r.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((r.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END) AS highest_level FROM patient AS p JOIN laboratory AS r ON r.id = p.id WHERE p.admission = '-' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS h WHERE h.id = p.id AND h.hgb < 10) GROUP BY p.id, p.sex HAVING MAX(CASE WHEN (r.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((r.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END) = (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN (r2.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((r2.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END) FROM patient AS p2 JOIN laboratory AS r2 ON r2.id = p2.id WHERE p2.admission = '-' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS h2 WHERE h2.id = p2.id AND h2.hgb < 10))

question: Among the patients in the thrombosis prediction data, how many have a first laboratory record showing both a normal glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase (GOT) level and an elevated anti-ribonuclear protein (RNP) concentration? By normal GOT I mean a value below 60, and by elevated RNP I mean a value above 10. By first laboratory record I mean the one with the earliest laboratory test date for that patient. I need just a single count of these patients.
evidence: GOT stands for glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase (also known as aspartate aminotransferase, AST); RNP stands for anti-ribonuclear protein.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT l.id) FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.date = (SELECT MIN(date) FROM laboratory WHERE id = l.id) AND l.got < 60 AND CASE WHEN (l.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END > 10

question: I'm reviewing the current kidney involvement status of the thrombosis prediction cohort. For every patient who has had a proteinuria test, I need their patient identifier, sex, the date of their most recent proteinuria test, and the proteinuria level measured on that test. "Most recent" means the latest proteinuria test by test date.
evidence: A proteinuria test is a test that measures the level of protein in the urine; the proteinuria level is the result value it reports.
SQL: SELECT p.id AS patient_id, p.sex AS sex, l.date AS most_recent_test_date, l."U-PRO" AS proteinuria_level FROM patient AS p JOIN laboratory AS l ON l.id = p.id WHERE NOT l."U-PRO" IS NULL AND l.date = (SELECT MAX(l2.date) FROM laboratory AS l2 WHERE l2.id = l.id AND NOT l2."U-PRO" IS NULL) ORDER BY p.id NULLS FIRST

question: I'm screening the thrombosis cohort for a follow-up panel. Can you give me the patient ids of outpatients (patients followed at the outpatient clinic rather than admitted) whose creatinine phosphokinase is in the normal range (below 250) but whose anti-ribonuclear protein antibody level is above 4 (strictly greater than 4)? Please note that an anti-ribonuclear protein result reported as negative means no antibody was detected. I just need the patient ids, nothing else.
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT t1.id FROM patient AS t1 INNER JOIN laboratory AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.id WHERE t2.cpk < 250 AND t1.admission = '-' AND CASE WHEN (t2.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((t2.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END > 4

question: I'd like to know how many patients in the cohort have a positive anti-ribonuclear protein (RNP) result but no thrombosis. A positive RNP result means the anti-ribonuclear protein level is above 0, and no thrombosis means the thrombosis degree is 0. Please return just the number of such patients.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t1.id) FROM examination AS t1 INNER JOIN laboratory AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.id WHERE CASE WHEN (t2.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((t2.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END > 0 AND t1.thrombosis = 0

question: I'm reviewing patients with an elevated anti-ribonuclear protein result. Among patients who ever had an anti-ribonuclear protein result of 16 or higher, I want to follow up the three whose liver enzymes stayed in the normal range. The normal range for GPT is below 60. For each patient, take their highest GPT value among their laboratory tests that fall in the normal range. Rank patients from that highest value down; if two patients share the same value, the one with the smaller patient ID comes first. Please return exactly three patients, one row per patient, with only each patient's Birthday.
evidence: GPT stands for glutamic pyruvic transaminase, a liver enzyme; anti-ribonuclear protein is an autoantibody measured in laboratory tests.
SQL: SELECT t1.birthday FROM patient AS t1 INNER JOIN laboratory AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.id WHERE t2.gpt < 60 AND t1.id IN (SELECT id FROM laboratory WHERE CASE WHEN (rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END >= 16) GROUP BY t1.id ORDER BY MAX(t2.gpt) DESC NULLS LAST, t1.id ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 3

question: I'm trying to size a subgroup in the thrombosis cohort: how many female patients had a normal prothrombin time (below 14 seconds) along with an elevated anti-ribonuclear protein level (16 or higher)? Please use the prothrombin time and anti-ribonuclear protein level from the same laboratory record for each patient. I just need the count of such female patients.
evidence: Normal prothrombin time: below 14 seconds. Elevated anti-ribonuclear protein: a measured level of 16 or higher.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t1.id) AS patient_count FROM patient AS t1 INNER JOIN laboratory AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.id WHERE t1.sex = 'F' AND t2.pt < 14 AND CASE WHEN (t2.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((t2.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END >= 16

question: Among inpatients (admission marked '+'), find the laboratory anti-DNA antibody test with the highest recorded level, and report the patient's age in completed years at that test date and the patient's diagnosis. If several tests share the highest level, use the one with the earliest test date.
evidence: An inpatient is a patient admitted to the hospital: the Admission record is marked '+' (a '-' marks an outpatient followed at the clinic). Age in completed years means the age at the last birthday reached on or before the test date. The anti-DNA antibody level is a laboratory reading reported alongside the other antibody tests.
SQL: WITH cand AS (SELECT p.diagnosis, CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(l.date AS TIMESTAMP))) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(l.date AS TIMESTAMP))) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END - CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(p.birthday AS TIMESTAMP))) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(p.birthday AS TIMESTAMP))) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END - CASE WHEN SUBSTRING(CAST(l.date AS TEXT) FROM 6 FOR 5) < SUBSTRING(CAST(p.birthday AS TEXT) FROM 6 FOR 5) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS age, CASE WHEN (l.dna) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l.dna) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END AS level, l.date AS test_date FROM patient AS p JOIN laboratory AS l ON p.id = l.id WHERE NOT l.dna IS NULL AND NOT p.birthday IS NULL AND p.admission = '+') SELECT age, diagnosis FROM cand WHERE level = (SELECT MAX(level) FROM cand) ORDER BY test_date NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1

question: I need to find lupus patients with liver lab abnormalities. Can you give me the ID and sex of every patient who has at least one total bilirubin (T-BIL) result at or above the upper normal limit of 1.2 mg/dL, and who has a confirmed diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)? SLE counts if it's among the patient's confirmed diagnoses, even when other diseases are diagnosed or suspected alongside it, but a suspected SLE alone doesn't count. The diagnosis should be the patient's overall diagnosis, not something noted at a single examination. Please order results by sex, then patient ID, and return only the ID and sex.
evidence: T-BIL: total bilirubin; SLE: systemic lupus erythematosus; susp.: suspected, not a confirmed diagnosis
SQL: SELECT p.id, p.sex FROM patient AS p WHERE p.id IN (SELECT id FROM laboratory WHERE "T-BIL" >= 1.2) AND POSITION(',' || 'SLE' || ',' IN ',' || REPLACE(p.diagnosis, ' ', '') || ',') > 0 ORDER BY p.sex NULLS FIRST, p.id NULLS FIRST

question: I'm reviewing how often older female patients show elevated anti-RNP antibody results, split by whether they were admitted to the hospital or followed at the outpatient clinic. For female patients aged at least 50 as of 2026-10-09, please give me a two-row breakdown by care setting (admitted to the hospital vs. followed at the outpatient clinic), showing for each setting how many patients had at least one anti-RNP laboratory result of at least 4, and how many had no such result. A patient's admission marker of '+' counts as admitted to the hospital and '-' counts as followed at the outpatient clinic; patients with any other admission marker are out of scope. Order the two rows alphabetically by care setting.
evidence: anti-RNP: anti-ribonuclear protein antibody, measured in laboratory results; admission marker: the patient's recorded admission sign.
SQL: SELECT CASE WHEN p.admission = '+' THEN 'admitted to the hospital' ELSE 'followed at the outpatient clinic' END AS care_setting, SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND CASE WHEN (l.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END >= 4) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS patients_with_rnp_at_least_4, SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND CASE WHEN (l.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END >= 4) THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS patients_without_such_result FROM patient AS p WHERE p.sex = 'F' AND p.birthday <= CAST((CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST('2026-10-09' AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST('2026-10-09' AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END - 50) || SUBSTRING(CAST('2026-10-09' AS TEXT) FROM 5) AS DATE) AND p.admission IN ('+', '-') GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY care_setting NULLS FIRST

question: I'm putting together a cohort summary and need one number: how many patients followed at the outpatient clinic (admission marker '-') have a most recent IgG lab result of 2000 or higher? By most recent, I mean the IgG measurement with the greatest laboratory date for that patient - since a patient has at most one lab record per date, there should be no ambiguity.
SQL: WITH latest_igg AS (SELECT id, MAX(date) AS lastdate FROM laboratory WHERE NOT igg IS NULL GROUP BY id) SELECT COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM patient AS p JOIN latest_igg AS li ON li.id = p.id JOIN laboratory AS l ON l.id = li.id AND l.date = li.lastdate WHERE p.admission = '-' AND l.igg >= 2000

question: Among all patients diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus, I want to find the patient whose anti-DNA test result was the strongest ever recorded for that disease. Please report the patient's identifier, the patient's diagnosis, and that patient's highest anti-DNA test result, using the number exactly as the test wrote it. If several patients tie for the highest anti-DNA result, list every tied patient.
evidence: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is an autoimmune disease; anti-DNA is an antibody test reported as a number.
SQL: WITH ranked AS (SELECT p.id AS patient_id, p.diagnosis AS diagnosis, l.dna AS highest_anti_dna, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.id ORDER BY CASE WHEN (l.dna) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l.dna) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END DESC NULLS LAST, l.date DESC NULLS LAST) AS rn FROM patient AS p INNER JOIN laboratory AS l ON p.id = l.id WHERE CAST(p.diagnosis AS TEXT) LIKE '%SLE%' AND NOT l.dna IS NULL), best AS (SELECT patient_id, diagnosis, highest_anti_dna FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1) SELECT patient_id, diagnosis, highest_anti_dna FROM best WHERE CASE WHEN (highest_anti_dna) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((highest_anti_dna) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END = (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN (highest_anti_dna) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((highest_anti_dna) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END) FROM best) ORDER BY patient_id NULLS FIRST

question: For our thrombosis study cohort, I'd like to know how often patients have a normal IgG status at their most recent check, broken down by care setting. Please give me, for patients admitted to the hospital and for patients followed at the outpatient clinic, the percentage of that setting's patients whose most recent IgG measurement was normal. The percentage should be out of every patient in that setting, so patients who never had an IgG measurement count toward the denominator but not the numerator. Please round to one decimal place, and label the two results exactly as 'admitted to the hospital' and 'followed at the outpatient clinic'.
evidence: An IgG measurement is considered normal when it is above 900 and below 2000.
SQL: WITH latest AS (SELECT id, igg, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY id ORDER BY date DESC NULLS LAST) AS rn FROM laboratory WHERE NOT igg IS NULL) SELECT CASE WHEN p.admission = '+' THEN 'admitted to the hospital' ELSE 'followed at the outpatient clinic' END AS care_setting, ROUND(CAST(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN l.igg > 900 AND l.igg < 2000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(p.id), 0) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS patient_share FROM patient AS p LEFT JOIN latest AS l ON l.id = p.id AND l.rn = 1 WHERE p.admission IN ('+', '-') GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 NULLS FIRST

question: In the thrombosis prediction cohort, I'd like to know whether the female predominance I saw for strongly positive anti-RNP results across follow-up also holds at patients' current status. Please give me a single integer: the number of female patients whose most recent visit shows a strongly positive anti-RNP result, minus the number of male patients whose most recent visit shows such a result. Use only the result at each patient's most recent visit, not earlier visits. A strongly positive anti-RNP result means a level of 32 or higher.
evidence: anti-ribonuclear protein (RNP): an autoantibody measured in the laboratory work-up; visit: a date on which the patient's laboratory tests were performed
SQL: WITH latest AS (SELECT id, MAX(date) AS maxdate FROM laboratory GROUP BY id) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.sex = 'F' AND CASE WHEN (l.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END >= 32 THEN p.id END) - COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.sex = 'M' AND CASE WHEN (l.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END >= 32 THEN p.id END) AS female_minus_male FROM patient AS p JOIN latest AS la ON p.id = la.id JOIN laboratory AS l ON l.id = la.id AND l.date = la.maxdate

question: In the thrombosis prediction cohort, I want to gauge how often the most recent anti-ribonuclear protein measurement among female patients was markedly elevated while CPK stayed low at that same measurement. Please give me a single integer: the number of female patients whose most recent anti-ribonuclear protein titer was above 64 and whose CPK from that same laboratory record was below 250. Above 64 means strictly greater than 64, and below 250 means strictly less than 250.
evidence: Anti-ribonuclear protein is an autoantibody measured as a titer in the blood; a negative result means the antibody was not detected.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS female_patients FROM patient AS p JOIN laboratory AS l ON l.id = p.id WHERE p.sex = 'F' AND NOT l.rnp IS NULL AND l.date = (SELECT MAX(l2.date) FROM laboratory AS l2 WHERE l2.id = p.id AND NOT l2.rnp IS NULL) AND CASE WHEN (l.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END > 64 AND l.cpk < 250

question: I'm preparing a capacity report for the lupus service. Among the patients whose profile lists a confirmed SLE diagnosis (not just suspected), I need: (1) how many were admitted to the hospital as inpatients, (2) how many were followed at the outpatient clinic, and (3) what percentage of the confirmed-SLE patients who were in one of these two care settings were inpatients. Please round the percentage to two decimals.
evidence: SLE means systemic lupus erythematosus. A disease name followed by 'susp' (e.g., 'SLE susp') means only suspected, not confirmed, and does not count.
SQL: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN admission = '+' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS inpatients, SUM(CASE WHEN admission = '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS outpatients, ROUND(CAST(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN admission = '+' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN admission IN ('+', '-') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS inpatient_pct FROM patient WHERE CAST(diagnosis AS TEXT) LIKE '%SLE%' AND CAST(diagnosis AS TEXT) NOT LIKE '%SLE susp%'

question: I'm putting together a renal-involvement review. Could you pull the demographics of patients who show both marked tissue damage and clinically significant proteinuria? Specifically, I need the patient ID, sex, and birthday of every patient who has at least one LDH result of 500 or higher and at least one urinary protein result of 100 mg/dL or more. A few details: an LDH of exactly 500 counts, and a urinary protein of exactly 100 mg/dL counts. The qualifying LDH and the qualifying urinary protein don't have to come from the same lab visit. Please give me one row per patient, ordered by patient ID, and nothing beyond those three fields.
evidence: Urinary protein is reported in mg/dL; a dipstick grade may carry the equivalent concentration in mg/dL in parentheses, e.g. '+2(100)' is 100 mg/dL. A result written as '>=' followed by a value means at least that many mg/dL, e.g. '>=300' is 300 mg/dL or more. 'TR' means a trace and '-' means none detected; any other marker is not a quantified mg/dL concentration. An LDH of 500 or higher is outside the normal range.
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT p.id, p.sex, p.birthday FROM patient AS p WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND l.ldh >= 500) AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS u WHERE u.id = p.id AND CASE WHEN CAST(u."U-PRO" AS TEXT) LIKE '%(%' THEN CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST(u."U-PRO" AS TEXT) FROM POSITION('(' IN u."U-PRO") + 1 FOR POSITION(')' IN u."U-PRO") - POSITION('(' IN u."U-PRO") - 1)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST(u."U-PRO" AS TEXT) FROM POSITION('(' IN u."U-PRO") + 1 FOR POSITION(')' IN u."U-PRO") - POSITION('(' IN u."U-PRO") - 1)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END WHEN CAST(u."U-PRO" AS TEXT) LIKE '>=%' THEN CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST(u."U-PRO" AS TEXT) FROM 3)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST(u."U-PRO" AS TEXT) FROM 3)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END ELSE CASE WHEN (u."U-PRO") IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((u."U-PRO") AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END END >= 100) ORDER BY p.id NULLS FIRST

question: Some registered patients have unknown thrombosis status because no examination has ever been recorded under their patient number. How many of these patients are women and how many are men? Please give me one row per sex with the sex of the patients and the number of such patients of that sex, and nothing else.
evidence: F is the code for female and M is the code for male in the patient profile.
SQL: SELECT p.sex AS sex, COUNT(*) AS patients FROM patient AS p WHERE p.sex IN ('F', 'M') AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM examination AS e WHERE e.id = p.id) GROUP BY p.sex ORDER BY p.sex NULLS FIRST

question: I need the number of female patients whose first visit to the hospital fell in 1998 (1 January 1998 through 31 December 1998) and who were admitted to the hospital. Only count patients whose sex is recorded as female; if there is no sex entry, don't count them.
evidence: An admission mark beginning with a plus sign means the patient was admitted to the hospital; a minus sign means the patient was followed at the outpatient clinic.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM patient WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST("First Date" AS TIMESTAMP)) = '1998' AND sex = 'F' AND CAST(admission AS TEXT) LIKE '+%'

question: I'm reviewing confirmed SLE cases for a study of neurologic involvement. Among patients whose examination lists SLE among the diagnosed diseases and who have a symptom recorded at such an examination, I need the case detail of the youngest such patient. Please send me the symptom recorded at that qualifying examination and that patient's overall diagnosis (their overall diagnosis, not the diagnosis written at the examination). If two patients share the same birth date, use the one with the smaller patient ID; and if that patient has more than one qualifying examination, use the most recent one.
evidence: SLE is systemic lupus erythematosus. A disease name followed by 'susp' means the disease was only suspected, not diagnosed.
SQL: WITH target AS (SELECT 'SLE' AS d) SELECT e.symptoms, p.diagnosis AS overall_diagnosis FROM patient AS p JOIN examination AS e ON e.id = p.id WHERE NOT p.birthday IS NULL AND NOT e.symptoms IS NULL AND TRIM(CAST(e.symptoms AS TEXT)) <> '' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM target WHERE REPLACE(',' || REPLACE(e.diagnosis, ' ', '') || ',', ',' || d || ',', '') <> ',' || REPLACE(e.diagnosis, ' ', '') || ',') ORDER BY p.birthday DESC NULLS LAST, p.id NULLS FIRST, e."Examination Date" DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1

question: I'm auditing inpatient intake during the February 1998 admission wave. Among patients first seen at the hospital in the second half of February 1998 (visit date from 15 to 28 February 1998), find the oldest inpatient at first presentation and give me that patient's diagnosis only. If two patients tie in age, use the one with the smaller patient ID.
evidence: 'Inpatient' means the patient was admitted to the hospital rather than followed at the outpatient clinic, regardless of whether the record notes extra detail about the admission.
SQL: SELECT p.diagnosis FROM patient AS p WHERE p."First Date" >= '1998-02-15' AND p."First Date" <= '1998-02-28' AND CAST(p.admission AS TEXT) LIKE '+%' ORDER BY p.birthday ASC NULLS FIRST, p.id ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1

question: I'm summarizing anti-cardiolipin IgM levels for lupus patients. What was the average anti-cardiolipin IgM concentration across examinations performed between 1993-10-01 and 1993-10-31 (both days inclusive) in which systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) was diagnosed? Please round the average to 1 decimal place.
evidence: SLE = systemic lupus erythematosus
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(e."aCL IgM") AS DECIMAL), 1) AS avg_acl_igm FROM examination AS e WHERE e."Examination Date" BETWEEN '1993-10-01' AND '1993-10-31' AND POSITION(',' || 'SLE' || ',' IN ',' || REPLACE(e.diagnosis, ' ', '') || ',') > 0

question: How many patients in the thrombosis prediction cohort have a diagnosis of psoriatic arthritis? The count should cover every patient ever recorded in the registry, with no restriction to a time period or follow-up status. I just need that single number.
evidence: Psoriatic arthritis: a chronic inflammatory joint and skin disease belonging to the rheumatic diagnoses.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM patient WHERE UPPER(REPLACE(diagnosis, ' ', '')) = UPPER(REPLACE('Psoriatic arthritis', ' ', ''))

question: I need to size a comparison group for my study of liver-enzyme abnormalities. How many patients in the registry have never had an ALT result above the normal range? Please give me the count broken down by sex: the number of male patients and the number of female patients. Every patient in the registry counts, including patients with no laboratory results at all, since they have never had an abnormal result. The report should cover exactly the two sexes, male and female.
evidence: ALT is measured by the GPT laboratory value; a GPT result of 60 or higher exceeds the normal range.
SQL: SELECT p.sex AS sex, COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM patient AS p WHERE p.sex IN ('M', 'F') AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND l.gpt >= 60) GROUP BY p.sex ORDER BY p.sex NULLS FIRST

question: For patients with at least one red-blood-cell result below 3.5 (RBC), I need a breakdown by care setting: how many patients were admitted to the hospital (+) versus followed at the outpatient clinic (-), and the average completed age of each group on 2026-10-09, rounded to one decimal place. Age means completed years on 2026-10-09.
evidence: Red-blood-cell result below 3.5 (RBC); admission status + marks a patient admitted to the hospital, - marks a patient followed at the outpatient clinic.
SQL: SELECT p.admission AS care_setting, COUNT(*) AS patient_count, ROUND(CAST(AVG(CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST('2026-10-09' AS TIMESTAMP))) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST('2026-10-09' AS TIMESTAMP))) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END - CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(p.birthday AS TIMESTAMP))) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(p.birthday AS TIMESTAMP))) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END - CASE WHEN TO_CHAR(CAST('2026-10-09' AS TIMESTAMP), 'MM-DD') < TO_CHAR(CAST(p.birthday AS TIMESTAMP), 'MM-DD') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS average_age FROM patient AS p WHERE p.admission IN ('+', '-') AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND l.rbc < 3.5) GROUP BY p.admission ORDER BY p.admission COLLATE "C" NULLS FIRST

question: Among the patients who have laboratory test records on file, how many are female and how many are male? Please give me one line for the female patients and one line for the male patients, each showing the sex and the number of patients of that sex.
SQL: SELECT p.sex AS sex, COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS patient_count FROM patient AS p JOIN laboratory AS l ON l.id = p.id WHERE p.sex IN ('F', 'M') GROUP BY p.sex

question: I'm studying antiphospholipid antibodies in Sjögren's syndrome (SJS). Could you tell me the average anti-cardiolipin IgM concentration among SJS patients, rounded to two decimal places? To clarify: use only patients with an established SJS diagnosis recorded at the patient level (a diagnosis marked 'susp', such as 'SJS susp', is only a suspicion and those patients should not be included). Include every examination recorded for these patients regardless of date. A recorded anti-cardiolipin IgM value of 0 means the antibody was not detected at that examination, so treat it as no measurement and leave it out of the average - count only examinations where a concentration was detected.
evidence: SJS is the abbreviation used for Sjögren's syndrome; a diagnosis marked 'susp' (e.g. 'SJS susp') is only a suspicion of the disease, not an established diagnosis.
SQL: WITH RECURSIVE tokens AS (SELECT id, '' AS tok, COALESCE(diagnosis, '') || ',' AS rest FROM patient UNION ALL SELECT id, TRIM(CAST(SUBSTRING(CAST(rest AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION(',' IN rest) - 1) AS TEXT)), SUBSTRING(CAST(rest AS TEXT) FROM POSITION(',' IN rest) + 1) FROM tokens WHERE rest <> '') SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(CASE WHEN e."aCL IgM" > 0 THEN e."aCL IgM" END) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_acl_igm FROM examination AS e WHERE e.id IN (SELECT id FROM tokens WHERE tok = 'SJS')

question: How many female patients have a Sjögren's syndrome diagnosis recorded in a medical examination? Please count across the full examination history with no date restriction, and note that suspected cases don't count—only an actual SjS diagnosis should be included. I just need that single number.
evidence: SjS is the standard medical abbreviation for Sjögren's syndrome, and the diagnosis is recorded under that abbreviation.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t1.id) AS n_female_sjs_patients FROM patient AS t1 JOIN examination AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.id WHERE t1.sex = 'F' AND CAST((',' || REPLACE(t2.diagnosis, ' ', '') || ',') AS TEXT) LIKE ('%' || ',' || 'SjS' || ',' || '%')

question: How many patients who were never admitted to the hospital (outpatient follow-up only) had at least one normal anti-ribonuclear protein (RNP) result? A normal RNP result means the test found no anti-ribonuclear protein antibody: a negative result, or a measured value of zero. I just need a single number.
evidence: anti-ribonuclear protein (RNP): an antibody test
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS patient_count FROM patient AS p JOIN laboratory AS l ON p.id = l.id WHERE p.admission = '-' AND l.rnp IN ('negative', '0')

question: I'd like to know, among patients who have at least one normal anti-SM laboratory result (recorded as 'negative' or '0') and whose examinations show no thrombosis, how many have ever had significant proteinuria on any laboratory record. Significant proteinuria means 30 mg/dl or more; '-' and 'TR' count as no proteinuria. I only need the number of such patients.
evidence: anti-SM: normal is recorded as 'negative' or '0'; proteinuria is measured semi-quantitatively as '-', 'TR', or the approximate daily urinary protein excretion in mg/dl
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM patient AS p WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND l.sm IN ('negative', '0')) AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM examination AS e WHERE e.id = p.id AND e.thrombosis = 0) AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM examination AS e WHERE e.id = p.id AND e.thrombosis <> 0) AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND CASE WHEN (l."U-PRO") IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l."U-PRO") AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END >= 30)

question: Which patients followed at the outpatient clinic have both an abnormal red blood cell count and a positive anti-ribonuclear protein antibody result? Please return the patient IDs. Note: the two findings don't need to be from the same laboratory visit - a patient qualifies if at least one lab test shows an abnormal RBC and at least one, possibly different, lab test shows a positive anti-ribonuclear protein antibody. Here, a positive anti-ribonuclear protein antibody means a titer above zero, an abnormal RBC means RBC <= 3.5 or RBC >= 6.0, and outpatient follow-up means Admission = '-'.
SQL: SELECT t1.id FROM patient AS t1 WHERE t1.admission = '-' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l1 WHERE l1.id = t1.id AND (l1.rbc <= 3.5 OR l1.rbc >= 6)) AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l2 WHERE l2.id = t1.id AND CASE WHEN (l2.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l2.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END > 0) ORDER BY t1.id NULLS FIRST

question: In our autoimmune-cohort registry, I'm profiling young patients with strongly positive anti-RNP findings. What is the average age, in years, of the patients who were younger than 70 as of 2026-10-09 and who have at least one anti-RNP result of 64 or higher? Please give the average as a single number to one decimal place.
evidence: anti-ribonuclear protein (anti-RNP) result: the reading recorded for a patient's anti-RNP test in the laboratory record
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST('2026-10-09' AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST('2026-10-09' AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END - CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST(p.birthday AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST(p.birthday AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END - CASE WHEN SUBSTRING(CAST('2026-10-09' AS TEXT) FROM 6) < SUBSTRING(CAST(p.birthday AS TEXT) FROM 6) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS average_age FROM patient AS p WHERE (CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST('2026-10-09' AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST('2026-10-09' AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END - CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST(p.birthday AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST(p.birthday AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END - CASE WHEN SUBSTRING(CAST('2026-10-09' AS TEXT) FROM 6) < SUBSTRING(CAST(p.birthday AS TEXT) FROM 6) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) < 70 AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND CASE WHEN (l.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END >= 64)

question: I'd like a single number: how many female patients in the thrombosis prediction data have a laboratory record showing a normal white blood cell count, an abnormal fibrinogen level, and an anti-ribonuclear protein (RNP) reading above 15, considering all recorded laboratory dates?
evidence: A normal white blood cell count means strictly between 3.5 and 9.0; an abnormal fibrinogen level means at most 150 or at least 450.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) FROM patient AS p JOIN laboratory AS l ON l.id = p.id WHERE p.sex = 'F' AND l.wbc > 3.5 AND l.wbc < 9.0 AND (l.fg <= 150 OR l.fg >= 450) AND CASE WHEN (l.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END > 15

question: As part of our clinical audit I'm profiling patients born between 1936 and 1956 inclusive who never had a creatinine phosphokinase (CPK) result above the normal range. A CPK of 250 or higher counts as above the normal range, and patients with no CPK results on record count as never having exceeded it. For that group, please give me the women's percentage of the group's men and women, rounded to one decimal place.
evidence: Creatinine phosphokinase (CPK) of 250 or higher is above the normal range.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(CASE WHEN (SUM(CASE WHEN sex = 'F' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(CASE WHEN sex = 'F' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END * 100 / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN sex IN ('M', 'F') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS percentage FROM patient WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(birthday AS TIMESTAMP)) BETWEEN '1936' AND '1956' AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory WHERE laboratory.id = patient.id AND laboratory.cpk >= 250)

question: I'm preparing a case series on early renal involvement and need to size my cohort. How many patients were under age 50 on the day of a laboratory test performed between 1 January 1981 and 31 December 1986 inclusive, had a platelet count from 100 through 400 at that test, and showed proteinuria at that test? Age means completed years on the day of the test, so under 50 is strictly below 50. The platelet range is inclusive. I just need the number of patients satisfying all conditions.
evidence: A patient showed proteinuria at a test when that test's dipstick reading reports protein: a dash or zero means no protein was found, a number is the amount of protein found, TR stands for trace protein, and a reading written in percent signs is the dipstick saturated, the strongest reading.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS patient_count FROM patient AS p JOIN laboratory AS l ON l.id = p.id WHERE SUBSTRING(CAST(l.date AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) BETWEEN '1981' AND '1986' AND l.plt BETWEEN 100 AND 400 AND NOT p.birthday IS NULL AND (CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST(l.date AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST(l.date AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END - CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST(p.birthday AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST(p.birthday AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END - CASE WHEN SUBSTRING(CAST(l.date AS TEXT) FROM 6 FOR 5) < SUBSTRING(CAST(p.birthday AS TEXT) FROM 6 FOR 5) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) < 50 AND NOT l."U-PRO" IS NULL AND NOT l."U-PRO" IN ('-', '0')

question: Among molecules containing at least one single bond, what is the average number of oxygen atoms per molecule? Include molecules with no oxygen and round to four decimal places.
evidence: The '-' bond-type symbol denotes a single bond.
SQL: WITH molecules AS (SELECT DISTINCT molecule_id FROM bond WHERE bond_type = '-'), oxygen AS (SELECT molecule_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM atom WHERE element = 'o' GROUP BY molecule_id) SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(COALESCE(oxygen.n, 0)) AS DECIMAL), 4) FROM molecules LEFT JOIN oxygen ON oxygen.molecule_id = molecules.molecule_id

question: Among carcinogenic molecules with at least one single bond, what is the average number of single bonds per molecule?
evidence: In this dataset, '+' denotes a carcinogenic molecule and '-' denotes a single bond.
SQL: SELECT AVG(single_bond_count) FROM (SELECT b.molecule_id, COUNT(*) AS single_bond_count FROM bond AS b JOIN molecule AS m ON m.molecule_id = b.molecule_id WHERE m.label = '+' AND b.bond_type = '-' GROUP BY b.molecule_id) AS per_molecule

question: Which elements have the fewest atom occurrences across non-carcinogenic molecules? Include all elements tied for the minimum.
evidence: A '-' carcinogenicity label means non-carcinogenic.
SQL: WITH counts AS (SELECT a.element, COUNT(*) AS n FROM atom AS a JOIN molecule AS m ON m.molecule_id = a.molecule_id WHERE m.label = '-' GROUP BY a.element) SELECT element FROM counts WHERE n = (SELECT MIN(n) FROM counts) ORDER BY element NULLS FIRST

question: How many distinct iodine atoms and distinct sulfur atoms, respectively, participate in at least one single bond?
evidence: The '-' bond-type symbol denotes a single bond.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t1.element = 'i' THEN t1.atom_id ELSE NULL END) AS iodine_nums, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t1.element = 's' THEN t1.atom_id ELSE NULL END) AS sulfur_nums FROM atom AS t1 INNER JOIN connected AS t2 ON t1.atom_id = t2.atom_id INNER JOIN bond AS t3 ON t2.bond_id = t3.bond_id WHERE t3.bond_type = '-'

question: Among carcinogenic molecules, what percentage contain no fluorine atoms? Round to two decimal places.
evidence: A '+' carcinogenicity label means carcinogenic.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM atom AS a WHERE a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id AND a.element = 'f') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) FROM molecule AS m WHERE m.label = '+'

question: What is the most common bond type in molecule TR010, and is that molecule carcinogenic? Return the bond type and YES or NO.
evidence: In this dataset, a molecule labeled '+' is carcinogenic; a molecule labeled '-' is not.
SQL: SELECT b.bond_type, CASE WHEN m.label = '+' THEN 'YES' ELSE 'NO' END FROM bond AS b JOIN molecule AS m ON m.molecule_id = b.molecule_id WHERE b.molecule_id = 'TR010' GROUP BY b.bond_type, m.label ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC NULLS LAST, b.bond_type NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1

question: What are the bonds that have phosphorus and nitrogen as their atom elements?
SQL: SELECT t2.bond_id FROM atom AS t1 INNER JOIN connected AS t2 ON t1.atom_id = t2.atom_id WHERE t2.bond_id IN (SELECT t3.bond_id FROM connected AS t3 INNER JOIN atom AS t4 ON t3.atom_id = t4.atom_id WHERE t4.element = 'p') AND t1.element = 'n'

question: List the distinct elements of atoms that do not participate in any bond.
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT a.element FROM atom AS a WHERE NOT a.atom_id IN (SELECT atom_id FROM connected UNION SELECT atom_id2 FROM connected) ORDER BY a.element NULLS FIRST

question: How many atoms occur in molecules that have at least one triple bond and at least one phosphorus or bromine atom?
evidence: The '#' bond-type symbol denotes a triple bond.
SQL: WITH triple AS (SELECT DISTINCT molecule_id FROM bond WHERE bond_type = '#'), hetero AS (SELECT DISTINCT molecule_id FROM atom WHERE element IN ('p', 'br')), qualified AS (SELECT t.molecule_id FROM triple AS t JOIN hetero AS h ON h.molecule_id = t.molecule_id) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM atom AS a JOIN qualified AS q ON q.molecule_id = a.molecule_id

question: Among all atoms in molecules containing at least one single bond, what percentage are chlorine atoms? Round to four decimal places.
evidence: The '-' bond-type symbol denotes a single bond.
SQL: WITH molecules AS (SELECT DISTINCT molecule_id FROM bond WHERE bond_type = '-') SELECT ROUND(CAST(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN a.element = 'cl' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 0) AS DECIMAL), 4) FROM molecules AS m JOIN atom AS a ON a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id

question: What fraction of all atoms in molecule TR006 are hydrogen? Give the fraction and the molecule's recorded carcinogenicity label.
SQL: WITH subquery AS (SELECT DISTINCT t1.atom_id, t1.element, t1.molecule_id, t2.label FROM atom AS t1 INNER JOIN molecule AS t2 ON t1.molecule_id = t2.molecule_id WHERE t2.molecule_id = 'TR006') SELECT CASE WHEN (COUNT(CASE WHEN element = 'h' THEN atom_id ELSE NULL END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((COUNT(CASE WHEN element = 'h' THEN atom_id ELSE NULL END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END / NULLIF((CASE WHEN COUNT(atom_id) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE COUNT(atom_id) END), 0) AS ratio, label FROM subquery GROUP BY label

question: I want to know whether molecular saturation is associated with carcinogenicity in our compound library. Please report, for molecules in which every bond is a single bond: the number of carcinogenic molecules minus the number of non-carcinogenic molecules. And for all other molecules: the same difference (carcinogenic count minus non-carcinogenic count). Rules: label '+' means the molecule is carcinogenic; label '-' means non-carcinogenic; bond type '-' denotes a single bond; each molecule belongs to exactly one of the two groups.
evidence: In the labels, '+' indicates a carcinogenic molecule and '-' indicates a non-carcinogenic molecule; for bond types, '-' indicates a single bond.
SQL: SELECT (SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN m.label = '+' THEN 1 ELSE -1 END) FROM molecule AS m WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM bond AS b WHERE b.molecule_id = m.molecule_id AND b.bond_type <> '-')) AS diff_molecules_with_only_single_bonds, (SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN m.label = '+' THEN 1 ELSE -1 END) FROM molecule AS m WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM bond AS b WHERE b.molecule_id = m.molecule_id AND b.bond_type <> '-')) AS diff_other_molecules

question: In our toxicology library, how many carbon-carbon pairs joined by a double bond are there in total across the carcinogenic compounds? I want a single number for the whole library.
evidence: A compound is carcinogenic when its label is '+' and non-carcinogenic when its label is '-'. In the bond notation, '-' is a single bond, '=' is a double bond, and '#' is a triple bond.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS num_pairs FROM connected AS c JOIN bond AS b ON b.bond_id = c.bond_id JOIN molecule AS m ON m.molecule_id = b.molecule_id JOIN atom AS a1 ON a1.atom_id = c.atom_id JOIN atom AS a2 ON a2.atom_id = c.atom_id2 WHERE m.label = '+' AND b.bond_type = '=' AND a1.element = 'c' AND a2.element = 'c' AND c.atom_id < c.atom_id2

question: Among the molecules labeled '+' (carcinogenic), which chemical element is the most common among the atoms that take part in at least one bond? Also give the percentage of all atoms in those '+' molecules that this element accounts for, rounded to two decimal places. Count the percentage over every atom of the '+' molecules, whether or not it takes part in a bond. If several elements tie for most common, report each of them.
SQL: WITH plus_atoms AS (SELECT a.atom_id, a.element FROM atom AS a JOIN molecule AS m ON m.molecule_id = a.molecule_id WHERE m.label = '+'), bonded AS (SELECT atom_id, element FROM plus_atoms WHERE atom_id IN (SELECT atom_id FROM connected) OR atom_id IN (SELECT atom_id2 FROM connected)), bonded_counts AS (SELECT element, COUNT(*) AS n FROM bonded GROUP BY element), top AS (SELECT MAX(n) AS mx FROM bonded_counts), all_counts AS (SELECT element, COUNT(*) AS na FROM plus_atoms GROUP BY element), total AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS tot FROM plus_atoms) SELECT bc.element, ROUND(CAST(100.0 * ac.na / NULLIF(t.tot, 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS pct FROM bonded_counts AS bc JOIN top ON bc.n = top.mx JOIN all_counts AS ac ON ac.element = bc.element CROSS JOIN total AS t ORDER BY bc.element NULLS FIRST

question: For the molecule containing atom TR041_10, I'd like to know the molecule id, whether it's carcinogenic (YES or NO), and the number of multiple bonds in that molecule. Please use the rule that a molecule labeled '+' is carcinogenic (YES) and one labeled '-' is not (NO).
SQL: SELECT t2.molecule_id, CASE WHEN t2.label = '+' THEN 'YES' ELSE 'NO' END AS flag_carcinogenic, COUNT(t3.bond_id) AS multiple_bonds FROM atom AS t1 INNER JOIN molecule AS t2 ON t1.molecule_id = t2.molecule_id INNER JOIN bond AS t3 ON t3.molecule_id = t2.molecule_id WHERE t1.atom_id = 'TR041_10' AND t3.bond_type <> '-' GROUP BY t2.molecule_id, t2.label

question: For the carcinogenic molecules in the toxicology database, how many carbon-carbon bonds are there of each bond type (single, double, and triple)? Please give me the bond type and the corresponding count.
evidence: A molecule labelled '+' is carcinogenic. Bond types are recorded as follows: a single bond as '-', a double bond as '=', and a triple bond as '#'. A carbon-carbon bond is a bond whose two bonded atoms are both carbon.
SQL: SELECT b.bond_type, COUNT(DISTINCT c.bond_id) AS bond_count FROM connected AS c JOIN atom AS a1 ON a1.atom_id = c.atom_id JOIN atom AS a2 ON a2.atom_id = c.atom_id2 JOIN bond AS b ON b.bond_id = c.bond_id JOIN molecule AS m ON m.molecule_id = b.molecule_id WHERE a1.element = 'c' AND a2.element = 'c' AND m.label = '+' GROUP BY b.bond_type ORDER BY b.bond_type NULLS FIRST

question: I want to know how widely chlorine atoms bond to other atoms across the toxicology database. Please give me a single number: the count of atoms that bond with chlorine atoms. Nothing else.
evidence: Chlorine means the element recorded under the code cl.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a1.element = 'cl' THEN c.atom_id2 ELSE c.atom_id END) AS bonded_atoms FROM connected AS c JOIN atom AS a1 ON c.atom_id = a1.atom_id JOIN atom AS a2 ON c.atom_id2 = a2.atom_id WHERE a1.element = 'cl' OR a2.element = 'cl'

question: I'm studying the immediate chemical environment of sulfur atoms in carcinogenic molecules. Please tell me, as a single number, how many atoms are directly bonded to a sulfur atom in carcinogenic molecules. A molecule labeled '+' is carcinogenic; a molecule labeled '-' is not.
evidence: Sulfur refers to the element 's'. A direct bond is a bond between two atoms.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t2.atom_id2) AS atom_count FROM atom AS t1 INNER JOIN connected AS t2 ON t1.atom_id = t2.atom_id INNER JOIN molecule AS m ON t1.molecule_id = m.molecule_id WHERE t1.element = 's' AND m.label = '+'

question: I'm compiling bond records of unusual carcinogenic molecules for a structural alert review. Please find the bonds that belong to carcinogenic molecules (labelled '+') that contain an element recorded for no other molecule in the dataset. Note that this search covers the whole dataset, so an element counts as belonging to no other molecule when no molecule other than the one at hand records it. For each such bond, return only the bond id and molecule id.
evidence: A '+' label means carcinogenic.
SQL: SELECT t1.bond_id, t1.molecule_id FROM bond AS t1 INNER JOIN molecule AS t2 ON t1.molecule_id = t2.molecule_id WHERE t2.label = '+' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM atom AS a WHERE a.molecule_id = t1.molecule_id AND a.element IN (SELECT element FROM atom GROUP BY element HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT molecule_id) = 1))

question: I'm building a control group of nitrogen-containing structures for a carcinogenicity review. How many molecules in the database contain at least one nitrogen atom, where none of those nitrogen atoms takes part in a double bond or a triple bond? A nitrogen held only by single bonds is fine; any nitrogen in a double or triple bond disqualifies the molecule. Molecules with no nitrogen at all don't count. I just need the single number of such molecules.
evidence: Nitrogen refers to the element code 'n'; '=' denotes a double bond; '#' denotes a triple bond; '-' denotes a single bond.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS number_of_molecules FROM molecule AS m WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM atom AS a WHERE a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id AND a.element = 'n') AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM atom AS a2 INNER JOIN connected AS c ON c.atom_id = a2.atom_id OR c.atom_id2 = a2.atom_id INNER JOIN bond AS b ON b.bond_id = c.bond_id WHERE a2.molecule_id = m.molecule_id AND a2.element = 'n' AND b.bond_type <> '-')

question: In the toxicology database, how many atoms are bonded to chlorine atoms, taken across all molecules? I want a single number. By chlorine I mean the element 'cl'.
evidence: cl: chlorine
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t1.atom_id) AS bonded_atom_count FROM connected AS t1 INNER JOIN atom AS t2 ON t1.atom_id2 = t2.atom_id WHERE t2.element = 'cl'

question: For a report on structural features of carcinogenic compounds, I'm looking at compounds that form a triple bond. Among those, what percent are labeled carcinogenic and what percent are labeled non-carcinogenic, each rounded to two decimal places? The two percents should sum to 100, apart from rounding.
evidence: Label '+' means carcinogenic; label '-' means non-carcinogenic.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(CASE WHEN (COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN m.label = '+' THEN b.molecule_id END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN m.label = '+' THEN b.molecule_id END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT b.molecule_id), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS pct_carcinogenic, ROUND(CAST(CASE WHEN (COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN m.label = '-' THEN b.molecule_id END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN m.label = '-' THEN b.molecule_id END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT b.molecule_id), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS pct_non_carcinogenic FROM bond AS b JOIN molecule AS m ON b.molecule_id = m.molecule_id WHERE b.bond_type = '#'

question: I'm characterizing how strongly rare chemical elements are integrated into the molecular skeleton of carcinogenic compounds. For every carcinogenic molecule that contains at least one atom of an element that appears in no other molecule in the database, I want the number of bonds its atoms of that element take part in. Please judge an element's rarity over every molecule in the database, carcinogenic or not. Return the molecule_id and that bond count for each qualifying molecule, one row per molecule, sorted by molecule_id.
evidence: '+' is the label of a carcinogenic molecule, '-' of a non-carcinogenic one; a bond is a link between two atoms of a molecule.
SQL: WITH rare AS (SELECT element FROM atom GROUP BY element HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT molecule_id) = 1) SELECT m.molecule_id, COUNT(DISTINCT c.bond_id) AS bond_count FROM molecule AS m INNER JOIN atom AS a ON a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id LEFT JOIN connected AS c ON (c.atom_id = a.atom_id OR c.atom_id2 = a.atom_id) WHERE m.label = '+' AND a.element IN (SELECT element FROM rare) GROUP BY m.molecule_id ORDER BY m.molecule_id NULLS FIRST

question: I'd like a ranked inventory of every molecule in the toxicology database that contains at least one carbon atom. For each qualifying molecule, give me its molecule id, carcinogenicity label, number of atoms, number of bonds, number of carbon atoms, number of chlorine atoms, number of carbon-touching bonds, and number of multiple bonds - one row per molecule, including molecules where some of these counts are zero. Rank the rows from the most carbon-touching bonds to the fewest; break ties by larger total atom count, then by molecule id ascending. Give consecutive rank positions 1, 2, 3, ... with no gaps after ties.
evidence: A carbon-touching bond is a bond with a carbon atom at one of its ends; a bond between two carbon atoms counts as one bond. A multiple bond is a double or triple bond. The carcinogenicity label '+' means carcinogenic, '-' means not carcinogenic.
SQL: WITH carbonbonds AS (SELECT a.molecule_id, COUNT(DISTINCT c.bond_id) AS carbon_bond_count FROM connected AS c JOIN atom AS a ON c.atom_id = a.atom_id WHERE a.element = 'c' GROUP BY a.molecule_id), moleculestats AS (SELECT m.molecule_id, m.label, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM atom AS a WHERE a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id) AS atom_count, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM bond AS b WHERE b.molecule_id = m.molecule_id) AS bond_count, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM atom AS a WHERE a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id AND a.element = 'c') AS carbon_count, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM atom AS a WHERE a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id AND a.element = 'cl') AS chlorine_count, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM bond AS b WHERE b.molecule_id = m.molecule_id AND b.bond_type <> '-') AS multiple_bond_count FROM molecule AS m WHERE m.molecule_id IN (SELECT molecule_id FROM atom WHERE element = 'c')), ranked AS (SELECT ms.molecule_id, ms.label, ms.atom_count, ms.bond_count, ms.carbon_count, ms.chlorine_count, COALESCE(cb.carbon_bond_count, 0) AS carbon_touching_bonds, ms.multiple_bond_count, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(cb.carbon_bond_count, 0) DESC NULLS LAST, ms.atom_count DESC NULLS LAST, ms.molecule_id NULLS FIRST) AS position FROM moleculestats AS ms LEFT JOIN carbonbonds AS cb ON cb.molecule_id = ms.molecule_id) SELECT position, molecule_id, label, atom_count, bond_count, carbon_count, chlorine_count, carbon_touching_bonds, multiple_bond_count FROM ranked ORDER BY position NULLS FIRST

question: I'm studying the hydrogen bonding pattern of the molecule that contains the yttrium atom. How many bonds in that molecule have a hydrogen atom at one end? Just give me the single overall count, please.
evidence: An yttrium atom has element symbol Y; a hydrogen atom has element symbol H.
SQL: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.bond_id) AS bond_count FROM connected AS c JOIN atom AS a ON a.atom_id = c.atom_id OR a.atom_id = c.atom_id2 WHERE a.element = 'h' AND a.molecule_id = (SELECT molecule_id FROM atom WHERE element = 'y')

question: As part of a connectivity review, I'd like to know how heavily atoms are connected in molecule TR397: what is the average number of bonds an atom of TR397 has? Please give me just that one number, rounded to two decimal places.
SQL: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(cnt) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_bonds_per_atom FROM (SELECT a.atom_id, COUNT(DISTINCT c.bond_id) AS cnt FROM atom AS a LEFT JOIN connected AS c ON (c.atom_id = a.atom_id OR c.atom_id2 = a.atom_id) WHERE a.molecule_id = 'TR397' GROUP BY a.atom_id) AS __photo_derived_1

question: I'm studying bond patterns in compounds that are not carcinogenic. For each element, how many double or triple bonds join a carbon atom to an atom of that element, across all non-carcinogenic molecules? Give me one row per element with the element and its count of such bonds—nothing else.
evidence: A molecule labeled '-' is not carcinogenic; a molecule labeled '+' is carcinogenic.
SQL: SELECT a2.element AS element, COUNT(DISTINCT c.bond_id) AS bond_count FROM connected AS c JOIN bond AS b ON c.bond_id = b.bond_id JOIN atom AS a1 ON c.atom_id = a1.atom_id JOIN atom AS a2 ON c.atom_id2 = a2.atom_id JOIN molecule AS m ON b.molecule_id = m.molecule_id WHERE m.label = '-' AND a1.element = 'c' AND b.bond_type <> '-' GROUP BY a2.element ORDER BY a2.element NULLS FIRST

question: For molecule TR377, I'd like a profile of its bond composition, covering single and double bonds only. For each bond kind, please give me: the bond kind symbol, the number of bonds of that kind in the molecule, and the number of element pairs that bond kind joins. Also include the molecule's carcinogenicity label. List the bond kinds from most frequent to least; if two kinds are equally frequent, list them alphabetically by symbol.
evidence: A single bond is shown as the symbol '-' and a double bond as '='; a molecule label '+' means carcinogenic and '-' means not carcinogenic.
SQL: WITH scoped AS (SELECT bond_type, COUNT(*) AS bond_count FROM bond WHERE molecule_id = 'TR377' AND bond_type IN ('-', '=') GROUP BY bond_type), pairs AS (SELECT b.bond_type, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a1.element < a2.element THEN a1.element || '-' || a2.element ELSE a2.element || '-' || a1.element END) AS pair_count FROM bond AS b JOIN connected AS c ON c.bond_id = b.bond_id JOIN atom AS a1 ON a1.atom_id = c.atom_id JOIN atom AS a2 ON a2.atom_id = c.atom_id2 WHERE b.molecule_id = 'TR377' AND b.bond_type IN ('-', '=') GROUP BY b.bond_type) SELECT s.bond_type, s.bond_count, p.pair_count, m.label AS molecule_label FROM scoped AS s JOIN pairs AS p ON p.bond_type = s.bond_type JOIN molecule AS m ON m.molecule_id = 'TR377' ORDER BY s.bond_count DESC NULLS LAST, s.bond_type NULLS FIRST

question: I'm screening for molecules to flag for follow-up. Can you give me the molecule_id of the first three molecules, in alphabetical order, that are non-carcinogenic, contain at least one metal atom, and have single bonds between their atoms? Please return only the molecule ids.
evidence: A molecule label of '-' means the molecule is non-carcinogenic. A bond type of '-' means a single bond between two atoms. The metals are sodium (na), potassium (k), calcium (ca), copper (cu), zinc (zn), tin (sn), lead (pb), magnesium (mg) and lithium (li).
SQL: SELECT DISTINCT t1.molecule_id FROM molecule AS t1 INNER JOIN bond AS t2 ON t1.molecule_id = t2.molecule_id INNER JOIN atom AS t3 ON t1.molecule_id = t3.molecule_id WHERE t2.bond_type = '-' AND t1.label = '-' AND t3.element IN ('na', 'k', 'ca', 'cu', 'zn', 'sn', 'pb', 'mg', 'li') ORDER BY t1.molecule_id NULLS FIRST LIMIT 3

question: I'm profiling the compound library and want to size the fully saturated portion of each element's atom population - atoms attached only by single bonds behave differently from unsaturated sites. For each element symbol in the database, how many atoms are connected only by single bonds and never part of any multiple bond? Please give me one row per element symbol with the element symbol and the number of such atoms, sorted alphabetically by element symbol. This should cover all compounds in the database. Note that an atom with no bonds at all doesn't count as being connected by single bonds, so exclude those.
evidence: A single bond is a bond between two atoms sharing exactly one electron pair, denoted by the bond-type symbol '-'. A multiple bond is a double or triple bond, i.e. a bond between two atoms sharing more than one electron pair.
SQL: WITH per_atom AS (SELECT a.atom_id AS atom_id, a.element AS element, CASE WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM connected AS c WHERE c.atom_id = a.atom_id) AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM connected AS c JOIN bond AS b ON b.bond_id = c.bond_id WHERE c.atom_id = a.atom_id AND b.bond_type <> '-') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS saturated FROM atom AS a) SELECT element, SUM(saturated) AS atoms FROM per_atom GROUP BY element ORDER BY element NULLS FIRST

question: In the toxicology compound database, which elements take part in a triple bond, and how widely are they distributed across the tested compounds? For each such element, give me its element symbol and the number of molecules that contain that element. Order the results from the most widespread element to the least; where two elements have equal counts, list them alphabetically by element symbol.
evidence: The '#' bond-type symbol denotes a triple bond.
SQL: SELECT a.element AS element, COUNT(DISTINCT a.molecule_id) AS n_molecules FROM atom AS a WHERE a.element IN (SELECT at.element FROM bond AS b JOIN connected AS c ON b.bond_id = c.bond_id JOIN atom AS at ON c.atom_id = at.atom_id WHERE b.bond_type = '#') GROUP BY a.element ORDER BY n_molecules DESC NULLS LAST, a.element NULLS FIRST

question: For molecule TR397, I want to see which elements form the bonding skeleton. For each element present among its atoms, how many atoms of that element take part in at least one bond? Please report two things per row: the element symbol (e.g. c, h, o) and the number of that element's atoms in TR397 that take part in a bond. One row per element, ordered alphabetically by element symbol. Only atoms belonging to TR397 should count.
evidence: Takes part in a bond: the atom is one of the two atoms a bond joins.
SQL: SELECT a.element, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN NOT c.bond_id IS NULL THEN a.atom_id END) AS bonded_atoms FROM atom AS a LEFT JOIN connected AS c ON (c.atom_id = a.atom_id OR c.atom_id2 = a.atom_id) WHERE a.molecule_id = 'TR397' GROUP BY a.element ORDER BY a.element NULLS FIRST
